docs.d: Short answers about what you need, Cora Max, using Cora away from home, equipment, alerts, Reef Buddy, languages, plans and your data.
x: Short answers, with links to the full pages. If something isn't working, go straight to Troubleshooting . If you want steps for a task, try How do I...? .
Do I need a Cora Max, or is my phone enough?

You don't need to buy anything to start. Cora Mobile on its own tracks your tanks, logs tests, sends alerts and runs Cora Assistant. A Cora Max at the tank adds a few things. Without one, your phone reads a Neptune Apex, Red Sea or Jecod device only while Cora Mobile is open on the same Wi-Fi. A Cora Max reads them around the clock, keeps your readings current while you're away, and passes on commands you send from away. More in Equipment by brand .
How do I add my first tank?
After you sign up, Cora Mobile asks three questions: a name, the type of tank and how much water. Only the name is required. More in Setting up Cora Mobile .
Can I try Cora before I sign up?
Yes. On the sign-in screen, tap Explore a demo reef . It's a sample tank, and you don't need an account. More in Setting up Cora Mobile .
My tank is still cycling. Can Cora help?

Yes. Tap Starting a new tank? on the dashboard to start the cycling journey. The card only shows on a tank with no readings yet, so do it before you log a test or link equipment. More in Guided journeys .
What does "tank profile" mean, and why does it ask so many questions?

The tank profile describes your system: size, livestock, lighting, and how you dose and test. Cora uses your answers to set sensible starting ranges, and to make Reef Buddy and Cora Assistant talk about your tank instead of reefs in general. You can skip any section. More in Your tank profile .
One tank with no equipment takes a few minutes. Each device needs its own pairing step, so that part takes longer. You can add more later.
Can one Cora Max show more than one tank?
Yes, up to four. The Reef Room shows them side by side. For more tanks, add a second Cora Max.
Can two Cora Max screens show the same tank?
Yes. Add both to the same tank and they show the same live data. Primary Cora Max only decides which one talks to the tank's equipment. More in More than one Cora device .
What is "Primary Cora Max", and do I need to set it?

It decides which Cora Max reads a tank's equipment. Most people never touch it. With one Cora Max there's nothing to choose. The default, Any active (automatic) , lets every online Cora Max share the job. Pick a specific one only if you want a single device doing it. More in More than one Cora device .
Which device answers "Hey Cora" if I have more than one Cora Max?
Only one Cora device answers at a time. You choose it in Cora Mobile under Settings → Cora Assistant . It has nothing to do with Primary Cora Max. More in Talking to Cora .
Why can't Cora Mobile find my Cora Max when I try to pair it?

A new Cora Max is found over Bluetooth. Turn Bluetooth on, allow Cora to use it, and stand near the screen. You also need at least one tank in Cora Mobile. After the Wi-Fi step, your phone talks to Cora Max over Wi-Fi, so stay on the same network until pairing finishes. Each error message and its fix is in Troubleshooting .
Does my phone need to be on the same Wi-Fi as my Cora Max?
Only while you pair it. After that, you can use Cora from anywhere. A few of a device's own settings still need your phone on that device's network.
Does Cora Max need the internet, or just my home Wi-Fi?

Both. It needs your home Wi-Fi to reach your equipment, and the internet to reach Cora Cloud for syncing, your other devices and the Assistant. The status tag in the top bar shows which one it has. More in The Cora Max home screen .
What happens if my internet goes down?

Cora Max and Cora Mobile keep showing the last data they have and keep working with equipment on their own network. Syncing between devices, voice and the Assistant come back when the connection does.
Can I move Cora Max to a new Wi-Fi network or router?

Yes. On Cora Max, join the new network under Settings → Cora Max Settings → Wi-Fi . Your tanks, devices and account stay the same. Equipment on the old network goes out of reach until it joins the new one, so reconnect each device the way you first added it. More in Setting up Cora Max .
Why does Cora Mobile ask for Local Network and Bluetooth access?

It needs Local Network access to find Wi-Fi equipment and reach a Cora Max on your home network, and Bluetooth to pair a Cora Max and equipment that uses Bluetooth. Without them, it can't find the device. More in Cora Mobile settings .
Can I check on my tank when I'm not home?

Yes. With a Cora Max at the tank, your readings stay current wherever you are. Without one, a Neptune Apex, Red Sea or Jecod device shows the last readings your phone saved while it was on the same Wi-Fi. An AquaWiz is read through its maker's cloud, so it keeps updating either way. Readings you log by hand and the tank's history are always there.
Can I control equipment when I'm away from home?

Yes, if a Cora Max at the tank is online and can reach that equipment. Your command goes to Cora Cloud and the Cora Max carries it out. Without a Cora Max, you can control a Neptune Apex, Red Sea or Jecod device only while your phone is on its network. More in More than one Cora device .
Can two people use the same tank?

There's no shared access between two separate accounts yet. A household can sign in to the same Cora account on more than one phone. Everyone sees the same tanks, gets the same notifications, and changes apply to the whole account. For a tank sitter, Going away makes a read-only page that needs no account. A shared snapshot is only a picture.
How do I add another tank?
In Cora Mobile, open Settings and tap Add tank . Then move its devices to it, and add it to your Cora Max if you have one. More in Managing your tanks .
I removed a tank by mistake. Can I get it back?

Yes. Removing a tank only hides it. Open Settings → Removed tanks and tap Restore . Its readings, journal and devices come back as they were. If a removed tank still sends alerts, see Troubleshooting .
What equipment does Cora work with?

Neptune Apex (with DŌS and Trident), Red Sea ReefBeat equipment, Jecod and Jebao pumps and the AquaWiz KH Controller. For anything else, you can log readings by hand. Every brand, with links to its pages, is in Equipment by brand .
Is Cora affiliated with Neptune, Red Sea or Jebao?

No. Cora isn't affiliated with, endorsed by, or partnered with any manufacturer it connects to. Cora talks to their public accounts, official APIs or local network protocols. A manufacturer's own app or firmware update can change or break that connection at any time, without notice. More in Connecting your equipment .
My phone found nothing when I searched for equipment. Why?

Check that the equipment is powered on and already set up in the manufacturer's app, if it needs one. Then check that your phone allows Local Network and Bluetooth access for Cora. Cora can't find equipment that has never joined your network. More in Troubleshooting .
Is it safe to let Cora control my dosing pump?

Cora only doses what you set up: a product, an amount and a schedule you define, within the limits you set for each head. If a dose stops partway, Cora raises an alert saying so, and tells you how much went in when it can. Read it before you assume the full dose went in. More in Controlling your equipment and Troubleshooting .
How does Cora know how strong my dosing product is?
It comes from the built-in product library, which lists salts and dosing products with their published figures. If you add your own product, you enter the strength yourself. More in Dosing .
Why am I not getting any notifications?
Usually a category is switched off in Settings → Notifications , or your phone isn't allowing notifications from Cora. The steps are in Troubleshooting .
Cora isn't grading it: the alert for it is off, it has no range, or the reading is too old. See Troubleshooting .
Can I stop notifications at night?

Cora Mobile has no quiet hours of its own. Use your phone's Focus or Do Not Disturb, and let Cora through if you still want urgent alerts. On Cora Max, Night dimming dims the screen at night, and you can turn Alert sound off under SOUND & VOICE in Settings → Cora Max Settings . More in Notifications .
How do I quiet an alert for a while without turning it off?

On Cora Max, tap Snooze . It mutes that alert on that screen for the rule's Cooldown between alerts (up to 1 week). The alert stays open and its range doesn't change. On your phone, set a longer Cooldown between alerts on the rule instead. More in Alerts and thresholds .
What's the difference between Snooze and Dismiss?

Both are on Cora Max and only affect that screen. Snooze mutes the alert there for a while, and it comes back if the problem is still there when the snooze ends. Dismiss closes it there until the reading is back in range. If the problem comes back later, you get a new alert.
Why did I get an alert on my phone but not on Cora Max, or the other way round?

The switches in Settings → Notifications belong to your account, so they apply to every phone you're signed in on. Cora Max shows every alert unless on-screen alerts are turned off for that screen (on your phone, Devices , your Cora Max, Alerts ), or you snoozed or dismissed it there. More in Alerts on Cora Max .
What is Reef Buddy, and how is it different from the Assistant?

Reef Buddy is your daily briefing, written for you without you asking. It has a headline, two scores and the points behind them. Cora Assistant is what you ask questions, whenever you like, by typing or talking. More in Reef Buddy .
Why did my briefing stop, or why doesn't my second tank get one?

Reef Buddy is part of the paid plans and the 30-day trial. Each plan covers a set number of tanks, counted in the order of Settings → Reorder tanks . On a day when nothing changed, the briefing stays quiet. More in Troubleshooting .
What can I ask Cora, and what can it do?

Ask about your tank's readings, history, dosing, lab results and journal. Cora can also do things for you, like log a test or switch equipment, and asks you to confirm first. It tells you when it has no data or connection for something, instead of guessing. More in Asking Cora and Talking to Cora .
Does Cora remember what I told it last time?
Yes, within the limits on the Asking Cora page. It can use earlier context about your tank, so you don't have to repeat yourself.
Why did Cora give me a wrong or strange answer?

Cora answers from the data it has for the tank you selected. The usual causes are the wrong tank, missing readings, or a question that could mean two things. Check the tank picker or rephrase, and try again.

English, German, French, Turkish, Italian, Spanish and Polish. Cora uses one language for the whole account, so everyone signed in to that account sees the same language on every device. More in Cora Mobile settings .
I changed the language on my phone. Why did my Cora Max change too?
Language is an account setting. Change it on your phone or any Cora Max and it changes everywhere within moments.
Will old reports and alerts be translated?
No. Anything already written stays in its original language. New alerts, reports and Reef Buddy briefings use the new language.
What's free, and what needs a plan?
See Plans and subscriptions for what each plan includes.
Is the Max plan the same as Cora Max?
No. The Max plan is a subscription in Cora Mobile. Cora Max is the wall screen. You don't need one for the other.
What happens to my tank history if my trial or plan ends?
Nothing is deleted. Your tanks, devices and history stay with your account whatever plan you're on. Only the features you can use change.
Does deleting my Cora account cancel my Apple or Google subscription?
No. Cancel the subscription with Apple or Google as well. The Delete Account confirmation has a Manage subscription button for that. More in Exporting your data and deleting your account .
How do I change my email or password?

To change your password, sign out and use Forgot password? on the sign-in screen. To change your email after you've verified it, contact support. If you sign in with Apple or Google, change these with Apple or Google. More in Signing in and account recovery .
What does Cora do with my tank data?

Cora uses it to show your readings, run alerts, and power Reef Buddy and Cora Assistant. What's stored and how it may be used is in Exporting your data and deleting your account , Cora Mobile settings and the privacy policy.
Can I get a copy of everything Cora has stored about my tank?

Yes, you can export it from Cora Mobile. Exporting your data explains what the export includes. Still can't find your answer? Troubleshooting goes through fixes symptom by symptom, or email cora@coraiq.tech .

docs.d: What Cora means by tank, source, widget, threshold, Primary Cora Max, feed mode, scene and the other words you'll see in the apps.
x: The words you'll meet in Cora Mobile and on Cora Max, in alphabetical order. Each one links to the page that explains it in full.

The one language your whole Cora account uses: English, German, French, Turkish, Italian, Spanish or Polish. It isn't set per person or per device. Change it in Settings → Language on your phone or on any Cora Max, and every device follows within moments. Anything already written stays in its original language. See Cora Mobile settings .
How long ago a reading was taken, shown on every parameter widget as now , 1h , 2d . It isn't when the screen last refreshed. An old age means the reading itself is old.

Cora telling you something needs attention. Usually it's a reading outside the range you set. It can also be a parameter moving too fast, an equipment fault, a device that stopped reporting, a consumable running low, or a lab result coming in. Most alerts clear by themselves once the problem passes. See Alerts and thresholds .
The Cora device that answers when you say "Hey Cora". You pick it in Settings → Cora Assistant . Only one device answers at a time. It's a different setting from Primary Cora Max .
The AquaWiz KH Controller, an alkalinity tester. Cora reads it through AquaWiz's own cloud. See Equipment by brand .

A rule that runs by itself, like "if temperature goes above 27, turn on the fan". Each rule has a trigger , optional conditions and one or more actions. Find them in Cora Mobile under Settings → Automations . See Automations and scenes .
Adjusting a probe so its readings match a known reference, usually a calibration solution. You can record when you calibrated or cleaned a probe. See Parameter Mapping and probes .
A Cora Max setting that stops anyone switching equipment from that screen, by touch or by voice, after a set time with no touch. Readings and questions still work. See Cora Max settings .

How a command to your equipment ended. Confirmed : the equipment reported back that it did it. Unconfirmed : sent, but nothing reported back, so check the device. Refused : it didn't run. No change : it was already that way. See Controlling your equipment .
An extra check on an automation , such as a reading being above a value. The actions only run when the conditions are met. See Automations and scenes .

The shortest time Cora waits before sending the same alert again, from 15 minutes to a week. It keeps one ongoing problem from pinging you every few minutes. You set it for each alert rule as Cooldown between alerts . See Alerts and thresholds .

The part of Cora you ask questions and ask to do things. You can type or talk to it in Cora Mobile, and talk to it on Cora Max. It's also the name of the settings group where you choose the answering device and data sharing. See Asking Cora .

The service that keeps your phone, your Cora Max and your equipment in step, and stores your history. Syncing between devices and the Assistant need it. Readings you already have, and equipment on its own network, keep working without it.
The wall screen for the reef room. It shows your tanks live, reads your equipment around the clock, and you can talk to it. See Setting up Cora Max .
The phone app. The icon on your home screen says Cora . See Setting up Cora Mobile .

A button in the dashboard editor. Cora proposes a whole layout from what the tank reports and has linked. It works on a paid plan and during the trial, and needs AI data sharing on. Templates are ready-made layouts to start from. See Editing the Cora Max dashboard .
CO₂ in the water, in mg/L, as an ICP report gives it. It isn't the CO₂ of the air in your room. See ICP and health reports .

One pump of a Neptune DŌS doser. You can give each head a use (a water change, kalkwasser, a reactor, feeding and more), track it in litres or large containers, and set its own limits. If a head loses contact mid-dose, Cora raises a restore alert. See Controlling your equipment .
One delivery of liquid from a DŌS head or another dosing pump, using the product and amount you set. Cora logs every dose so your consumption and history match up.

A pause for feeding. On a Neptune Apex, Feed starts one of the feed cycles, A to D , programmed on the Apex, and the Apex decides what pauses and when it comes back. A Jecod pump can pause for feeding from its own page. Some Jecod pumps can't end the pause by themselves: keep the pump's page open on your phone until the pause ends, or the pump stays stopped. See Outlets and controls and Controlling your equipment .
How you usually feed, set once for the tank (for example, flakes twice a day). After that you only log the days that differ, and Reef Buddy takes both into account. See The journal .
A step-by-step plan Cora walks you through, such as cycling a new tank or working through a problem. See Guided journeys .
A deeper, periodic look at a whole system. It takes every parameter, source, dose and recent lab result into account together. See ICP and health reports .
A lab water test that covers a wide range of elements. Upload the PDF your lab sends, or have the lab send it to Cora, and Cora tracks every element over time. See ICP and health reports .
One specific point in a Reef Buddy briefing, such as a parameter drifting, two sources disagreeing, or something you haven't tested in a while.
Jecod and Jebao pumps. Cora reads and controls them over your network or Bluetooth. See Equipment by brand .
Your record of what you did to the tank. Cora reads it too, so you can ask "what did I do before the alkalinity dropped?" and get an answer. See The journal .
The Neptune Systems controller, with its DŌS doser and Trident tester. Cora reads it on your home network. See Equipment by brand .
A switchable socket on your controller. In Cora it has three states: Auto , Off and On . See Outlets and controls .
Something you can measure in your water, like alkalinity, calcium, nitrate or temperature.
Where you tell Cora what each probe on a controller measures, and which device feeds each reading. See Parameter Mapping and probes .

The Cora Max that reads a tank's equipment on your network for you. Set it to one Cora Max, or to Any active (automatic) , where every online Cora Max for the tank shares the job. It's about reading equipment, not voice (that's the answering device ). Change it in Cora Mobile: Settings , open the tank, then Primary Cora Max . See More than one Cora device .
A six-digit number Cora Max shows at the end of setup. It's the only way into recovery on that Cora Max. You can also find it with the Cora Max's details in Cora Mobile. See Updates and recovery .
Red Sea's family of connected equipment: ReefDose, ReefRun, ReefMat and ReefATO+. Cora reads it on your home network. See Equipment by brand .
Your daily briefing. It has a headline, two scores ( Stability out of 100 and Data as a percentage), and the insights behind them. It's part of the paid plans. See Reef Buddy .
The Cora Max screen that shows all your tanks side by side. On screen it's called Cora Tanks . See The Reef Room .
A tank you removed. Its data is kept, and you can bring it back from Settings → Removed tanks . See Managing your tanks .

A Cora Max dashboard layout you've kept under My dashboards . You can apply it again later or load it onto another tank or Cora Max. The phone dashboard has no saved designs. See Editing the Cora Max dashboard .

A named group of actions, like "Water change" or "Night". You can run it when you want, on a schedule, or from inside another automation . Scenes are shared by Cora Mobile and Cora Max. See Automations and scenes .

A button on a Cora Max alert. It mutes the alert on that Cora Max for the rule's cooldown (up to a week) without closing it. Dismiss , the other button, closes it on that Cora Max until the reading is back in range. Your phone's notifications aren't affected by either. See Alerts on Cora Max .

Where a reading came from: a probe, a controller, a lab result, or you with a test kit. Every reading has one, so Cora can tell you when two sources disagree. If more than one source reports the same reading, Parameter Mapping is where you choose which one to trust, or leave it Automatic.

The coloured dot on each row of the Devices tab in Cora Mobile. Green is working, orange is a warning or fault, red is offline and grey means Cora doesn't know yet. See Adding, editing and removing devices .
The tag in the Cora Max top bar that says how this screen is getting its data, such as Online , Cloud , Stale or Offline . See The Cora Max home screen .
A body of water you track. A frag system or a quarantine tank counts as a separate tank. See Your tank profile .
The range you're happy with for a parameter. It can be a range, a ceiling or a floor. You set it, and the defaults are only a starting point. See Alerts and thresholds .
Neptune's tester for alkalinity, calcium and magnesium. It runs with a Neptune Apex. See Equipment by brand .
What wakes an automation : a parameter crossing a value, an alert, a time of day, or a device going offline or coming back. See Automations and scenes .
Tank-sitter mode. You make a dated plan with a checklist of jobs, and Cora turns it into a read-only page you can share with whoever looks after the tank while you're away. See Going away .
"Hey Cora", the phrase that starts a voice conversation on Cora Max. You can turn it off on each Cora Max and tap the Cora icon instead. See Talking to Cora .
One tile on a dashboard that shows one thing, such as a value, a gauge, a graph or an outlet. See Widget reference .

Cora Mobile is the phone app. You set almost everything up here (tanks, devices, dashboards, alerts, dosing products), and it's what you carry when you're away from the tank. The icon on your home screen says Cora . Cora Max is the wall screen for the reef room. It shows the same tanks and the same live data, big enough to read from across the room, reads your equipment around the clock, and you can talk to it. Both use the same account, so your tanks, readings, devices and records are the same on each. Each screen keeps its own dashboard layout, and a Cora Max's Wi-Fi, brightness, sound, wake word and child lock apply only to that screen. More in More than one Cora device . Every reading shows its source and age. If two sources disagree, such as a probe and a test kit, Cora tells you instead of quietly averaging them. When something starts to drift, Reef Buddy brings it up in your daily briefing.

docs.d: Check on Cora Max whether a command really reached your equipment, who or what asked for it, and why one was refused.
x: Activity is the log of every attempt to change something on your equipment, and what happened to it. It's the same log your phone shows. Look here first when something you asked for doesn't seem to have happened. Open it from the tank menu (tap the tank name in the top bar), or go to Settings → [your tank] → Activity . The legend at the top explains each outcome.

Each row shows the equipment and what was asked, for example Return: Turned off , and the time. It also tells you two more things. What asked for it. For example Tapped on this Cora , Voice on this Cora , Cora app , Voice in the Cora app , Automation rule or Sent from the cloud . How it travelled. LAN means it went over your own network. VIA CLOUD means it went through Cora Cloud. If you have more than one Cora Max, the entry also says which one carried it out.

The legend at the top of the screen repeats these. Outcome Means Confirmed The equipment reported back that it did it Unconfirmed Sent, but nothing reported back. We don't know whether it worked Refused Didn't run. A safety rule, a lock or the equipment itself turned it down No change It was already in the state you asked for Under a Refused or Unconfirmed entry, a line says why, and what to check before you try again. For example: No device answered in time, so it MAY still have run. Check the equipment before repeating this.

On a touchscreen, a command that was sent but never acknowledged looks the same as one that worked. This screen shows you the difference. Find the entry for what you asked. If it's Refused , read the reason under it. Nothing ran. If it's Unconfirmed , check the equipment itself before you try again, so you don't do it twice. If it still doesn't add up, see Establishing why something changed .
Activity shows what the system did. The journal shows what you did by hand. Between them, they explain most surprises.

docs.d: What to do when an alert pops up on Cora Max, how to snooze or dismiss it, change alert thresholds at the wall, and set the alert sound.
x: This page covers what Cora Max does when something needs your attention, and what you can change at the wall. How ranges, rules and phone notifications work is in Alerts and thresholds .

When a reading goes out of range, a device reports a fault, a dose is missed or a supply runs low, Cora Max shows the alert in the middle of the screen. There are three buttons under it. Respond by voice starts a conversation with Cora about this alert, so you don't have to tap anything else. More about this in Talking to Cora . Snooze silences the alert on this Cora Max for a while. The button shows how long, for example Snooze 1 h . That's the cooldown set for this alert in Cora Mobile's alert settings, and it can be as long as 1 week (handy for something like a low reagent level that won't change for days). Dismiss closes the alert now. It stays quiet on this screen until the problem is gone. If it comes back later, you'll get a new alert. When the alert is about a doser, such as a DŌS or ReefDose head running low or a missed dose, the card also has an Open DŌS or Open ReefDose button. It takes you to that doser's page, where its alerts are set. If Snooze or Dismiss shows an error, try once more. If it keeps failing, see An alert is not clearing . Snooze only affects this Cora Max While an alert is snoozed or dismissed, this Cora Max stops popping it up, sounding it and speaking it, and it leaves the top bar. Your phone still gets its notifications, other Cora Max screens still show the alert, it stays in Notification history , and your alert settings don't change.

Every active alert also shows up as a small tag in the top bar, big enough to spot from across the room. If there are more than fit, you'll see +2 (or however many). Tap a tag to bring that alert back to the middle of the screen. Tap +2 to open Active alarms , the list of everything that's active. Tap one in the list to open it.

Settings → Cora Max Settings → Notification history is the inbox for your whole account. It holds every briefing, alarm and account notice for your system, including the ones this screen didn't raise and anything your phone missed. When a reading goes out of range and comes back, you see both.

Alert thresholds and Units first, then the Primary Cora Max for this tank. Tap the tank name in the top bar and choose Alert thresholds , or go to Settings → [your tank] → Alert thresholds . Both open the same ranges you see on your phone, and a change you make here applies everywhere. You can also change a threshold by long-pressing its widget on the dashboard, or by voice: "Hey Cora, set the pH alert to 7.9 to 8.4." Cora tells you the change and waits for your OK. Each parameter in the list has its own switch. An alert you've switched off says Alert off . Cora keeps its range, but it doesn't grade that reading while it's off. The widget stays neutral grey and never raises an alert. If a parameter has no alert yet, it says No alert set , and Add alert sets one up with the range shown. Each reading has its own switch. A reading with no alert shows No alert set and an Add alert button. The threshold sheet has the same switch at the top, next to Alert on or Alert off . If you save a new range on an alert that's off, Cora asks Turn this alert on? Tap Turn on to switch it on with the new values, or Keep off to save them and leave it off.

Equipment with something that runs out has an Alert settings button on its page on Cora Max. That's a Trident (reagents and waste), DŌS heads, Red Sea ReefDose, ReefATO+ and ReefMat. Pick the level you want to hear about, and you get one notification when it's passed. On a DŌS head, Missed dose alerts also tells you when the head misses its scheduled doses. What each doser alert means is in Doser alerts .
Alert sound, spoken alerts and waking the screen

These belong to this screen only. Find them in Settings → Cora Max Settings . Alert sound (under SOUND & VOICE ) plays a tone when a new alert arrives. Its slider sets the volume. Spoken alerts (under SOUND & VOICE ) has Cora say the alert out loud. Wake screen on alarm (under DISPLAY ) lights up a dimmed screen when an alert arrives. Critical alerts always wake it. To stop a Cora Max showing alerts on its screen at all, open Cora Mobile, go to Devices → your Cora Max, and turn off Alerts . Notification history and your phone's notifications don't change. One alert for the whole account Each device doesn't raise its own copy of an alert. Cora Max, your phone and any other screen show the same one, and it clears on all of them when the reading is back in range.

docs.d: Build, run, edit and delete scenes on Cora Max, from Settings → Automations or a scene tile on the dashboard.
x: A scene is a saved set of equipment actions that run together, either for a set time or until you stop it. You can build, run and edit scenes on Cora Max. Scenes made on your phone and on Cora Max are the same scenes. Automation rules (the "when this happens, do that" kind) are set up on your phone. More in Scenes and automations . The Scenes list, filtered by tank. With no scenes yet, it says so and offers New Scene.

Settings → Automations opens Scenes , the list of every scene for all your tanks. If you have more than one tank, there's a filter chip for each, plus All tanks . Tap a scene to edit it, or tap New Scene to build one. If you have more than one tank and no filter is picked, Cora Max asks Which tank is this scene for?

A new scene: a name, Permanent or Timed, Ask before running, then Add Step. Type a Scene name . Tap Add Step and pick what the step does. You only see the kinds of equipment this tank has: Apex Outlet : switch a Neptune Apex outlet to ON , OFF or AUTO . Control a Red Sea device : for example ReefDose: dose now , ReefDose: set daily dose , ReefRun: set pump speed , ATO: start a manual fill or ReefMat: advance the roll . Control a wavemaker : set a Jecod pump's flow or wave mode, turn it on or off, or Pause for feeding . Run a Trident test : alkalinity, combined or nutrients. Each run uses reagent. Run an Apex feed cycle : pick the cycle. The Apex runs the feed timer and resumes by itself. Add more steps the same way. You can reorder or remove them. A step this screen can't edit says Not editable here . Edit that one on your phone. Choose how long it runs. Timed runs for the minutes you set in Run for (minutes) . Permanent runs until you stop it. Leave Ask before running on unless you're sure the scene never touches anything that needs a second look. Tap Save . Doses in a scene A Neptune DŌS head can never be a scene step. A ReefDose: dose now step can, and it has its own Max per dose (mL) . Leave it empty for 10 mL. A dose above that ceiling is refused, never made smaller. Keep Ask before running on for any scene that doses.

Scenes show up as tiles on the dashboard. Tap Run to start one. If the scene asks before running, Cora Max first lists what it's about to do, one line per step. Read it, then run it or cancel. While a timed scene runs, its tile counts down to the end and shows Stop if you want to end it early. A permanent scene's tile shows it as running until you tap Stop . When a scene ends or you stop it, the tile shows Restoring… while Cora puts the equipment back. Running or stopping a scene goes through Cora Cloud, like any other command. You'll find the result in Activity . Scenes can't be run by voice on Cora Max. Use the tile, Settings → Automations , or your phone. If a scene won't run or won't stop, have a look at Troubleshooting . Child lock covers scenes too While Child lock has locked the screen, you can't run, stop or edit a scene from it, just like every other control.

To change a scene, open it from Settings → Automations or long-press its tile on the dashboard. Change what you need and tap Save . To remove it, tap Delete Scene . This can't be undone. An older Cora Max can run a scene but not edit it Older Cora Max versions still show and run every scene, but can't change one. Update Cora Max ( Updates and recovery ), or edit the scene on your phone.

docs.d: Switch Apex outlets from Cora Max, start or cancel feed mode, use the Outlets & Feed drawer, and what Auto, Off and On mean.
x: This page covers switching outlets and starting feed mode from Cora Max. You can do it from outlet tiles on the dashboard, from the Outlets & Feed drawer, or by voice. These controls act on your tank There's no undo. Outlets with a padlock ask you to confirm first. The rest change as soon as you tap. A command can come back Confirmed , Unconfirmed (sent, but nothing reported back), Refused or No change . More in Controlling your equipment .

Every outlet is in one of three states. Auto hands the outlet back to its Apex programming. Most of the time, that's where an outlet should be. Off and On are manual overrides. They take effect right away and stay until you change them back . They don't expire, and nothing resets them for you. A manual override doesn't expire Set it back to Auto when you're done, because nothing else will. An override isn't a lock, though. You, your voice or an automation can still change it later.

Outlet tiles show the three states, with the current one highlighted. Tap the one you want. Some outlets have a padlock . It means the outlet asks you to confirm before it changes, so a stray tap can't switch something critical. When you tap it, a dialog shows the outlet, its current state, the override you're about to set and what that can do to the tank. There's no lock to turn off somewhere else. By default the padlock is on heaters, chillers, return pumps, top-off (ATO), feeders and any outlet Cora can't classify. Lights, skimmers, wavemakers, dosing pumps, reactors, UV and fans switch on one tap.

You'll only see this on a tank with a Neptune Apex. Tap the small Outlets & Feed label at the bottom of the dashboard, or swipe up anywhere on the dashboard. It opens Controls , with FEED across the top and OUTLETS below. Feed cycles across the top, then the outlets picked for this dashboard. It shows the outlets and feed cycles you picked under Outlets & Feed in the dashboard editor , or all of them if you haven't picked any. Padlocked outlets ask you to confirm here too. Sockets on other controllers are switched from their own device pages, see Controlling equipment from Cora Max . If an outlet tap comes back with The Apex did not answer: it may have applied , check the outlet before you try again.

Feed mode is the safe way to pause flow while you feed. Your Apex pauses the equipment that should pause, leaves the rest alone, and puts everything back by itself when time's up. Use it instead of switching pumps off by hand. It puts the system back even if you forget. Feed cycles are Feed A, Feed B, Feed C and Feed D, shown as A , B , C and D under FEED . They're the cycles programmed on your Apex, and each one can pause a different set of equipment. Pick the one that fits what you're doing. Cancel ends a running cycle early and puts everything back right away. Start one from the drawer, or say "start feed mode" . If Cora Max says the Apex didn't answer, the feed may already be running. Check the return pump before you start it again.

You can switch outlets by voice, for example "turn the skimmer off" or "put the fan back on auto" . Before anything reaches your equipment, Cora checks with you first . It tells you what it's about to do and waits for your OK. If it isn't sure what you asked, it won't act. More in Talking to Cora .

Every request is logged, with what asked for it and how it went, whether it came from Cora Mobile, a Cora Max, voice, the Assistant or an automation. On Cora Max, tap the tank name in the top bar and choose Activity . On your phone, it's under Settings → Activity . More in Activity on Cora Max . When something changed and you don't know why, look there first.

docs.d: Add, move and remove tiles on the Cora Max dashboard, pick a grid, use templates or Design with AI, and save layouts to reuse on any Cora Max.
x: This page shows how to arrange the tiles on a Cora Max dashboard. It uses a fixed grid : the display doesn't scroll, so every tile has to fit on one screen. That's the main difference from the phone dashboard. Open the editor from the tank menu : tap the tank name in the top bar, then Dashboard layout . It's also under Settings → [your tank] → Dashboard layout . Grid sizes across the top, then the tiles. This is a layout screen, so each tile shows its type and source instead of a reading. Nothing is saved until you press Save. You can also edit it from your phone In Cora Mobile, open the Devices tab, tap your Cora Max, then tap Dashboard layout on the tank's card. It's quicker than arranging tiles by hand on a wall screen, and the result shows up on Cora Max as soon as you save.

Pick the grid size first. Changing it later moves all the tiles around. Grid Tiles Feels like 2×2, 3×2, 3×3 4–9 Large. Easy to read from across the room. 4×4, 5×3, 6×4 16–24 The usual choice for a full system. 6×5, 8×4, 8×5 30–40 Dense. A whole reef room on one screen. 9×5, 10×5 45–50 Very dense. Best on the largest screens. Auto up to 32 Cora picks a shape that fits however many tiles you've added. A fixed grid holds as many tiles as it has cells, up to 50 on 10×5. Auto has its own limit of 32 tiles. Past that, the text gets too small to read from a distance. Not sure? Start with Auto Add the tiles you want and leave the grid on Auto . Cora picks a shape that fits them. If you like it, you can switch to that fixed shape afterwards. Changing the grid only drops tiles when they don't fit When you change the grid, Cora doesn't throw tiles away by position. Tiles that still have a valid cell stay where they are, and the rest are packed back in, in order. You only lose tiles when the new grid has fewer cells than you have tiles , and Cora tells you how many went. Going from 10×5 (50 cells) to 3×3 (9) loses most of them.

Tap an empty cell (it shows a + ) to open Add widget . Under TYPE , pick the kind of tile, then what it shows (a reading, an outlet, a device or a scene). Under SIZE , pick how big it is. A tile can be one or two cells wide and one or two cells tall. A Graph also has a TIME RANGE . A doser tile has Show remaining as , in Days or Milliliters (mL) . Tap Add . The gestures are listed along the top of the editor: tap a tile to edit , long-press to move it , and ✕ to remove it . Clear all empties the grid so you can start over. The tile types are Value, Gauge, Graph, Status, Outlet, Scene, ReefBeat, Apex module and Jecod. You'll find them in the Widget reference . The Scene tile only exists on Cora Max. It runs a scene with one tap.

Outlets & Feed in the editor chooses which outlets and feed cycles appear in Controls , the drawer you swipe up from the bottom of the dashboard. It doesn't add tiles. If you pick none, Controls lists all of them. To put an outlet on the grid itself, add an Outlet tile. More in Outlets and controls .

Templates sits at the top of the editor, beside My dashboards and Design with AI . It's open on every plan and never uses AI, so it also works without AI data sharing. It opens Dashboard templates , a few ready-made layouts built from what this tank reports and has linked: Overview : few, large tiles, with the core parameters as gauges and your main devices Equipment : one tile per device first, then outlets and the core parameters Parameters : charts and readings first, with devices and outlets last Each one shows a preview and how many tiles it has on which grid. Tap Use this . Cora asks Replace your dashboard? first. Tap Save current as preset first if you want to keep the layout you have, or Replace . Nothing is saved until you press Save .

The editor has a Design with AI button. It works on a paid plan and during the trial. Cora proposes a whole layout from what this tank reports and has linked, and shows how many tiles it has and on which grid. Tap Use this to put it in the editor, or Try again for another. You can make 5 designs per tank per day. An AI design replaces what's on this dashboard now. Nothing is saved until you press Save , and you can keep your current layout first by saving it to My dashboards . On the free plan, Design with AI points you to the plans. It also needs AI data sharing turned on in Cora Mobile. More in Asking Cora .

People read a wall display from further away than a phone, and usually with a quick glance. Make your key parameters two by two. Alkalinity, temperature and pH are things you'll want to read without walking over. Put controls at the edges. Outlet tiles are the ones you reach for, and they're easier to hit at the sides. Group tiles by subject. Keep everything about dosing together and everything about flow together, because you scan a wall by area. Keep trace elements small. They and other slow-moving numbers are for reference, so a one-by-one value tile is plenty.

Nothing you do in the editor takes effect until you press Save . If you leave with unsaved changes, Cora asks Discard changes? first. My dashboards keeps designs you want to come back to. They're saved on your account, not on this screen, so any Cora Max on your account can load them, for another tank or for a replacement screen. Save this design stores what's in the editor. You can keep up to 30. Load puts a saved design in the editor. Designs saved from your phone are marked Phone . Before loading, Cora tells you how many tiles will come across. Anything that can't, such as a reading this tank doesn't report or a device that isn't on this tank, is listed under Left behind: with the reason. For example, you might keep a dense everyday layout and a big-tile one for when you're working in the tank.
Each tank has its own layout. Switch to that tank and open Dashboard layout from its tank menu, or use Settings → [that tank] → Dashboard layout .

docs.d: Device pages on Cora Max for Neptune Apex, Trident and DŌS, Red Sea ReefBeat, Jecod and AquaWiz, by brand.
x: This page covers what you can see and do on each device's page on Cora Max, brand by brand. Cora Max reaches the same equipment as your phone. Open a device page from the devices icon in the top bar, from Settings → Devices , or by tapping a device tile on the dashboard. Feed A to D and Cancel, then the outlets, laid out for a wall screen. These controls act on live equipment There's no preview and no undo. A command goes out the moment you tap, but sending it doesn't mean it's done. It comes back Confirmed , Unconfirmed , Refused or No change , and you can see which in Activity . You add, assign and remove equipment on your phone. Cora Max shows it once your account has it. See Connecting your equipment .

Device Shows Neptune Apex Probes and outlets, and you can switch each outlet Trident Test state, reagent and waste levels, and a button to start a test DŌS , including the DŌS QD Each head's dosing, schedule, runway and container volume (with pause, fill, dose now and a one-time twenty-second measure) Red Sea ReefBeat Whatever the unit has: dosing heads, reservoir, roller days, pump mode, plus a full ReefDose plan editor and ReefMat settings Jecod Pump mode and intensity, and its day program AquaWiz No page of its own. It's listed in Devices , and its readings go on the dashboard Most device pages have a pencil to rename the device. The new name shows on your phone too. More in Devices and device health .

The Apex page lists your probes and outlets, with your feed cycles at the top. Each outlet switches between Auto , Off and On , and padlocked outlets ask you to confirm. How the three states and feed mode work is in Outlets and controls . You can also reach outlets from the Outlets & Feed drawer at the bottom of the dashboard. It lists the outlets turned on for this dashboard (or all of them, if you haven't picked any). A large Apex with several modules shows all of its outlets and probes. DŌS heads never show up in the outlet list, so you can't switch one on there and leave it running. Dose from the head's own page.
The Trident page shows the test state and the reagent and waste levels. You can start a test from here, and set a refill alert with Alert settings .

You have to measure a DŌS head once before Cora will dose with it by hand. Measure to dose runs the head for twenty seconds into a measuring container, and you enter how much came out. Cora keeps one measurement per head and uses the newest, whichever Cora Max took it. The head's page shows where and when it was measured. After a manual dose, a head you'd set to Off in Apex Fusion stays Off. Any other head goes back to Auto. A DŌS has no level sensor and keeps dosing from an empty container. Set a refill alert with Alert settings on the DŌS page. More in Doser alerts .
What a head is used for

In a head's settings sheet you can set its use type . The options are Supplement , Water change: new saltwater in , Water change: old water out , Kalkwasser , Calcium reactor , Food or Top-off , and Other . The use type changes two things. How big a container it can track. Every use type can track a container of up to 1,000 litres. Above the Apex's own 150 litre counter, Cora tracks the volume itself, and Cora resets the Apex counter every 100 litres. Whether it can take a large dose by hand. Supplement and Food heads keep today's small, careful ceiling. Every other use type can have its own Largest dose by hand limit, up to a hard ceiling of 10 litres, and its own daily limit for automations and the Assistant . A large hand dose also needs Large doses turned on in the head's settings, off by default. Turn it on only after you've watched the first large dose run at the tank. You can link a water-change pair (new saltwater in, old water out) as a Paired head and set a Balance warning above amount. If the two heads' totals for the day drift apart by more than that, Cora warns you. A pair that's out of balance usually means one side isn't pumping as it should.
If a large dose is interrupted

A large dose changes what the head is doing on the Apex for a while, then puts its normal schedule back. If the connection drops partway through, Cora Max shows a banner on that head's page: "A large dose on [head] did not finish cleanly. Cora keeps trying to put its program back; check it in Apex Fusion." Check the head in Apex Fusion yourself, then tap I checked the head in Fusion to clear the banner. Only do this once you've confirmed that the head's own schedule is running, not Cora's dosing program. If the banner won't clear, or keeps coming back, have a look at Troubleshooting .

Each Red Sea unit has a page that fits what it does: ReefDose heads and containers, the ReefATO+ reservoir, ReefMat roll days and ReefRun pump speeds. Supply alerts for ReefDose heads, the ReefATO+ reservoir and the ReefMat roll are set with Alert settings on the unit's page. If a Red Sea unit stops itself, its page tells you what's wrong and puts the fix right next to it. That's Resume , Clear emergency , Sensor cleaned , I already loaded a new roll , or Reset for a dosing head. A ReefDose plan and ReefMat's scheduled advance, model, position and New roll all work the same way here as on your phone. Controlling your equipment has the detail.

The Jecod page shows the pump's mode and intensity, and you can change both. Its status sits in the title row, next to the pump's name. The top bar holds the power switch, the pattern running now and Feeding with four pills: 5 , 10 , 15 and 30 min. Tap a pill to pause the pump for that long. Below the bar are two cards: Same all day : tap a setting to run it all day. Schedule : the day graph and the list of plans, with now on the current one. Edit opens the editor, and the ⋮ menu holds Copy schedule to… , Save schedule as… and Saved schedules… . The card that is running has an outline and a Running chip. A Jecod pump has no End feed button. Every Jecod pump that can pause for feeding shows the 5 , 10 , 15 and 30 min pills. On a Jecod Pro the Feeding tile in the wave patterns does the same, for 10 minutes. Through a Cora Max that is away from the tank, a Jecod pump feeds for 10 minutes only. A pump that cannot feed right now shows the reason in one short line under the pills, and a long press shows the full sentence. You can write Jecod pump day programs at the wall as well as on your phone. The editor is the same, with a day graph, a list of periods and a row of actions. More in Scheduling equipment .

An AquaWiz KH Controller has no page of its own on Cora Max. It's listed in Devices , where you can rename it, and its readings show on the dashboard like any other source. Set it up and manage it on your phone, see Connecting your equipment .
You set refill thresholds (reagent, containers, reservoirs) on the device's own page here, the same as on your phone. More in Consumables .
Logging and calculating at the tank

Two things are often easier at the wall than on a phone. Log parameters lets you type test results on the on-screen keyboard. It's in the tank menu. Dose calculator works out a correction from the tank's volume and your product strengths. Open it from a parameter's page. It uses the same volume and product strengths as your phone, so a dose worked out here matches one worked out there. More in Dosing .

When more than one Cora Max shows a tank, one of them reads that tank's equipment. The device pages call it the Cora Max at the tank. The others can still open the device pages, and a status tag reading Cloud means you're on one of them. They show what the Cora Max at the tank last read and how long ago. Each command goes through Cora Cloud to the Cora Max at the tank, which carries it out. A few things only work on the Cora Max at the tank. Measure to dose and Re-measure only show up there. Once a head is measured, Dose now works from any Cora Max. You can change a Jecod schedule from another Cora Max only if the Cora Max at the tank has read the pump in the last hour, and never for a pump that only talks over Bluetooth. One Apply to the pump from there sends at most 12 changes, so send a bigger edit in parts.
What was changed, and by what
Every action is logged along with what caused it. More in Activity on Cora Max .

docs.d: See and rename the equipment Cora Max reads, choose which Cora Max reads each tank, fix a tank whose readings stopped, and manage a Cora Max from your phone.
x: Settings → Devices on Cora Max lists the equipment it can see and how each device is doing. The devices icon in the top bar opens the same list, filtered to the tank on screen.

Filter by tank, then each device grouped by brand, with a one-line summary and its tank. Cora Max sees the same equipment as your phone, because they both read the same account. Use the filter chips at the top to show All tanks or just one. Devices are grouped by brand. Each entry has a status dot (grey when Cora doesn't know yet, green when it's working, orange for a warning or fault, red when it's offline), a one-line summary of what the device holds ( 21 outlets · 4 feeds , 19 tests left ), the tank it belongs to and when it was Last seen . Tap a device to open its page. Every device page opens with a Status section. What each page can do is in Controlling equipment from Cora Max . If the list says Still loading some devices: this list may be incomplete. , give it a moment.
Tap the pencil on a device's row, or on its page, and type the new name. Leave the name empty to go back to the device's own name. The name is shared with your phone, so it changes there too.
You add, assign and remove devices on your phone. Cora Max shows and controls them. With no devices yet, this screen says Add devices in the Cora app. More in Adding, editing and removing devices .
Primary Cora Max: which device talks to your equipment

The Primary Cora Max is the Cora Max (or other Cora device) that reads a tank's controller and other equipment for the whole account. Each tank only needs one device doing this. Every other screen shows what it reads. To see or change it, open Settings → [your tank] → Primary Cora Max . You have two options. Any active (automatic) means every online Cora device that can reach this tank's equipment shares the work, and the latest write wins. Use this unless you have a reason to pin one device. Pin one device, so only that device reads the equipment. If it goes offline, no other Cora Max takes over. Only Cora Mobile, open on the same Wi-Fi, reads the equipment until you pin a different one or switch back to Any active (automatic) . You set this once for the tank, and it applies to every Cora screen. You can change it from any Cora Max that shows the tank, or from Cora Mobile ( Make Primary Cora Max on the Cora Max's page). More in More than one Cora device . Primary Cora Max and the Answering device are two separate settings Primary Cora Max decides which device reads your equipment . The Answering device in Cora Mobile decides which one answers "Hey Cora" . If you have more than one Cora Max, you can set them separately. More in Talking to Cora .

If one tank's readings stop while another tank on the same screen keeps updating, start here. Open Settings → [that tank] → Primary Cora Max . Check that a device is assigned and that it's online. If another Cora Max for this tank shows Main Cora offline in its top bar, the primary has lost its connection. What the status tag means is explained in The Cora Max home screen . Settings → Cora Max Settings → Network & Updates → Device polling shows how often this Cora Max reads your devices. You can only view it here. It's set from Cora Mobile. Check the Status section of Settings → Cora Max Settings . It shows polling status, last poll time and last cloud write for each tank, without changing anything. If that doesn't help, have a look at Troubleshooting .
Managing a Cora Max from your phone

Open the Devices tab on your phone and tap the Cora Max. The top card shows its variant, firmware and when it was last seen. From there you can rename it, and when there's a new version, tap Update to v… to install it now. The Recovery PIN card sits just below. One Cora Max's own settings on your phone: Child lock, Device Polling and Time zone, then its tanks. These settings only affect that one screen , just as if you'd changed them at the wall: Section Settings Display Brightness , Dim after Sound & Voice Alert sound turns the alert chime on that screen on or off, and Alert volume sets how loud it is. Alerts still show on screen, and alert history and push notifications don't change Child Lock Child lock locks that screen's touchscreen and stops it switching equipment by voice Network & Updates Device Polling (how often it reads your equipment) and Time zone (used for night dimming and the update window) Under Tanks , each tank this Cora Max shows has a card with Dashboard layout , Edit tank and its polling device. Add Tank and the remove icon change which tanks it shows, and those changes apply to the whole account. You can only make them on your phone. The steps are in Setting up Cora Max . Which device is the Primary Cora Max for a tank can be changed from either your phone or Cora Max. Under Reset , Reset display sends the screen back to its pairing screen. It stays on your Wi-Fi, so you can pair it again over Bluetooth, and your tank data is kept. Remove device takes it off your account. Your tank readings are kept, and you can pair it again later.

docs.d: The morning Reef Buddy briefing on Cora Max, giving feedback on insights, recording probe care, ICP results, health reports and history charts.
x: Cora Max shows the same insights as your phone, on a screen big enough to read from across the room. Reef Buddy, ICP Reports , Health Reports and Parameter History are all in the tank menu (tap the tank name in the top bar).

Each day at your Briefing time , once today's briefing is ready, Reef Buddy appears over the dashboard. If Reef Buddy briefing is on, Cora reads it out loud. It closes by itself after ten minutes if nobody touches it, or close it yourself. To read it again, tap the Reef Buddy icon in the top bar. A dot on the icon means you haven't opened today's briefing yet. The full Reef Buddy screen is in the tank menu. Set the time and the read-aloud switch in Settings → Cora Max Settings → REEF BUDDY . The Briefing time is the same on every device on your account.

Today's score and summary, the insights, and what moved since your last ICP. The Reef Buddy screen shows the Stability and Data scores, the summary and the insights behind them. What the scores mean is explained in Reef Buddy . After you log a test or add an ICP result, the screen shows New readings since this briefing and an Update briefing button. Tap it to redo the briefing with the new numbers. It works once a day. After that the screen says You can update the briefing once a day. Next update: tomorrow.

Tap an insight to open it. Why am I seeing this? shows the readings, target and journal entries it's based on. Does this match what you see? Answer Confirmed , Already knew , Doesn't match or Not sure , then say whether it was Valuable or Not really . Cora uses your answers to learn your tank. When Cora doubts a reading, it shows it under Worth a check , for example a probe that may be drifting. There you can: tap I checked it to record what you did to the probe, tap Add to Maintenance to make it a task ( Check pH probe or Verify dosing configuration ), or tap Dismiss . It stays quiet unless the problem persists.

After you clean, calibrate or replace a probe, record it so Cora doesn't mistake the jump for probe drift. Open that parameter's history chart and tap Record probe care (the sensor icon at the top), or use I checked it on a probe insight. Pick what you did, optionally enter a reference reading, and tap Log probe care . More in Recording probe care .

The latest result and its score, every report on file, and the open report's summary. This screen shows your uploaded results with the score and summary for each, plus trends across all your reports. The score out of 100 comes from comparing your results with their ranges. If any parameter is out of range, the score can't go above 70. If one is far out of range, it can't go above 40. The colour shows the band. Green (healthy) is above 70, amber (needs attention) is 40 to 70, and red (critical) is below 40. You upload results from your phone. More about this in ICP and health reports .

You can run and read a health report at the wall. Open Health Reports and tap Generate . It's the same assessment your phone makes from your parameters, ICP results and journal, and its score works the same way as an ICP score. Health reports need AI data sharing. If it's off, Cora Max shows Data sharing needed . Turn it on in Cora Mobile under Settings → Cora Assistant . Each plan has a number of health reports a month. When they're used up, you see Monthly limit reached until next month. More in Plans .

Open the tank menu and tap Parameter History , then pick a parameter. It opens as a full-screen chart. Tapping a tile on the dashboard opens the same chart. On a wall display, this is the best way to spot a slow drift. A month of alkalinity at full screen shows a trend a small tile can't. The parameter name in the header is a dropdown, so you can switch parameters and keep the timeframe. Timeframe sets the period. Source shows All sources or one source this parameter comes from, such as Apex , Manual , ICP or ReefBeat . Only sources this parameter has are listed. Compare draws a second parameter on the same chart. Each source has its own colour. Device readings such as ReefBeat and AquaWiz are squares, and readings someone took by hand (Manual and ICP) are larger dots. All sources shows every source side by side and never averages one source's readings with another's. Dashed lines mark logged doses. Under the chart you'll see Latest , Avg , Min , Max and the 30d low and 30d high . For alkalinity, calcium and magnesium, the Dose calculator button at the top works out a correction dose. More in Looking into a parameter .

An active journey shows as a slim banner at the top of the tank's dashboard. Tap it to see the steps and how far along you are. On a new tank that's cycling, you can take readings here. Log a test on the cycling screen records ammonia, nitrite and nitrate without reaching for your phone. An issue journey is view only at the wall. Starting one, completing a step, recording an outcome, and resolving or dismissing it all happen on your phone. More about this in Guided journeys .

docs.d: Log a test, add a journal entry, record a feed and tick off maintenance on Cora Max, and what you still do on your phone.
x: Cora Max shows the same records as your phone, but you can't change all of them here. This is what you can do at the wall. Area On Cora Max Log parameters Type in test results Journal Read entries and add new ones. Log Fed extra or Skipped a feed in one tap Maintenance Mark a task Done or Snooze it. You create and edit tasks on your phone Livestock View only. Add and edit on your phone All of them are in the tank menu (tap the tank name in the top bar) and under Settings → [your tank] . Anything you add here shows up on your phone right away, and the other way round.

Open Log parameters , tap a parameter, type the reading with the on-screen keypad and save. It goes straight to the tank's dashboard and history, so you can record a test at the tank where you did it. You can also say "Hey Cora, log alkalinity 8.1." Cora checks each number before it saves. If one looks like a typo, or is far outside your last 30 days, it asks Double-check these values? and may suggest what you meant ( "did you mean 8.1?" ). Tap Go back to fix it, or Save anyway if the reading is right. If a newer reading for that parameter is already showing, your value says Saved to history only . It's kept in the history and charts, and the dashboard keeps showing the newer one.

Open Journal from the tank menu and tap New entry . Give it a title, and add a description, tags or a photo if you like. Attach water params saves the current readings with it. Or say "Hey Cora, log that I fed mysis." More about this in The journal .

At the top of the journal screen, Fed extra and Skipped a feed each add one journal entry. A line below them shows your feeding routine, for example Feeding routine: Flakes: 2 pinches, twice a day . You set the routine in Cora Mobile. With none saved, the line says Set your feeding routine in the phone app . If Cora Max reads your Neptune Apex, it also logs a Feed A to D cycle when one starts, whether you started it here, at the Apex or in Apex Fusion. There's no journal icon in the top bar The icon next to the devices icon is Reef Buddy , and its dot means today's briefing is unread. You add journal entries from the tank menu or by voice.

Tasks due, with Snooze and Done on each, and what was completed recently. The top of the screen says how many tasks are due. Below it, Upcoming lists each task with TODAY , IN 3d or OVERDUE 2d , and Completed · last 7 days shows what you've done lately. Tap Done when you finish a task. Tap Snooze to push it back by 1 Day , 3 Days , 1 Week , 2 Weeks or 1 Month . You add and change tasks on your phone. More about this in Maintenance .

This is the full inventory, with what's In the tank and what's No longer in the tank . It's view only here. You add and edit livestock in Cora Mobile, and what you add there shows up on this screen right away. More about this in Livestock . One set of records Each tank has one journal, one livestock inventory and one maintenance list. Cora Max and your phone show the same records.

docs.d: See all your tanks side by side on Cora Max, read each tank's health at a glance, and switch between tanks.
x: The Reef Room is the overview of every tank this Cora Max shows. Open it with the grid icon at the far left of the top bar. On screen, it's called Cora Tanks . Each tank with its health score, headline parameters and anything out of range.

A Cora Max shows up to four tanks , and the Reef Room gives each one an equal share of the screen. Tanks Layout 1 One large tile 2 Side by side 3 Three across 4 Two by two With one tank, Cora Max opens on that tank's dashboard. The grid icon still takes you to the Reef Room. Four tanks is the limit You can assign at most four tanks to a Cora Max, when you pair it or later on your phone under Devices → your Cora Max . If you try to add a fifth, you'll be asked to remove one first. If you have more tanks than that, use a second Cora Max. Each one keeps its own set. The steps are in Setting up Cora Max .

Each tile sums up one tank. A coloured bar down the left edge, for the worst state on that tank. A health score in a ring (with one to three tanks). Next to it is a line like 3 of 37 parameters out of range (or All 37 parameters in range ), and how many are near their limits. A status chip: N out of range , N to watch for readings near their limits, Healthy , or Monitoring while there's nothing to grade yet. The tank's key readings. Wider tiles add a 24-hour trend line to each one. When it last updated , and Open dashboard . The health score looks at how far out each parameter is and how much it matters, so lots of good readings can't hide one serious problem. It only reads 100% when nothing is out of range. If a major parameter like alkalinity, calcium or magnesium is far out of range, the score can't go above 33%. A heavy metal far out of range can bring it down to 0%. Parameters near their limits are counted on the tile but don't lower the score. Under the tiles, a strip shows today's insights and each tank's health headline in turn. Tap a card in the strip to open that tank's Reef Buddy .

Tap a tile , or Open dashboard , to go to that tank. Swipe sideways on the dashboard to move between tanks and back to the Reef Room. The grid icon takes you back to the Reef Room from any tank page. You won't see it on the Reef Room itself. Each tank has its own dashboard layout, so the screen changes completely as you move between them. More in Editing the Cora Max dashboard .

docs.d: Every Cora Max setting, from rename, brightness, night dimming, speaker and wake word to child lock, language, Wi-Fi, re-pairing and factory reset.
x: Open settings with the gear at the far right of the top bar. The CORA group (Automations, Devices, Cora Assistant), then one row per tank. Settings has three groups. CORA holds things that apply to all the Cora devices in your household. TANKS has one row per tank. The last row, Cora Max Settings , is everything about this screen alone. Two kinds of setting Some settings belong to your account . They're the same whichever phone or Cora Max you look at, and changing one changes it everywhere. Others belong to this screen only, like its brightness or Wi-Fi. The CORA and TANKS groups are account settings. Cora Max Settings holds this screen's own settings.

These apply to every Cora device on your account. Row Opens Automations Every scene for all your tanks, with a filter by tank. More in Scenes on Cora Max Devices The equipment Cora controls, for all your tanks. Tap the pencil to rename a device. More in Devices and device health Cora Assistant Which device answers when someone says "Hey Cora." More in Talking to Cora

Each tank has a row that opens its own settings. Alert thresholds sets the healthy range for each reading. More in Alerts on Cora Max . Units picks the units this tank uses for salinity, temperature, alkalinity, volume, phosphate and nitrate. With Auto , each reading shows in the unit its source recorded it in. If you pick a specific unit, everything on this tank is converted to it, on every screen and when the Assistant speaks. Primary Cora Max is the device that reads this tank's equipment. More in Devices and device health . Dashboard layout is this tank's Cora Max layout. More in Editing the Cora Max dashboard . Under RECORDS & REPORTS : Log parameters , Journal , Maintenance , Livestock , Reef Buddy , Health Reports , ICP Reports and Activity . More in Journal, livestock and maintenance and Reef Buddy and reports .
Cora Max Settings: everything about this screen

The last row in Settings carries this Cora Max's name. It opens everything that applies to this screen only . At the top is a card with this screen's name and its firmware version ( Cora Max · firmware 0.28.170 ). Tap the pencil ( Rename this device ) to give it a new name, for example "Living room". Show details lists its Cora ID , MAC address , Wi-Fi network , IP address , its tanks and the account it's paired to. Support may ask you for these. Below the card are these sections. Section Covers DISPLAY Brightness . Dim after and Dim level : how long with no touch before the screen dims, and how dim it gets. Night dimming , with From , To and Night brightness . Show clock in the top bar. Wake screen on alarm SOUND & VOICE Speaker ( Internal , 3.5 mm or BT ), Alert sound and its volume, Spoken alerts , and Wake word on or off. More in Talking to Cora REEF BUDDY Reef Buddy briefing reads the morning briefing aloud. Briefing time is when it arrives, the same on every device CHILD LOCK Child lock on or off, and Lock after . See Child lock below NOTIFICATIONS Notification history , the inbox for your whole account with every briefing, alarm and account notice LANGUAGE The one language your whole account uses: English, Deutsch, Español, Français, Italiano, Polski or Türkçe. See the note below NETWORK & UPDATES Wi-Fi , Firmware Update , and Device polling , which shows how often this Cora Max reads your devices (you change it in Cora Mobile) STATUS One card for each tank this screen shows, with Polling status , Last poll , Last cloud write and Cloud save . View only HELP & ABOUT Help & Support (contact support or report a problem) and About (version and licenses) RESET Re-pair this device and Factory reset . See below When the screen has dimmed, your first tap only wakes it. It doesn't press anything. Language applies to your whole account When you change Language , every phone and every Cora Max on your account switches with it. New reports, alerts and briefings come in the new language. Reports and alerts you already have stay in the language they were written in and aren't translated again. Alarms and their recoveries, newest first, each with its tank name. Recoveries are logged as well as alarms. So when a parameter goes out of range and comes back, you see both halves.

Child lock stops small hands from changing anything on a screen that children or visitors can reach. Readings, charts and alerts keep updating. Only the controls stop. To turn it on, go to Settings → Cora Max Settings → CHILD LOCK , turn on Child lock , and pick Lock after . The choices are 30 seconds, 1, 2, 5, 15 or 30 minutes (1 minute unless you change it). Cora Max then locks itself after the Lock after time with no touch. Every touch resets that time. While it's locked: Every tap is ignored, and Locked shows in the middle of the screen for a few seconds. A tap still wakes a dimmed screen. The volume keys stop changing the volume. Cora still answers questions by voice, but refuses anything that changes your equipment. To unlock, do either of these: Press Volume Up or Volume Down three times within two seconds. The two seconds start at the first press. Hold five fingers in the top-right corner of the screen for ten seconds. Unlocked shows for a moment. The lock comes back after the Lock after time with no touch. To turn child lock off for good, unlock, then turn off Child lock in Settings. The five-finger hold also opens the Recovery PIN box Holding five fingers in the corner is also how you get into Recovery . So after the screen unlocks, a Recovery PIN box opens as well. Tap Cancel to go back to the unlocked screen. Cancelling doesn't count as a wrong PIN. If Cora Max has no PIN yet, you see Recovery is unavailable instead. Tap OK . The volume-key unlock doesn't open recovery. Child lock isn't a security lock. Anyone who sees how you unlock it can do the same.

Cora Max Settings → RESET has two options. Re-pair this device clears this screen's pairing and takes it back to the pairing screen. Factory reset also clears every preference saved on this screen. Its confirmation tells you what's cleared and what's kept. Neither one touches the tank data already saved to Cora Cloud. Both remove this Cora Max from your account and make it forget its Wi-Fi network, so you pair it again from Cora Mobile like a new one. If Cora Max can't reach Cora Cloud to remove itself, it says This Cora Max is still listed in the Cora app. Remove it from there too. Open it in Cora Mobile under Devices and choose Remove device . The RESET section, with Re-pair this device and Factory reset. You can also reset a Cora Max from your phone, in Cora Mobile under Devices → your Cora Max → Danger zone . That helps when the screen is out of reach or locked. Option Where Wi-Fi What happens Re-pair this device On Cora Max Forgotten Back to the pairing screen. Pair it from Cora Mobile Factory reset On Cora Max Forgotten Pairing and every on-screen setting cleared. Pair it from Cora Mobile Reset display Cora Mobile, Danger zone Kept Back to the setup screen the next time it's online. Pair it again over Bluetooth Remove device Cora Mobile, Danger zone Removed from your account and its tanks. It can be paired again later In every case, tank data already saved to your account is kept. Pair the device to a tank again and it comes back. What you lose is the screen's own setup, like its display, sound and voice settings. You may get your layouts back Before a reset, Cora Max saves a copy of its configuration. If you pair it back to the same tank , it offers Restore previous layout for this tank? Take it, or choose Start fresh if you wanted a clean screen.

A Cora Max can show one tank or several, and you switch between them from the top bar. You choose which tanks it shows on your phone , under Devices → your Cora Max. More in Changing which tanks it shows .
Cora Max keeps itself up to date. Updates download in the background and install inside the update window. More in Updates and recovery .

docs.d: Pair a new Cora Max with Cora Mobile over Bluetooth, connect it to Wi-Fi, pick its tanks, and move it to another tank later.
x: This page takes you from a new Cora Max to a working wall screen. You pair it from your phone over Bluetooth, and you don't type anything on the screen itself. Set your tanks up on your phone first Cora Max shows the tanks and devices on your account, and it can't create a tank itself. Set them up in Cora Mobile first. Cora Max picks them up as soon as you pair it.

Cora Max, plugged in and switched on. It's meant to stay plugged in. Cora Mobile on your phone, signed in, with at least one tank already created. Bluetooth turned on on your phone, and the phone close to Cora Max. Your Wi-Fi network name and password. Put Cora Max where you can see it from across the room and talk to it, away from splashes and salt creep.

Turn Cora Max on. It shows a pairing screen that says Open the Cora app on your phone , then Tap Add Device. and Pick this Cora Max from the Devices list. Below that it shows Discoverable as and its name, ending in a short code. If you're pairing more than one, that code tells them apart on your phone. Waiting for your phone. The bottom line shows the name your phone will list. The same screen has a short notice about integrations with other makers' equipment. The Terms you accepted in Cora Mobile also cover Cora Max.

Everything else happens in Cora Mobile. A sheet walks you through five steps, shown across its top: Connect · WiFi · Auth · Tanks · Done . Find it. Open the Devices tab, tap Add Device , then Cora . The Add Your Cora screen lists Cora devices on your network and nearby setup devices found over Bluetooth. Tap Scan if yours isn't there yet, then tap your Cora Max. Add Device, then Cora. Cora Mobile looks on your Wi-Fi and over Bluetooth, with Enter IP Address Manually below. Connect. Your phone connects to Cora Max over Bluetooth and shows its MAC address, firmware, variant and hardware revision. Check it's the right one, then tap Continue . WiFi. Pick your network from the list, or tap Rescan , and type the password on your phone. From here on your phone talks to Cora Max over Wi-Fi, so keep the phone on the same network. Auth. Your phone links Cora Max to your account. This runs by itself, and Cora Max shows its own progress, such as Verifying your account… and Setting up your tank… . Cora Max shows each step while your phone links it to your account. Tanks. Under Assign Tanks , pick the tanks this Cora Max will manage, up to four . Done. Your phone says Cora Max is set up and shows a Recovery PIN . Tap the button that opens your tank's dashboard, or Go to Devices . Cora Max shows Paired , then Opening dashboard… . Write the Recovery PIN down The Recovery PIN has six digits and it's the only way into recovery on that Cora Max. To use it, hold five fingers on the top-right corner of the screen for ten seconds, then enter the PIN. Recovery lets you redo Wi-Fi, pair again, check for an update or factory reset. You can find the PIN again on your phone under Devices → your Cora Max → Recovery PIN , but never on Cora Max itself.

Bluetooth is off. Turn it on, then tap Scan again. Turn Bluetooth on and scan again. Bluetooth permission is off for Cora. Allow Bluetooth for Cora in your phone's settings, then tap Scan . An iPhone may also ask for local network access. Allow that too. No nearby Cora setup devices were found over Bluetooth. Stand next to Cora Max, check it still shows the pairing screen, and scan again. No Tanks Found at the Tanks step. Your account has no tank yet. Create one in Cora Mobile, then retry the step. Not linked to your tank yet at the end. Cora Max is paired, but the tank link didn't finish. Tap Retry now . Until it finishes, alerts for this screen use default ranges. More fixes in Troubleshooting .
