Cora Max now sees the same tanks, devices, readings and records as your phone. If one of your tanks had a Cora Max before, Cora Max asks Restore previous layout for this tank? Restore brings back the display, sound and alert settings the old one saved. Start fresh skips them. A tank with no readings yet shows No readings yet and a Log your first test button. Cora Max builds a starting dashboard from your tank profile. It doesn't copy the one on your phone. You can pair more than one Cora Max to the same account, say one in the fish room and one in the living room. Each one can show different tanks and has its own layout. If two show the same tank, More than one Cora device explains which one reads the equipment.

The big-screen dashboard is a fixed grid, and everything has to fit on one screen. The quickest way to arrange it is from your phone: open the Devices tab, tap your Cora Max, then tap Dashboard layout on the tank's card. You can also do it at the wall from the tank menu. To reuse a layout from another Cora Max or another tank, load it from My dashboards in the editor. More in Editing the Cora Max dashboard .
Moving Cora Max to another tank

You change which tanks a Cora Max shows on your phone. Cora Max's own settings can't do it. In Cora Mobile, open the Devices tab and tap your Cora Max. Under Tanks , tap Add Tank and pick the tank. A Cora Max takes up to four. When it already has four, the button is gone, so remove one first. To take a tank off this screen, tap the red remove icon ( Remove tank ) on that tank's card, then tap Remove . To move Cora Max from one tank to another, add the new tank, then remove the old one. The new tank gets a starting dashboard built from its profile. Arrange it with Dashboard layout . If this Cora Max was the pinned Primary Cora Max for the tank you removed, that pin is cleared and the tank goes back to Any active (automatic) . More in Devices and device health .
Cora Max updates itself. A new version downloads in the background and installs at night. Your version is shown at the top of Settings → Cora Max Settings . More in Updates and recovery .
Moving it to a different Wi-Fi network
Go to Settings → Cora Max Settings → Wi-Fi , pick the new network and enter the password. Cora Max stays paired, so you don't need to set it up again.

docs.d: What the top bar, status tag, alert tags, tank menu and dashboard on Cora Max mean, and how to switch tanks and open Outlets & Feed.
x: This page explains what you see on Cora Max. It shows one tank at a time, with live readings filling the screen so you can read them from across the room. One tank's dashboard fills the screen, with the top bar above it.

The top bar, numbered left to right to match the list below. From left to right: The grid icon opens the Reef Room , the overview of every tank this screen shows. The tank name , with a small arrow. Tap it to open the tank menu , which has every screen for the tank you're looking at. The full list is below. Alert tags show what needs attention right now: readings out of range, device faults, missed doses or low supplies. Tap a tag to bring that alert back to the middle of the screen. If there are more than fit, you'll see +2 (or however many). Tap it to see every active alarm. The clock . You can hide it with Show clock in Settings → Cora Max Settings . The status tag shows what this screen is doing right now. Green means all is well, blue means busy, amber needs a look, and red is a fault. Every status is listed below. Battery and Wi-Fi . The devices icon opens Devices , filtered to this tank. A tank with no devices doesn't show it. The Reef Buddy icon opens today's briefing. A dot means you haven't read it yet. The Cora Assistant icon starts a voice conversation. The gear opens settings. Cora Assistant starts listening right away Tapping the Cora Assistant icon starts a live voice session. If you wanted settings, that's the gear on the far right.

Tag Meaning Online This screen is collecting your readings, and they're up to date Cloud Another Cora is collecting this tank's readings and this screen is showing them. They're just as up to date as with Online . If you have more than one Cora, the one that isn't collecting shows this Polling Apex , Voice active Busy with something right now (blue) Polling off Collecting is turned off for this tank. You can turn it back on in Cora Mobile Updating Collecting is paused while an update installs Stale Readings have stopped coming in. The screen shows the last ones it got Apex retry 12s Your Apex didn't answer. Cora Max tries again when the countdown ends Cloud sync failed Your Apex answered, but its readings couldn't be saved to Cora Cloud, so the dashboard falls behind. Cora Max keeps trying Cloud save refused Cora Cloud is refusing to save some of this screen's data. Nothing is wrong with your tank or with Cora Max, and nothing needs changing on this screen. The fix is a Cora Cloud update. Open Settings → Cora Max Settings and scroll to the Status section, where the Cloud save line says which data is affected. Then contact support Offline No connection. The screen shows the last data it got Offline, retrying in 45s Your network is up, but Cora Cloud has been out of reach for more than 30 seconds. Cora Max reconnects by itself, and the countdown shows when it tries next Main Cora offline This screen is a second Cora Max for this tank, and the Primary Cora Max (the one pinned to read this tank's equipment) has gone offline. This screen keeps showing the last data it has until the primary comes back or you choose a different Primary Cora Max. More in More than one Cora device Apex password Your Apex turned down the saved password. Have a look at Troubleshooting How the retry countdown works Cora Max tries to reconnect at a steady pace. It waits about 15 seconds after the first drop, then 15 seconds again, then 30 seconds twice, then once a minute until it gets through. It never gives up. Offline, retrying in 45s is normal.

The rest of the screen is the dashboard, a fixed grid that keeps every widget visible. It doesn't scroll. Widgets work the same as on your phone, but big enough to read from a few steps back. What each shape shows is in the Widget reference . To change what's on the dashboard, see Editing the Cora Max dashboard . Every widget with a measured parameter shows its age and source , just like on your phone. A number with 2d next to it is two days old. Device and control tiles show their own state instead.
After the Dim after time with no touch, the screen dims. Your first tap only wakes it, so it can't press a control by accident. Tap again to use the screen.

The tank menu, opened from the tank name in the top bar. Tap the tank name to open the menu for the tank on screen. Item Opens Log parameters Type in test-kit readings on the on-screen keyboard Journal The journal for this tank Reef Buddy The latest briefing Health Reports Health assessments Maintenance The task list ICP Reports Uploaded lab results Parameter History Pick any parameter that has data and open its chart Alert thresholds The healthy range for each metric on this tank Livestock This tank's inventory, view only on this screen Activity Every outlet, feed and dose , and what happened Dashboard layout Arrange the widgets on this screen Units The display units for this tank's readings Tank settings The full settings screen for this tank

Tap the grid icon at the far left of the top bar to go to the Reef Room , then open the tank you want. You can also swipe sideways on the dashboard. Each tank has its own dashboard layout, so the whole screen changes as you switch.

On a tank with a Neptune Apex, a small Outlets & Feed label sits at the bottom of the dashboard. Tap it, or swipe up anywhere on the dashboard, to open Controls . FEED starts one of your Apex feed cycles with A , B , C or D . Cancel ends it early. Outlets can each be switched between Auto, Off and On. It lists the outlets and feed cycles you picked for this dashboard, or all of them if you haven't picked any. More in Outlets and controls . This drawer controls real equipment A command goes out the moment you tap, but sending it doesn't mean it's done. It comes back Confirmed, Unconfirmed, Refused or No change, and you can see which in Activity . Feed mode is the safe way to pause flow for feeding, because it puts everything back by itself. A manual Off stays off until you change it back.
If something looks out of place
If readings look stale, or the status tag is amber or red, start with Troubleshooting .

docs.d: How Cora Max updates itself, the install window and update channel, checking the version, the Recovery PIN, and what to do if Cora Max won't start or shows a support code.
x: Cora Max keeps itself up to date. This page explains when updates install, how to check your version, and how to get Cora Max going again if it won't start normally.

New versions download in the background as soon as they're out. They install inside the Install window , 3 to 5 in the morning unless you change it, so the screen doesn't restart while you're looking at it. When a version brings release notes, Cora Max shows them. You don't need to do anything to stay current.
Checking the version and update settings

Firmware Update, in the NETWORK & UPDATES section of Cora Max Settings. Your version is on the card at the top of Settings → Cora Max Settings ( Cora Max · firmware 0.28.170 ), and under HELP & ABOUT → About . Settings → Cora Max Settings → Firmware Update (in NETWORK & UPDATES ) shows the version you're on and whether an update is waiting. Tap Check for updates to look now, or Download & install when one is there. Under Update settings on the same screen: Install window sets the hours updates may install, with a Start and End time, in this screen's local time. The time zone is set in Cora Mobile, under Devices → your Cora Max → Time zone . To see whether this screen is reading your devices and saving to Cora Cloud, go back to Cora Max Settings and scroll to STATUS . It shows each tank's Polling status , Last poll , Last cloud write and Cloud save .

A prompt tells you what's new and gives you two choices. Update now installs right away and restarts. It takes about a minute. Keep Cora Max powered. Snooze 24 hours hides the prompt and asks you again a day later. While an update is waiting, a small dot shows on the Settings icon in the top bar and on the Firmware Update row. The dot stays through a snooze, so you can still see an update is there. It goes away while the update installs. If you leave it, the update installs itself in the Install window . You can also start it from your phone: in Cora Mobile, open Devices → your Cora Max and tap Update to v… . You don't lose readings during an update Your data lives in your account. When Cora Max restarts, it comes back with the same tanks, dashboards and history.

Recovery is a maintenance mode for when Cora Max won't start normally, or when you need to fix its setup without a laptop. Hold five fingers in the top-right corner of the screen for ten seconds . The Recovery PIN box opens. Type the 6-digit PIN and tap Enter . You saw the PIN when you paired Cora Max. You'll also find it in Cora Mobile under Devices → your Cora Max → Recovery PIN . Cora Max itself never shows it, so a guest or a child leaning on the screen can't get into recovery. If you type the wrong PIN three times, recovery locks for 30 seconds, and for longer after each further wrong try. Too many attempts tells you how long to wait. If Cora Max has never been online since pairing, it has no PIN yet and shows Recovery is unavailable . Connect it to Wi-Fi first. From Recovery you can: Re-do Wi-Fi setup : pick a new Wi-Fi network and password Re-pair this device : clear the pairing and set it up again with Cora Mobile Force OTA check : check for updates now Factory reset : remove the pairing and every setting on the screen Tank data already saved to Cora Cloud is kept in every case. If Cora Max fails to start several times in a row, it can also roll itself back to the previous version. The same gesture unlocks child lock If Child lock is on, holding five fingers in the corner also unlocks the screen. Tap Cancel in the Recovery PIN box if you only wanted to unlock. A screen in recovery isn't controlling anything Your controller keeps running its own programming. But an automation step that this Cora Max has to carry out can't run while it's in recovery. The rule fires, but the step never reaches the equipment.
If Cora Max shows "Cora Max hit a problem"

This screen means something went wrong while Cora Max was starting or running. It shows a Support code (it starts with CXB- ). Write down the support code. Wait. Cora Max restarts itself in about 10 minutes. To restart it now, hold five fingers in the top-right corner for 10 seconds. If it keeps happening, email cora@coraiq.tech with the support code.
If a unit does not restart
Email cora@coraiq.tech with the version shown on screen and the message it shows. Don't re-pair it first. The pairing state often helps work out what happened.

docs.d: Use voice and "Hey Cora" on Cora Max, what it can and can't do by voice, AI data sharing and your monthly allowance, and what to do when Cora doesn't answer.
x: You can talk to Cora Max. It's the easiest way to use it when your hands are wet or you're across the room. Voice on Cora Max is Cora Assistant, the same assistant you use on your phone.

AI data sharing has to be on. Turn on Allow Cora Assistant to use saved tank data in Cora Mobile, under Settings → Cora Assistant . While it's off, Cora Max shows Voice needs your OK and nothing you say is sent. More in Asking Cora . Voice uses your monthly AI allowance. Voice sessions have their own monthly count, and each spoken reply also uses messages from the same Assistant allowance as your phone, more than a typed one. Your plan sets both. More in Plans and subscriptions .

Say "Hey Cora" . Cora Max listens in the background for the wake phrase and starts a session when it hears it. Or tap the Cora Assistant icon in the top bar. Cora starts listening right away and answers out loud. There's no confirmation step, so if you tapped it by mistake, tap Cancel . Nothing is lost. Cora Assistant listening, with Cancel underneath.

Alert sound, Spoken alerts and Wake word, with Reef Buddy below them. These are in Settings → Cora Max Settings → SOUND & VOICE , and apply to this screen only. Wake word turns background listening on or off. With it off, tapping the Cora Assistant icon still works, so use this if you'd rather the screen wasn't listening all the time. Speaker picks where sound comes out: Internal , 3.5 mm or BT (Bluetooth). For voice, the internal speaker is the weakest of the three. BT opens Pair a Bluetooth speaker , where you put your speaker in pairing mode and pick it from the list.

If you have more than one Cora Max at home, only one of them answers the wake phrase. That's the Answering device . It's a separate setting from the device that reads your equipment, which is the Primary Cora Max (more in Devices and device health ). Change it in Settings → Cora Assistant on any Cora Max, or in Cora Mobile. It applies to your whole household. Only the Answering device listens for "Hey Cora". Your other Cora Max screens don't listen while it's online. If it goes offline, or hasn't been seen for more than 15 minutes, another Cora Max starts listening in its place, and stops again once it's back. The switch takes about a minute, so if nobody answers "Hey Cora" right after one, say it again or tap the Cora Assistant icon.

Questions about the tank: "What's my alkalinity?" "Has the temperature been stable today?" "When did I last change water?" "Why is pH lower than usual?" "Compare the last six months of my magnesium with my latest ICP." You don't need to repeat yourself for follow-ups. After a question about the display tank, "and the frag tank?" works.
What Cora can do by voice

Switch a Neptune Apex outlet on, off or back to auto: "Turn the skimmer off." "Put the fan back on auto." Start an Apex feed cycle (Feed A to D): "Start feed mode." Start a Trident test: "Start an alkalinity test." Change an alert range: "Set the pH alert to 7.9 to 8.4." Log a test result: "Log alkalinity 8.1." Write in the journal: "Log that I did a twenty litre water change." "Log that I fed extra mysis." "Log that I skipped the morning feed." Control Red Sea equipment: dose from a ReefDose head, change its daily dose, start a ReefATO+ fill, advance a ReefMat, or set a ReefRun pump's speed. Control Jecod pumps.
What Cora can't do by voice on Cora Max

Run or stop a scene. Use the scene tile or Settings → Automations . Dose from a Neptune DŌS head. Use the device's page on Cora Max. Change Cora Max's own settings, add devices or edit the dashboard. Cora Assistant on your phone can do some of these. More in Asking Cora .

Before anything reaches your equipment, Cora checks with you. It tells you exactly what it's about to do and waits for your OK. You can answer out loud, in your account's language. If what you said could mean more than one thing (you have two heaters and said "the heater"), Cora asks which one instead of guessing. Anything Cora does to equipment shows on screen with its result, and is logged in Activity . Confirming is your call The confirmation is there so nothing catches you by surprise. Read or listen to it before you agree, especially for anything that switches off life support or doses.

For the tank on screen: your live readings and how old each one is, up to about six months of history for any parameter, your recent journal and your lab results. If a reading is stale, Cora tells you so and doesn't treat it as current.
Which tank Cora is talking about
It's whichever tank the screen is showing. Switch tanks in the top bar first, or name the tank in your question.

Say "stop" or "goodbye" . You can also tap Cancel while Cora is listening, or Stop talking while it's speaking. If nobody speaks for about 30 seconds, the session ends by itself. Cora stops listening when the session ends.
While Child lock has locked the screen, Cora still answers questions, but it refuses anything that changes your equipment.

Reef words are hard, and equipment names are harder. If Cora keeps mishearing a device, give it a more distinct name. Go to Settings → Devices , tap the pencil next to the device (or Rename on its page), and type a short, everyday name. The new name shows on your phone too.

Check that Wake word is on ( Settings → Cora Max Settings → SOUND & VOICE ), that this Cora Max is your Answering device (see above), and that its volume is up. A noisy sump or a filter right next to Cora Max can stop it hearing the wake phrase. Move it, or speak a bit closer. If Cora Max shows a message instead of listening: Message What to do Voice needs your OK Turn on AI data sharing in Cora Mobile ( Settings → Cora Assistant ), then try again Free voice limit reached This month's allowance is used up. Upgrade your plan in Cora Mobile, or wait for next month Too many requests Wait a moment, then try again Connection issue Check this Cora Max's Wi-Fi, then tap the Cora Assistant icon again If that doesn't help, have a look at Troubleshooting .

docs.d: Can't sign in? Reset a forgotten password, verify or fix your email address, change your name, and sign out of Cora Mobile.
x: Your account keeps your tanks, readings and devices together. This page helps you get into it and keep it in order. Creating an account for the first time is covered in Setting up Cora Mobile .

Start with the one that matches what you see. You forgot your password. See Forgotten password . Cora says the address already has an account with a different sign-in method. You first signed up another way. Sign in the way you did the first time: with your email and password, with Google, or with Apple. You're in, but your tanks are missing. You're probably in a second, empty account. That happens when the other sign-in method uses a different address, such as Apple's Hide My Email or another Google account. Your tanks aren't gone. Sign out and sign in the way you did the first time. Cora says there were too many sign-in attempts. Wait a few minutes, or tap Forgot password? to reset your password and sign in right away. Cora says the account has been disabled. The message names an address to write to. Email it from the address you signed up with to have the account restored. The sign-in won't go ahead at all. Tick I agree to: Terms and Conditions and Privacy Policy first. Every way of signing in needs it.

You can sign in with an email address and password , or with Continue with Apple or Continue with Google . Use the same method every time. If you use Continue with Apple , choose Share My Email when Apple asks, so lab and ICP results can reach your Cora account. If you already chose to hide it, add your real address under Lab and ICP emails .

On the sign-in screen, tap Forgot password? , enter your email address and tap Send Link . Open the link on the same device and set a new password. The message is the same either way You'll see "if that address has a Cora account, a reset link is on its way" , whether or not the address is registered. This stops anyone using the screen to find out who has an account. If no email arrives, you probably signed up with a different address. If nothing arrives within a few minutes, check your spam folder. Then try the other ways to sign in. An account created with Continue with Apple or Continue with Google has no Cora password to reset. A new password needs at least 8 characters, an uppercase letter, a number and a symbol.

After you sign up with an email address, Cora sends a verification email from noreply@coraiq.tech with the subject "Confirm your email for Cora" . Tap Verify my email in it. The link expires after 24 hours. Then go back to Cora Mobile and tap I've Verified My Email . If the email hasn't arrived, check your spam folder, then tap Resend verification email on the verification screen. Cora sends at most one verification email a minute and five an hour, and the first one counts. If you tap too soon, Cora asks you to wait.

Cora Mobile checks your account when you tap I've Verified My Email . If your email still isn't verified, tap Verify my email in the newest message, wait a moment and check again. If the link has expired, tap Resend verification email . Once verification goes through, it applies on all your devices.

If you mistyped it, you don't have to start again. Tap Wrong address? Change email on the verification screen and enter the right address. Cora sends a new link to it. After you tap that link, sign in again with the new address. To start over with a different account, tap Sign out on the verification screen. "Sign out and sign in again, then retry" Changing an account's email address is a security step, so Cora sometimes wants a recent sign-in first. If it asks you to sign out and back in, do that, then tap Wrong address? Change email again.
Changing your password or email later

Cora Mobile has no setting for either one once your email is verified. For your password, sign out, then use Forgot password? on the sign-in screen. For your email address, contact support from Settings → Help & Support . See Reporting a problem . An Apple or Google account's password and address are managed by Apple or Google.
Go to Settings , then the account card at the top, and tap Display name . Cora Assistant uses it to address you.

Labs and emailed ICP results find your account by email address. If your lab knows a different address from the one you sign in with, or you signed in with a hidden Apple email, add it under Settings → your account card → Lab & ICP emails . Tap Add lab email , then Send code , enter the 6-digit code from the email and tap Verify . You can add up to 3. The steps are in ICP and health reports .

Settings → your account → Sign Out signs this device out. Nothing is deleted, and when you sign back in your tanks, readings and devices are all there. Your data explains how signing out differs from deleting your account.

docs.d: See every change sent to your equipment, who or what asked for it and whether it worked, and read the tank's timeline around a date.
x: Activity lists every attempt to change something on your equipment: outlet switches, feed cycles, doses, and anything a scene or automation did. Each row shows what asked for it and what happened next, including the requests that didn't work. Go to Settings → Activity . If you have more than one tank, pick it with the tank chips at the top. The outcome key at the top, then each action with its outcome, cause and route.

Each row carries an outcome. The same key is at the top of the screen under WHAT THE OUTCOMES MEAN . Outcome Means Confirmed The device said it did it Unconfirmed It was sent, but nothing reported back. It may or may not have reached the device Refused It was turned down and didn't run. Read the row to see why No change The equipment was already in that state, so nothing was sent One refusal is different. No device answered in time means the request may still have run. Check the equipment before you try again. A command that quietly did nothing is exactly what you want to find here, so failed and unchanged requests are kept along with the ones that worked.

Each row names its cause: Cause Means This app You tapped it in Cora Mobile Voice in this app You asked by voice, on this phone Tapped on a Cora Someone used a Cora Max screen. The row says which one Voice on a Cora Max Someone spoke to a Cora Max Cora Assistant You asked Cora Assistant to do it in a chat Automation rule An automation or scene did it Sent from Cora Cloud It came from your account through Cora Cloud Unknown source Recorded before Cora could tell where it came from

Each row also has a route chip. When something goes wrong, how the request reached your equipment often explains why. Chip Means LAN Sent over your own network, straight to the equipment VIA CLOUD Sent through your account, for equipment Cora can't reach directly ROUTE ? Recorded before routes were tracked, so the route is unknown If you have more than one Cora Max, the row also says which one carried out the request.

Activity is about equipment. The tank timeline, called Tank Story on screen, is about the tank. It lays out journal entries, maintenance, livestock changes, water tests and alerts in date order, with milestones along the way. To open it, go to the journal and tap the Tank timeline icon at the top. Use the chips at the top to show only Journal , Maintenance , Livestock , Water tests or Alerts , or All . Load older story goes further back. You can add a New Entry or dictate one from here too. Use Activity when you want to know "what did something do?" Use the timeline when you want to know "what was happening around this date?" Use the timeline with the journal The timeline gathers what Cora recorded. The journal holds what you did and why. Read them side by side to see cause and effect around a date.

docs.d: Set the healthy range for each reading, choose how often an alert can notify you, and find out why a device "stopped reporting".
x: You get an alert when a reading leaves the range you set for it. This page covers setting those ranges, what happens when an alert fires, and how long Cora waits before it says a device has stopped reporting. To open the Alert Center , tap Alerts in the row of buttons under the dashboard. It's also in Settings → your tank → Alert thresholds . Active alerts, each with its severity, what triggered it and when, plus View rule and Explain this alert.

It has two tabs. Active lists the alerts that are up right now, with a count badge. Rules holds the rules that raise them. Each active alert shows the parameter and tank, the reading that set it off, a short explanation, a severity chip, the kind of rule that fired ( Threshold or Rate of Change ) and when it fired. It has two buttons: View rule opens the rule behind it, so you can adjust the range. On a doser alert, such as a DŌS or ReefDose head running low or a missed dose, this button is Open doser instead. It opens that doser's page with its alerts. Explain this alert opens Cora Assistant with a question about the alert ready to send. Check it, change it if you like, then send it.

Rules grouped by parameter, each with its own switch. Rules are grouped by parameter. Each rule has its own switch on its row, so you can turn one off without opening it. A row also shows Firing now while its alert is up, or when it last fired (or Never fired ). A dosing head's rules are named after the head and what they watch, for example Iodine · days left or Iodine · remaining . A missed dose shows up as Iodine · missed dose . Each DŌS and each ReefDose has one row of its own here, and its head alerts aren't listed one by one. Tap the row to open that doser's page. See Doser alerts . At the bottom: Add recommended rules adds any of Cora's recommended rules that are missing. It skips a parameter that already has a rule. On a tank with no rules at all, this button reads Add Default Rules . Add Custom Rule sets up a rule of your own. Pick the parameter and the Rule type , Threshold or Rate of Change . The Add Rule button at the bottom right does the same.

Tap a rule's row to open it. You'll find: Alert minimum and Alert maximum , the range itself. Leave one empty for a ceiling or a floor. Recommended , which puts Cora's suggested range back. Gauge Range (Cora display) , with Gauge min and Gauge max . These only set the scale of the gauge on Cora Max. They never raise an alert. Cooldown between alerts , explained below . Enabled , and a delete button. A device fault rule, such as a Trident out of reagent, has no range. You only choose its cooldown.

Parameters Cora can grade have a target range. The defaults come from your tank type and age when you set the tank up, and they're a sensible start. If a parameter has no usable range, Cora doesn't grade it, and its widget stays neutral grey. The quickest way to change a range is to long-press the parameter's widget on the dashboard. That opens its thresholds. A normal tap opens the parameter view instead. Alert minimum and maximum, the gauge range for Cora Max, and the cooldown between alerts. If the parameter has no rule yet, the fields start on Cora's default and a note underneath says so. Change any value to set your own. You can set: a range, with a low and a high, for things like alkalinity or temperature a ceiling, with only a high, for things where low is fine, like nitrate or phosphate a floor, with only a low Set the range your tank really runs at The defaults are only a starting point. A low-nutrient tank running at 6 dKH isn't "wrong" because a chart says 8–9. Set the range you run, and Cora tells you when you drift.

An alert fires when a reading crosses a threshold. Cora checks each reading as it comes in, so one reading outside your range is enough. A rate-of-change rule watches how fast a parameter moves instead of where it sits. Use it when the speed of a change matters more than the number. Once an alert is up, it won't keep notifying you about the same thing. The rule's cooldown decides when it may notify you again.

The bell, at the top right of the main tabs, keeps your history. The number shows how many you haven't read. More in Notifications . A push notification reaches your phone if that category is switched on. The widget on the dashboard turns amber or red. Cora Max shows the same alerts on its screen.

Some alerts are about equipment, not a reading. When a device such as a Trident or a Jecod pump reports a fault, Cora sends a notification naming the tank and the device, for example "Display tank: Return pump needs attention" . It also says what's wrong, such as a jammed rotor. When the fault clears, you get a second one: "Display tank: Return pump is OK again" . Both fall under Equipment Faults in Settings → Notifications .

When a connected device goes quiet, Cora sends "[Device]: stopped reporting" . It doesn't mean the device is broken, only that Cora hasn't heard from it for a while. You get a second notification, "[Device]: reporting again" , when it comes back. How long Cora waits depends on the device: Device Cora waits Neptune Apex About 30 minutes without an update Red Sea ReefBeat About 30 minutes AquaWiz About 3 hours, because it reports less often Jecod pumps Three missed readings in a row, on the pump's reading interval (90 minutes at the default 30) Zigbee smart plug Still silent 30 minutes after its hub restarted. Give it a name with Rename so the alert says which plug What to check depends on how Cora reads the device. Apex, ReefBeat and Jecod are read by a Cora Max over Wi-Fi. Check the device's power and Wi-Fi, and that the Cora Max that reads it is switched on and online. AquaWiz is read through your account with the maker. Check the account connection on the device's page in Cora Mobile. These notifications fall under Equipment Faults in Settings → Notifications . A Red Sea tank can also show a banner, "Red Sea readings have stopped updating" , when no phone or Cora Max is reading its ReefBeat equipment. Tap it to pick a Primary Cora Max . The full fix is in Troubleshooting .

In Settings → Notifications you choose which categories can send you a push. See Notifications , which also covers keeping nights quiet . Reef Buddy has no switch of its own. Its timing is the Briefing time row, just below Notifications in Settings. On the free plan there's no briefing notification. Cora stays quiet unless something changed The daily briefing is one push per tank per day. On a day when nothing needs you, it usually stays silent instead of telling you all is well. If Cora is pushing, something changed.
Cooldowns: how often the same alert may notify you

Each rule has its own Cooldown between alerts . You set it when you add or edit the rule. A rule that never had one uses 1 h. The cooldown doesn't hide the alert. It only limits how often Cora pushes about it. The reading is still graded, and the alert stays on the widget and under the bell the whole time. You can pick 15 min, 30 min, 1 h, 2 h, 4 h, 8 h, 1 day, 3 days or 1 week. A short cooldown suits a fast-moving reading like temperature. A long one, up to a week, suits something that stays wrong for days while you wait for a part, such as a Trident out of reagent or an empty dosing container. Snooze is on Cora Max Cora Mobile has no Snooze button on an active alert. Snooze is on the Cora Max screen at the tank, and it mutes the alert for the cooldown you picked here. On your phone, the per-rule cooldown is how you change how often you hear about something.

An alert clears on its own when the reading comes back into range. There's nothing to dismiss. You get one notification when it does, for example "Display tank: Alkalinity recovered" . If the problem comes back later, you get a new alert. Short spikes raise alerts too One out-of-range reading is enough to raise an alert, so a probe that spikes will set one off. If a source is unreliable, recalibrate it or point the widget at a different source. Don't widen the threshold. Sometimes the reading is wrong and the tank is fine, for example when a probe needs calibrating. Fix the source in that case. If you widen a threshold to silence a bad probe, you'll miss the next real problem too.

Turn off the switch on the rule's row in the Rules tab. Cora keeps the rule and its range, so you can switch it back on without setting it up again. While a rule is off, Cora doesn't grade that reading. Its widget stays neutral grey and it never raises an alert. Turn a parameter off without deleting its range Deleting a rule doesn't always stop Cora assessing that reading. Default reference bands still colour the value and can still feed the briefing. Use the rule's switch.

docs.d: Use Cora Assistant by typing or talking, what it can see, what it can do for you, the data sharing switch, and memory.
x: Cora Assistant answers questions about your tank in plain language, and can log things and run your equipment when you ask. It can see your live readings, your history and your lab results, so its answers are about your tank. Open it from the Assistant tab. An answer built from the tank's live data, with this month's message count above the box.
The tank selector at the top sets what Cora is talking about. The questions you type and the answers you get all belong to that tank.

Type in the box at the bottom and send. If you're not sure where to start, tap one of the Try asking suggestions. Some things worth asking: "Why is my alkalinity falling?" "What changed since last week?" "Is my calcium where it should be for an SPS tank?" "When did I last do a water change?" To keep an answer, tap Save to journal under it. It goes into the tank's journal .

Tap Start voice conversation to talk back and forth. Cora listens, answers out loud and keeps listening until you stop it. It's handy when your hands are wet. While Cora is speaking, tap Tap to interrupt to cut in. Tap Stop conversation when you're done.
What Cora can do for you

Besides answering, Cora can do things on the tank you picked. Ask in your own words. Ask for For example Log a test you did by hand "Log alkalinity 8.1" Write a journal entry "Note that the clownfish is hiding today" Log a feeding that wasn't the usual one "I skipped feeding this morning" Change an alert range "Set the nitrate alert to 2 to 10" Run one of your automations or scenes "Run the water change scene" Switch an Apex outlet or start a feed "Turn the skimmer off" , "Start Feed A" Start a Trident test "Start a Trident test" Dose from a DŌS head "Dose 5 mL from the iodine head" Control Red Sea and Jecod equipment "Pause the return pump" Remember something about your system "Remember that I dose two-part" Cora only offers what the tank has. If there's no DŌS on the tank, it can't dose. Logging a test, a journal entry or a feeding happens when you ask for it. Anything that changes your equipment or an alert range is different: Cora tells you exactly what it's about to change and waits for your yes. It won't act on an unclear instruction. If a command might have run but Cora couldn't confirm it, it says so. Check the equipment before you ask again. Equipment control works away from home only when a Cora Max at the tank can reach the equipment. See What works away from home . Cora advises. You decide Check anything important with your own testing. Treat big changes the way you'd treat advice from anyone else, and sanity-check them before you act. The line under the message box says the same.

Two separate permissions, and the memory Cora keeps. The first time you open the dashboard, Cora asks Enable Personalized Reef Guidance? Enable turns on data sharing. Not Now leaves it off. If you use guided setup, its last page asks the same question. You can change it any time in Settings → Cora Assistant , which has two separate switches. Allow Cora Assistant to use saved tank data has to be on for Cora Assistant to answer you. If it's off, Cora shows its consent screen again before your next message or voice conversation. The screen lists what Cora Assistant uses, and Where your data goes names the AI provider that writes the replies. Agree & Continue turns the switch back on and carries on. Not now sends nothing and keeps what you typed. Contribute anonymized tank data is covered in Exporting your data and deleting your account .

Allow Cora Assistant to use saved tank data isn't only for chat. Every feature that sends your tank data to the AI needs it: Cora Assistant, typed or spoken, on your phone and on Cora Max ICP uploads and re-running an ICP analysis Lab results a lab or an email sends to you Health Reports Journal dictation and Analyze in the journal Design with AI for dashboards With it off, the feature asks for your OK first. Reef Buddy briefings still come, but with a plain fixed summary and no AI-written observation. On Cora Max, voice shows Voice needs your OK until you turn the switch on in Cora Mobile.

Cora Assistant uses your account language. That's the one language for the whole household, set in Settings → Language . Cora Assistant has no language setting of its own. Change it there, and from your next conversation Cora Assistant writes and speaks in the new language. More in Cora Mobile settings .

The chip above the message box, Using your tank's live data , shows what's in scope. Tap it to see what Cora is reading: current values and how old each one is, recent history, your journal and your ICP results. If your controller can't be reached, the chip says Live controller offline: using saved data . Cora then works from the last readings it has. Cora Assistant can look back over about six months of a parameter's history. So you can ask "Compare the last six months of my magnesium with my latest ICP." It tells you how old the data is Cora reports the age of the readings it uses. If your latest alkalinity reading is four days old, the answer says so and doesn't pass it off as current.

The two data switches, AI memory, Answering device and Share Cora's analysis with labs. Cora remembers things about your tank from one conversation to the next. For example, that you dose two-part, that your frag tank shares a sump, or that you're trying to bring nutrients up. You don't have to explain your system every time. Settings → Cora Assistant → AI memory shows what Cora has recorded about your tank and lets you reset it. Each tank has its own memory, so pick the tank first. The row only shows while Allow Cora Assistant to use saved tank data is on. What clearing memory touches Clearing removes what Cora has remembered about your conversations for one tank. That's its profile of your system, the concerns it was tracking, and every stored session. If any part of that can't be removed, Cora Mobile tells you it failed. Your tank data stays as it is. Clearing memory doesn't remove readings, journal entries, livestock, maintenance or reports. Your recent messages stay The reset doesn't delete the messages you've exchanged with Cora. For about half an hour afterwards, Cora can still see the last few of them when you carry on talking.

Your plan includes a monthly allowance of messages. The count sits above the message box. Voice conversations have their own monthly count, and each spoken reply also uses messages. When you run out, Cora shows You've hit your message limit with the plans you can move to. The numbers for each plan are in Plans and subscriptions .

Correct it in the conversation. That's the quickest fix and it usually sticks, though it may not last forever. If an answer sounds sure of itself but wrong, check the data chip first. Often the answer is right about the data Cora was given. The real problem is a stale reading, or a source assigned to the wrong tank. Rate an answer with the thumbs under it. A thumbs down asks What was wrong with it? Pick a reason, such as Wrong or Missed my tank , and tap Send rating . That's what helps us fix it.

docs.d: Make Cora act on its own when a reading, an alert, a time or a device goes offline, and group actions into scenes you run with one tap.
x: An automation is a rule Cora runs for you: when this happens, check that, then do this. A scene groups several actions into one thing you run when you want. Go to Settings → Automations . Automations and Scenes are separate tabs. Each rule has its own switch. The screen has two tabs, Automations and Scenes , with a New automation or New scene button. Each rule shows a one-line summary, an enable switch and a menu to Edit or Delete it. A rule that hasn't run yet says so. Rules act on real equipment If a rule switches a pump, the pump switches even when you aren't watching. Build one rule at a time and check it does what you expect before you add the next.

Every automation has three parts. The trigger wakes it up. The conditions must also be true. The actions are what it then does, in order. A new automation: triggers, If conditions, Then actions, Else-if and Else, then the cooldown and time window.

Add one or more triggers under When: any trigger . Any one of them starts the rule. Trigger Fires when When a metric changes A parameter crosses a value you set. Pick the Direction : Rising , Falling or Any change When an alert fires An alert is Raised , Cleared , or either. You can limit it to Threshold or Rate of change alerts. At a time of day A time of day, in your own timezone When a device goes offline Your Cora Max goes Offline , comes back Online , or either way Hear about it when your Cora Max drops off A rule with When a device goes offline and Notify Me tells you when the Cora Max that reads your equipment loses power or Wi-Fi.

Conditions decide whether the actions run. Tap Add condition and choose: Metric compare , a reading above, below or equal to a value Metric inside / outside a range Alert active Outlet is on / off , for an Apex outlet Time of day , a window such as 22:00 to 06:00 How an earlier step went , which checks whether an earlier step went OK or was Skipped . Use it for "try this, and if it didn't work, do that instead" With several conditions, set Match to All (AND) or Any (OR) .

An automation can do different things in different cases. Its first block is If . Tap Else-if to add another case, or add an Else block for everything else. Cora runs the first block whose conditions hold. You can also gate a single action. Tap Only if… on that step and give it its own condition. With no condition, the step always runs.

Cooldown between runs stops a rule firing again too soon. It starts at 10 min. Only run between limits the rule to a time window, for example daytime only. Test against live values checks the rule against your tank's readings right now, without doing anything. It tells you what would run , or why nothing would.

An action that needs equipment only shows up on a tank that has that equipment. Action What it does Control Apex Equipment Switch an outlet Run Apex Feed Cycle Start a feed. The Apex ends it on its own timer Run a Trident Test Start a test. Each run uses reagent Dose a DŌS Head Run a measured dose on a DŌS head Control a Red Sea Equipment Drive a ReefBeat unit Control a wavemaker Set a Jecod pump's flow, wave mode or power, or Pause for feeding . The Cora Max at the tank puts the pump back when the feed ends Notify Me Send yourself a push with your own Title and Message Wait Before Next Step Pause before carrying on Run a Scene Run a scene from inside this rule Manage an Automation Turn another rule on or off Create a Maintenance Task Put a job on the tank's maintenance list, for example change the CO2 scrubber media when pH drops below a value A dose can't be undone, and it's capped You can't take a dose back out of the tank. A rule can only dose from a head that has been measured with Measure to dose on a Cora Max. The dose runs on a Cora Max at the tank. Dosing from rules is capped at 10 mL per head per day , however the rule is written. What Create a Maintenance Task does Pick the tank, then Existing task (an existing task becomes due now) or New task (give it a Task name ). A new task is a one-off, due right away, and the rule doesn't raise it again while it's still open. You get one notification, and the one-off task leaves the list when you complete it. Wait is short Wait Before Next Step pauses for up to 60 seconds, and a branch can wait 60 seconds in total. After the pause, the next step sees fresh readings. For a longer hold, like a return pump off for 30 minutes during a water change, use a scene with Run for (below).

A scene is a named group of actions, like "Water change", "Photo mode" or "Night". Tap New automation or New scene and pick Scene at the top. A scene has no trigger. You run it with Run now in the list, from inside a rule with Run a Scene , or on a timetable through a rule with At a time of day . Run for sets how long a scene lasts: a number of minutes or hours, or Until I change it . When the time is up, Cora switches the scene's outlets back to how they were. Other equipment stays as the scene left it. While a timed scene is running, the list shows a countdown and a Stop button that ends it early. If a scene switches an outlet that matters, such as a heater, chiller, return pump or top-off, Cora asks before running it and lists those steps. You can turn this off with Ask before running on the scene. A scene can call another scene, up to 3 deep. Cora won't run a scene that calls itself, because it could loop and keep acting on the tank. After a scene runs, you see what happened step by step, including anything that failed or didn't run.

You can also build and edit scenes on a Cora Max. It's the same set of scenes, shared across the account. An older Cora Max can still run a scene made on the phone. Editing on the device is newer, though, so an older Cora Max may show a scene without letting you change it. Edit it from the phone instead.
Every rule has an enable switch. Turning a rule off keeps its settings, which helps when you want it back next season.
Every action a rule takes is recorded with Automation rule as its cause. You'll find it in Activity .

docs.d: How to connect a Neptune Apex, Red Sea ReefBeat, Jecod or AquaWiz unit to Cora.
x: This page shows how to connect each brand of equipment to Cora and what each connection needs. They all start the same way: Devices → Add Device , then pick the brand. The brand list. Brand Opens Without a Cora Max Cora A scan for a new Cora Max, over Wi-Fi or Bluetooth Neptune Apex A network scan or its IP address, then which tanks it serves Local only Red Sea A scan on your network, then which tank each unit belongs to Local only Jecod / Jebao A scan on your network, or Bluetooth Local only AquaWiz Your AquaWiz sign-in Works
Without a Cora Max: local only

Neptune Apex, Red Sea and Jecod equipment is on your home network (or Bluetooth). If you have no Cora Max (or none on the tank you're adding to), the add screen for these brands says This integration works only locally on the Mobile app without Cora Max. That means: Your phone reads and controls the equipment while Cora Mobile is open on the same network, or in Bluetooth range. Away from home you see the last readings your phone saved, and you can't control it. A Cora Max at the tank reads this equipment around the clock and passes on your commands when you're away. AquaWiz is reached through the maker's own service, so it works from anywhere without a Cora Max. More in More than one Cora device .

Cora reads your Apex over your local network, including probes, outlets and any expansion modules you've fitted. Go to Devices → Add Device → Neptune Apex . Tap Scan Network for APEX and pick your Apex, or type its address under Or enter IP manually: . Fill in Apex login (only if you set one on the Apex): . Leave the password blank if you haven't set one. Tap Load metrics from APEX and tick the ones you want under Metrics to track . Set Poll Frequency . Don't leave it off: with polling off, nothing reads the Apex and its readings go stale. Tap Continue , tick every tank under Which tanks does this Apex serve? , then tap Save . An Apex can serve more than one tank. If the scan finds nothing, check that your phone is on the same Wi-Fi as the Apex, or enter the IP address yourself. Once it's connected, every probe your Apex reports becomes a source you can put on a dashboard. Outlets show up as controls, and each fitted expansion module gets its own device tile. Your own Apex programming keeps running exactly as you set it up. What you can control is in Controlling your equipment .

Cora talks to ReefBeat equipment on your local network. It supports ReefDose , ReefATO+ , ReefMat and ReefRun . Set the unit up in Red Sea's ReefBeat app first, and check it's on the same network as your phone. Go to Devices → Add Device → Red Sea . Cora scans your network. Pick which tank each unit belongs to. A Red Sea unit serves one tank. Picking a different one moves it there. Each unit gets its own device page, and its readings become sources. ReefDose reports its heads and containers, ReefATO+ its reservoir and fills, ReefMat the days it has left, and ReefRun its pump state. What each page lets you do is in Controlling your equipment .

Cora connects to Jecod pumps and can read and control them. Add one from Devices → Add Device → Jecod . A Jecod pump reaches Cora in one of two ways, and that decides what you can do with it. None seen yet: the scan explains what it needs and why a pump can miss a sweep. Over your network. The scan finds pumps that announce themselves, so you don't have to type an address. You can read and drive a network pump whenever it's powered and reachable. That means your phone is on the same network, or a Cora Max on that network passes your commands on. If you're away from home and there's no Cora Max on site, you can see a network pump but you can't control it. A pump often misses the first scan Pumps answer one scan and miss the next. If yours isn't listed, scan again before you decide it can't be reached. If a search finds nothing, the result shows the addresses it checked over Wi-Fi. If the Jebao app shows a different address for your pump, your phone is on another network. A guest or IoT network, or a 5 GHz-only band, won't see these pumps. On iPhone, Cora also needs Local Network access to see pumps on your Wi-Fi. Without it the list stays empty and no error appears, so the result explains this and offers Open Settings to turn it back on. You can also get there any time from Settings → Device access , described in Settings . Over Bluetooth. Some pumps can only be reached from a phone standing near them. The pump's page says so, and shows the last settings it read and how old they are. Cora needs Bluetooth permission for this. Grant it before you add a Bluetooth pump, or Cora can't find the pump at all. You have to be near a Bluetooth pump Its page shows the last settings Cora read and how long ago. Changing anything, even starting a feeding pause, needs the pump in range. Stand near it and open the page again. With either connection you get live state, mode and intensity, a feeding pause and a day program. A feeding pause started from your phone needs the pump's page kept open on some pumps. The details are in Controlling your equipment , and Scheduling equipment covers the day program.

Cora reads alkalinity from an AquaWiz KH controller through your AquaWiz account, so it works away from home and doesn't need a Cora Max. Go to Devices → Add Device → AquaWiz . Enter your AquaWiz username and password and tap Connect . Pick the tank, turn on Also read its pH if you want it, and tap Link to Cora . With Stay connected automatically on, Cora keeps your AquaWiz password and renews the connection on its own. With it off, Cora keeps only a sign-in token, which AquaWiz expires about every 30 days, and sends you a notification when it's time to sign in again. You get alkalinity as a source, updated as often as your controller titrates, and pH too if you turned it on and your unit reports it. What the AquaWiz card shows, and its supplement alert, are in Controlling your equipment . Cora shares your AquaWiz sign-in AquaWiz gives each account one sign-in, so Cora uses the same one as the AquaWiz app. If you change your AquaWiz password, Cora disconnects. Reconnect it from the device row afterwards. To take away Cora's access completely, remove the device in Cora and change your AquaWiz password.

Some parameters come from a test kit, not from equipment. To enter a result, scroll to the bottom of the dashboard and tap Log Parameters . Readings you log by hand count as much as any other. They show on widgets with their own source and age, and they feed Reef Buddy. Cora also checks your probes against them when it tells you two sources disagree.
The device row tells you what kind of problem it is. Look it up in the table in Adding, editing and removing devices . For anything that doesn't cover, see Troubleshooting .

docs.d: Set refill alerts for reagent, dosing containers, top-off reservoirs and filter rolls, and tell Cora when you've refilled.
x: Use refill alerts so Cora warns you before reagent, dosing liquid, top-off water or filter roll runs out. Open the device from Devices (or tap its tile on the dashboard), then tap the bell in the top bar.

One threshold per head, each with its own switch. The sheet is called Alerts: followed by the device's name. If the equipment has more than one container, each one gets its own threshold and its own switch, so a head you watch closely and one you rarely touch can be set differently. Turning a switch off keeps the value for later. Where to set it: Most devices : the bell in the top bar of the device's page. DŌS : the Alerts card on the DŌS page, or the bell. See Doser alerts . AquaWiz : the rule on the Rules tab of the Alert Center . Most thresholds are in days, not volume. Cora works out how long what's left will last at the rate you're using it. "Four days of calcium left" is something you can act on. "180 mL left" isn't.
What you can be warned about

Device Threshold Starts at Trident Tests remaining (the lowest reagent) 10 tests Trident Waste bottle (a full bottle fails the next test) 85% full DŌS head [head] · days left 7 days DŌS head [head] · remaining , in mL 100 mL DŌS head that takes old water out Waste container space left DŌS head Missed dose alerts (a switch) ReefDose head Days of supplement left 7 days ReefATO+ Reservoir runway , estimated from recent top-off use 2 days ReefMat Roll remaining , estimated from how fast the roller advances 3 days AquaWiz Alkalinity supplement left 100 mL A consumable alert works like any other alert. It shows in the Alert Center and can push to your phone. You get one notification when a level is crossed, and it clears when the level is back above the threshold.

Set it early enough that you have time to act. If it fires the day something runs out, it's no warning at all. Some equipment keeps going when it's empty A DŌS head with an empty container keeps running its schedule and reports doses it never delivered. It has no low-level warning of its own. A refill alert is how you catch this, so set one for every head you dose from.

Tell Cora on the device's page, so the alert clears and the next warning is worked out from the right level. Device Tap DŌS head Fill , then Full , or set Volume Remaining DŌS waste container Reset its free space to full after you empty it ReefDose head Remaining in bottle ReefMat New roll after you load a new roll Trident, ReefATO+ and AquaWiz report their own levels, so there's nothing to reset in Cora.

docs.d: Add, move, resize and remove widgets on your phone dashboard, set the column count, and edit a Cora Max dashboard from your phone.
x: The dashboard editor sets which widgets appear on a tank's dashboard and how they're arranged. Each tank has its own layout, and it follows your account to any phone you sign in on.

Scroll down the dashboard and tap Edit dashboard , just under the widgets. The editor opens as Edit Dashboard , with the hint Long-press a tile to move it. Tap to configure. The pencil in the tank header opens something else It opens Edit tank , the tank profile with volume, livestock, dosing, lighting and flow. That's covered in Your tank profile . Columns at the top, then each tile with its name and type. Tap a red cross to remove it.

Pick 2 , 3 or 4 next to COLUMNS at the top of the editor. The grid grows downward as you add widgets, and the dashboard scrolls. Columns Use when 2 You watch a few parameters and want big tiles 3 The default. Works for most tanks 4 You want a dense view, or you have a big phone

Tap Add tile under the grid, or tap an empty cell. In Add a tile , pick what kind it is. Metric covers a value, gauge, graph or status for a parameter. Outlet controls an Apex outlet. The other rows are for equipment, such as ReefBeat , Trident , DŌS or Jecod . Most of them only appear when the tank has that equipment. Pick the parameter, outlet or device. For a metric, pick the type. The Widget reference describes each one. You only see parameters the tank has. A parameter with no source shows up once you connect equipment that reports it, or log a reading by hand. The grid holds up to 20 rows. When it's full, Cora says Dashboard is full: remove a tile first. A graph needs two free cells side by side.

To move a widget, press and hold it, then drag. The others move around it. To remove a widget, tap the red cross in its corner, or tap the widget and then Remove . To change a widget's settings, tap it.

Tap a widget in the editor to open its settings. Depending on the widget, you can set: Setting Applies to Type Metric widgets: Value, Gauge, Graph or Status Parameter Metric widgets: which parameter it shows The outlet or device Outlet and equipment tiles: which one it shows Show remaining as Doser tiles: Days or Milliliters (mL) Width Every widget: 1× or 2× . A graph is always at least 2 wide Height Every widget: 1× or 2× Time range Graph: 1h, 6h, 24h, 7d, 30d or 1y Tap Done to keep the settings, or Remove to take the widget off. A widget has no label, source or range of its own. Its alert range comes from the tank's alert thresholds: long-press the widget on the dashboard, or see Alerts and thresholds . Which source a parameter follows is set per tank in Parameter Mapping .

Tap Save to keep the layout. To throw your changes away, tap the close icon. If you changed anything, Cora asks Discard changes? Tap Discard , or Keep editing to go back. The phone editor has no undo and no saved designs. Readings, history and journal entries are stored apart from the layout, so editing a dashboard can never lose them.

You edit the Cora Max dashboard separately, from Devices → your Cora Max → Dashboard layout , on the tank's card. It uses a fixed grid that doesn't scroll, and nothing reaches Cora Max until you tap Save & Publish . That editor has three extras the phone dashboard doesn't: My dashboards keeps up to 30 saved designs on your account. Any Cora Max on the account can load one. Tiles the target can't fill are listed under Left behind: before you load. Templates opens Dashboard templates : Overview , Equipment and Parameters . It's open on every plan and doesn't use AI. Design with AI , on a paid plan or during the trial, proposes a whole layout from what the tank reports and has linked. You can make 5 designs per tank per day. How each one works is in Editing the Cora Max dashboard .

docs.d: How to read Cora's dashboard, from widgets, reading age and sources to what the colours mean and the cards that come and go.
x: The dashboard is a grid of widgets for one tank. Each widget shows one thing. You decide what goes on it, as described in Editing your dashboard . The tank header and the Reef Buddy card, then gauges, values, graphs and device tiles.

Every dashboard starts with: The tank name, with a small glyph next to it. Tap the name to rename the tank. That's all it does. Feed , only on a tank with a Neptune Apex. It opens Feed mode with your Apex's Feed A to Feed D cycles. Your Apex decides what pauses and when it comes back, as you set it up there. While a cycle runs, the button shows which one, for example Feed A . Tap it and choose Cancel feed to end it early. Away from home, a Cora Max on the tank sends the command for you. The newspaper icon, which opens the latest Reef Buddy briefing. The share icon, which makes a snapshot of the tank. See Sharing your tank . The ruler, which opens Units for this tank. See Your tank profile . The pencil on the right, which opens the tank profile . Three controls that look alike The tank name renames the tank. The pencil on the right opens the tank profile . To edit the dashboard itself, tap Edit dashboard just under the widgets. If you have more than one tank, swipe sideways to move between them. See Managing your tanks .

Above the widgets, a card sums up the latest briefing. It shows the headline, a score out of 100 once Cora has enough data, the date it's from, and how many insights and drifting readings there are. Tap it to open the full briefing, or close it with × . A new card appears with the next briefing. More in Reef Buddy .
How to read a parameter widget

A widget for a measured parameter always shows the same three things in the same places. Device and control tiles, like an outlet, a dosing unit or a pump, show their own state instead, since there's no single reading behind them. The value is the reading itself, large and in the middle. The age sits below or next to it, as now , 1h or 2d . It's how long ago the source last confirmed that value, not when the screen last refreshed. For a probe, that's when its device last checked in, so a steady reading from a working probe stays fresh even when the number doesn't change. For a test-kit or ICP result, it's when you took the test. An age that keeps growing on a probe means its device has stopped reporting. The source badge is the small mark next to the age. It shows where the number came from: a probe, a controller, a lab result, or you with a test kit. Tap the widget to see the source written out, with its recent history. Why the age matters A perfect alkalinity reading from four days ago isn't your alkalinity today. Every value shows its age so you can see the difference quickly.

Cora doesn't use much colour, and each colour always means the same thing: Colour Meaning Green Comfortably inside the range for this parameter Amber Near an edge. Usually still inside the range , in the last tenth of it Red Past the edge, and worth acting on Grey No verdict. There's no recent reading, or no usable range to judge it by Amber usually means "fine for now, but drifting" Amber is a margin. A reading inside its range but in the last 10% of it turns amber, so you see drift while there's still time to act. There are two refinements. A range you set yourself is a hard line. Cross it and the widget goes straight to red, with no amber margin. A range Cora supplied is softer. Crossing it shows amber for the first 10% past the edge, then red beyond that. A one-sided limit , such as a ceiling for a contaminant or a floor for a nutrient, is graded on its high edge only. So copper at zero shows green and doesn't turn amber for sitting near the bottom of the scale. A widget outlined in amber or red needs attention. The whole widget gets the outline, so you'll spot it while scrolling. To change a range, long-press the widget. More in Alerts and thresholds .

Some cards only show when there's something to say. Most of them sit between the header and the widgets. Card When it shows What to tap Starting a new tank? On a tank with no readings at all. Once you've started, it becomes Continue cycling The card, to start guided cycling. See Guided journeys Tank parameters with No readings yet The tank has no readings yet Configure tank Couldn't reach your readings: showing what's cached. Cora can't load the latest readings, often with no connection Retry Lab result from {lab} is waiting. A lab sent a result and Cora needs to know which tank it's for Choose tank . See ICP and health reports Profile prompt ( Unlock smarter insights ) The tank profile is under 80% complete The card, to carry on with the profile Cora Pro trial: 9 days left The last days of your trial The card, or Keep Pro . See Plans and subscriptions Reef Buddy A briefing is ready The card How do you usually feed? You haven't set a feeding routine Set up routine Red Sea readings have stopped updating. Nothing is reading this tank's Red Sea devices See Alerts and thresholds Log your first water test No readings and no linked equipment, under the widgets The card. See Setting up Cora Mobile

Edit dashboard, the Log Parameters, Parameter History and Feeding buttons, and shortcuts to the four record areas. From top to bottom you'll find: A line saying when the dashboard last updated and which sources it used, with Edit dashboard beside it. That opens the dashboard editor . The Log your first water test card, on a tank with no readings and no linked equipment. Log Parameters , for entering test-kit readings by hand. Parameter History , to open the history of any parameter that has data, even one with no widget. See Looking into a parameter . Feeding , to log a feeding that differs from your routine. See The journal . Journal · Alerts · Maintenance · Livestock , shortcuts to those areas for this tank.

Tap any parameter widget to open its detail. You'll see the full history as a chart, every source that has reported it and your alert band. From there you can compare sources, exclude a bad reading or record probe care. See Looking into a parameter . Long-press a parameter widget to set its alert range straight from the dashboard.
If a widget has no value

A widget shows a value once it gets one. If it's blank, it's usually one of these: The device is offline. Check the Devices tab. The parameter has no source yet. Log it by hand, or connect equipment that reports it. Nothing has ever been reported or logged for the parameter. An old reading doesn't disappear just because it's older than the chart window. It stays on the widget with its age, so a stale value looks stale and doesn't look missing. For anything else, see Troubleshooting .

docs.t: Exporting your data and deleting your account
docs.d: Export your readings, journal and alerts as spreadsheet files, sign out, or delete your Cora account and what that removes.
x: Your tank records belong to you. This page shows how to export them, and how to delete your account if you want to. Settings, then your account: Export My Data and Delete Account sit below Sign Out.

Open Settings and tap the account card at the top. Account & Subscription opens. Tap Export My Data . Exporting is free on every plan , including the free one. Cora exports CSV files . They're spreadsheets that open in Excel, Numbers, Google Sheets or anything else that reads a table. File Contains cora_parameters.csv Your readings, each with its source and timestamp cora_journal.csv Your journal entries cora_alerts.csv Alerts raised cora_export_summary.csv What this export covers, including anything that was cut short What's in the export It covers readings, journal entries and alerts , the three records people ask for. It isn't a copy of your whole account. Dashboards, livestock, maintenance, automations, reports and device settings aren't included. Each of the three stops at 25,000 rows per tank . A tank logging thirty metrics every five minutes writes more than that in three days, so a long-running tank will hit the cap. The summary file tells you when that's happened. Check it before you assume the export is complete. The parameter export includes the source of each reading. So in a spreadsheet of your alkalinity, you can still tell what your probe said from what your test kit said. Export before big changes Take an export before you shut down a tank or make big changes to your setup. The files don't depend on Cora Mobile or your account.
Sign Out disconnects this phone from your account. Your data isn't touched, and signing back in brings everything back. Delete Account is permanent.

Deleting doesn't cancel your subscription An App Store or Google Play subscription belongs to the store . Deleting your account removes your record with Cora, but the billing doesn't stop . You'll keep being charged until you cancel with Apple or Google yourself. Cancel there first, then delete. See Cancelling . If you want to keep anything, export it first. Open Settings , tap the account card, then Delete Account . Read the confirmation. If you have a store subscription, it has a Manage subscription button so you can cancel first. Tap Delete . This removes your account, tanks, readings, journal, lab results and device links. You can't undo it, and there's no grace period. If you signed in a while ago, Cora may ask you to prove it's you before it deletes anything. With an email and password, it asks you to Confirm your password . With Apple or Google, sign in with them again. Then try again. Until you do, nothing is deleted.

Settings → Cora Assistant → Contribute anonymized tank data. While this is on, your tank's parameter history is kept for reef research with no link to you . That happens when you remove a tank, and when you delete your account. Turn it off and that history is deleted with everything else. This is a separate choice from deleting your account. It's the only part of your data that outlives the account, so give it some thought. It's on by default . If you delete your account without checking this switch, the de-identified copy stays behind.

The privacy policy has the full detail. Briefly, Cora stores your tank data, your account, and the sign-ins for any equipment you connected through a manufacturer's account. Removing a device forgets its sign-in. Deleting your account removes everything held under your name, with these exceptions: the anonymised research copy, if you left that switch on your store subscription, which only the store can cancel your customer record at our subscription management provider, which is deleted 120 days after your account so a store refund or payment dispute can still be handled Signing in again on another phone, or changing your sign-in, is covered in Signing in and account recovery . Plans and billing are in Plans and subscriptions .

docs.d: Open a device's page to see its live state and switch outlets, pumps, dosing heads and testers, brand by brand.
x: Use a device's own page to see its live state and change what it's doing. Open it from Devices → tap the device, or tap its tile on the dashboard. Status, today's readings and the water level, then leak, fills and probe calibration. Every device page is laid out the same way. The name and details are at the top, then a row of live readings, any state the device reports, and its controls. The bell in the title bar sets alert thresholds for that device, as described in Consumables . How to add a device in the first place is in Connecting your equipment . Jump to your equipment: Neptune Apex · Trident · DŌS · Red Sea · ReefDose · ReefRun · ReefMat · ReefATO+ · Doser alerts · Jecod · AquaWiz These controls act on live equipment There's no preview and no undo. Some controls ask you to confirm first.
What happens when you send a command

A command doesn't always go through. Cora tells you which of four things happened: Outcome Means Confirmed The equipment accepted the change and reported its new state Unconfirmed The command went out, but nothing reported back. It means "we don't know". It doesn't mean it worked. Check the device's own state Refused Something turned it down (a safety rule, a lock or the equipment itself), or no Cora device picked it up in time. It was cancelled and nothing ran No change The equipment was already set the way you asked Every outcome is recorded in Activity , along with what caused it. Without a Cora Max at the tank, Neptune Apex, Red Sea and Jecod equipment only works locally: your phone has to be on the same network (or in Bluetooth range) to send a command. With a Cora Max at the tank, Cora Mobile sends it through that Cora Max, even when you're away from home.

The Apex page: Status, Modules, Parameter Mapping and Tanks. The Apex page shows the controller's status, then Modules , Parameter Mapping and Tanks . Modules lists each fitted Trident and DŌS. Tap one to open its own page. Parameter Mapping is where you choose what each probe feeds. Probes report into Cora as sources, and you can put them on a dashboard. See Parameter Mapping and probes . Tanks shows which tanks the Apex serves. Tap Change to edit them. Outlets switch between Auto , Off and On from an Outlet widget on the dashboard. Auto hands control back to your Apex programming. See Widget reference . Your Apex keeps running its own programming. Cora only changes an outlet when you ask.

The Trident page shows the current test state and the reagent and waste-water levels. You can start a test from here. You can also set an alert for remaining tests and for the waste bottle, so Cora warns you before the reagent runs out or the bottle fills. See Consumables .

A DŌS that is off the AquaBus: the page shows its last known figures, a Needs attention card and the Alerts row. A DŌS QD works exactly like a DŌS, and everything here applies to both. When a Cora Max reads your Apex, dosing heads show up on the DŌS page. They never appear in the outlet list. Each dosing head shows what it's dosing, its schedule, what it has dosed today and how much is left in the container. It also shows the runway , which is how many days that will last at the current rate. If the DŌS stops answering on the AquaBus, its page shows Off the bus and a Needs attention card. The figures on the page are then the last it reported, not what it's doing now. Check the module's AquaBus cable and the Apex. For each head you can: Pause and Resume its schedule Fill , to tell Cora the container is full again or set how much is in it ( Total Volume is the container's size, Volume Remaining is what's in it now, and Full sets one to the other) Dose now , for a measured dose by hand Edit schedules in Apex Fusion Cora shows the schedule and tracks what's been dosed, but it doesn't change the schedule. You edit the schedule, dose rate and number of doses in the Apex Fusion app. Pausing, filling and dosing by hand all work here. Measure a head before you dose by hand Cora won't dose a head by hand until the head has been measured. Measure to dose and Re-measure are on the Cora Max that doses for the tank. Cora runs the head for twenty seconds, you measure what came out, and Cora works out the head's real rate. One measurement works for every Cora Max and Cora Mobile. Measure each head once, and again after you change its tubing. A DŌS keeps dosing when its container is empty The unit has no level sensor and won't stop on its own. Set a refill alert for each head under Alerts on the DŌS page, so Cora warns you before the container runs dry. See Doser alerts .
What each head is used for

Give each head a use type so Cora knows what it does and talks about it correctly. The choices are Supplement , Water change: new saltwater in , Water change: old water out , Kalkwasser , Calcium reactor , Food , Top-off and Other . Set it under Used for in the head's settings. The two water-change use types go in pairs . Set one head's Paired head to the head that moves water the other way, and Cora treats the two as one water-change pair. A container can be up to 1,000 L, for every use type. The Apex itself only counts up to 150 L, so above that Cora tracks the container itself from what the head doses. Enter the Total Volume when you set it up. Cora also resets the Apex's own counter now and then, and Activity shows that as Reset the Apex's own counter to 150 L . Each head also has a Largest dose by hand limit, so a typo can't turn a manual dose into something far bigger than you meant. Large hand doses only become available after the head's rate has been measured against a real test at the tank, and after you turn on Large doses in the head's settings. It's off by default. Turn it on only after you've watched the first large dose run at the tank.
