Each Red Sea unit has a page that fits what it does: Unit Page shows You can ReefDose Each head, its container and what it has dosed Dose, change the daily dose, edit the Dosing plan ReefRun Return and skimmer pump speed and state Change speed, switch a pump ReefMat Remaining roll, in days and metres Advance the mat, set ReefMat settings , register a new roll ReefATO+ Reservoir level and top-off activity Set a reservoir alert When you're away from the unit's network, Cora Mobile sends Red Sea commands through a Cora Max on the tank. If no Cora Max can do it, the page says so and nothing is sent.

Status, heads and today's total, Use doser for consumption, then each dosing head. For each head you can set Dose per day and Remaining in bottle , run Dose now , and Activate schedule . Refill alerts are set per head with the bell, as described in Doser alerts . The Dosing section shows Upcoming doses , what each head has dosed today ( Dosed today so far ), and Dosed per head for the Last 7 days or its Lifetime . Cora reads this while a Cora Max or your phone is on your home network.

Tap the calendar icon on a ReefDose page to open the Dosing plan . A plan is a daily total, split into up to four time windows. Each window has a start and end time, how many doses it should deliver, and a speed: Whisper , Regular or Quick . Add and remove windows, then save. Cora shows you what you're about to send and asks you to confirm before it replaces the head's whole plan. The editor reads the plan that's already on the unit first, so you're editing the real one, not a blank form.
ReefRun controls return and skimmer pumps. It isn't a wave pump. You can change a pump's speed, switch it on or off, and adjust skimmer settings.

The ReefMat page shows how much roll is left, in days and metres. Tap Advance now to move the mat on by hand. Cora asks Advance the mat now? first. You can also set a refill alert for the roll. Tap the gear for ReefMat settings : Scheduled advance turns on a fixed-time advance, separate from the auto-advance sensor already on the page. Turn it on and set how often, and how far each advance moves the mat. ReefMat model and Motor position ( Left or Right ) tell Cora which unit and orientation you have. After you load a new roll, tell Cora with New roll : its thickness, and its outer diameter if you know it. Advance now only moves the mat you already have loaded.

The ReefATO+ page shows the reservoir level and recent top-offs. Set a reservoir alert with the bell. Cora estimates how many days the reservoir has left from recent top-off use, and you can ask the Assistant about it too.
When a Red Sea unit stops itself

A unit can stop itself. A ReefRun pump does this when the skimmer cup fills, for example. When that happens, the page says why and offers the fix: Unit The page says Tap ReefRun Which pump stopped and why, for example Full cup. Empty it, then resume. Resume ReefRun or ReefMat Emergency stop Clear emergency ReefMat Mat jammed , Installation error or Setup error Resume ReefMat Load a new roll, then confirm it in Red Sea's app. I already loaded a new roll ReefMat Sensor needs cleaning Sensor cleaned ReefDose Head malfunction , with the head's name Reset ReefATO+ Clear Fault Resume Some of these ask you to confirm first. Away from the unit's network they go through a Cora Max on the tank, as described in Red Sea ReefBeat .

A DŌS and a ReefDose keep their alerts on their own page. The Rules tab of the Alert Center has one row per doser that opens it, and a doser alert's Open doser button brings you here too. On a DŌS page, tap the Alerts card (or the bell in the title bar). The sheet lists every head, and for each one you can set: [head] · days left , for example Iodine · days left : you get an alert below this many days of supply [head] · remaining : you get an alert below this much left in the container Waste container space left , for a head that takes old water out: you get an alert when the waste container is getting full Missed dose alerts : a switch that tells you when the head misses a scheduled dose Each threshold has its own switch, so you can turn one off and keep its value. Tap Save when you're done. On a ReefDose page, tap the bell in the title bar. Each head has its own days-left threshold and switch. Defaults and other consumables are in Consumables .

The pump page shows the current wave pattern (mode) and intensity, and you can change both. Its status sits in the title row, next to the pump's name. A switch with Same all day and Schedule marks the one that is running with · running , and the page opens on it. Building a day program, and copying, saving or sharing it, is in Scheduling equipment . If the pump is part of a group, the page shows its role, such as Leads the group , Follows: in step or Follows: alternating .

Start a feeding pause from Feeding on the pump's page: tap 5 , 10 , 15 or 30 min. Some pumps end the pause by themselves, and the page says The pump ends this itself. Keep the pump's page open during a feeding pause Some pumps don't end a feed by themselves, and the page says so. For those, and for any pump on a schedule, Cora Mobile brings the wave pattern and the schedule back only while the pump's page stays open. If you leave the page, the pump stays stopped in feed mode, or stays off its schedule, until you change it again or tap Schedule . A Bluetooth pump has to be in range of your phone to start a feed, and a network pump has to be on your network.

Fault checks sets how often Cora re-reads the pump so it can warn you about a fault, such as a jammed pump or one running dry. If you set it to off, those warnings stop for that pump. Fault checks need a Cora Max on the tank. Your choice is saved and the checks start once one is added. Use this for every pump on this tank copies the setting to all of them.

The AquaWiz card shows your alkalinity readings, and pH if your unit reports it. It also shows your target KH, your dose strength and, for a unit with dosing set up, its maximum dose per hour and how much alkalinity supplement is left in the container. These come straight from your AquaWiz settings, so change them in the AquaWiz app. Cora can't control an AquaWiz. If your unit tracks its container, Cora warns you when the supplement is running low, at 100 mL by default. Change it from its rule in the Alert Center .
What happens after you change something
Every change is recorded in Activity , with the surface it came from. If a device doesn't accept a change, that's recorded there too.

docs.d: Add equipment to Cora, assign it to a tank, rename it, check it's healthy and remove it, all from the Devices tab.
x: The Devices tab is where you add, assign, rename, check and remove every piece of equipment. Devices are grouped by brand, and you can collapse each group. Equipment is grouped by brand. Each group collapses.

On the Devices tab, tap Add Device . Pick the brand: Cora , Neptune Apex , Red Sea , Jecod or AquaWiz . Follow the brand's steps. Depending on the brand that's a network scan, an IP address, a sign-in or a device key. Connecting your equipment has the steps for each brand. Choose the tank it belongs to. Pick the brand of the equipment you are adding. Without a Cora Max, some equipment is local only Neptune Apex, Red Sea and Jecod equipment is reached over your home network or Bluetooth. Without a Cora Max, the add screen says This integration works only locally on the Mobile app without Cora Max. Your phone reads and controls it only while it's on the same network (or in Bluetooth range). Away from home you see the last readings your phone saved and can't control it. A Cora Max at the tank reads it around the clock and passes your commands on. More in Connecting your equipment . When you add equipment from your network, your phone has to be on the same network as the equipment.

A Cora Max shares its Bluetooth between all the equipment it reads, so it can only keep up with so much. When you add a Jecod pump that connects over Bluetooth, Cora checks how busy the tank's Cora Max is first. Usually you see nothing. Otherwise one of two messages appears: Bluetooth is getting busy : This Cora Max is close to its Bluetooth limit. More devices may update less often. Add a second Cora Max if you plan to add more. Tap Continue to add the device anyway, or Cancel . Bluetooth limit reached : This Cora Max is at its Bluetooth limit. Add a second Cora Max for these devices. The device isn't added. Tap OK . Cora checks the tank's primary Cora Max or, if none is chosen, the Cora Max with the most room. More in More than one Cora device .

Add Device, then Cora. Cora Mobile looks on your Wi-Fi and over Bluetooth, with Enter IP Address Manually below. Cora is how you pair a new Cora Max. It finds units already on your Wi-Fi, or nearby ones over Bluetooth. If it can't find yours, use Enter IP Address Manually on the same screen. The full walk-through is in Setting up Cora Max .

Tap any device in the list to open its page. Its controls come first, then sections that work the same way for every brand. Status shows the Model , Serial , Firmware and when Cora last heard from it ( Last seen ). Tanks shows which tank (or tanks) it's assigned to. Tap Change to reassign it. Connection is where you edit its IP address, sign-in or device key. Remove device , at the bottom. Cora Max and Neptune Apex can serve more than one tank, so their tank picker is a checklist. Cora Max can be assigned up to four. See More than one Cora device . Everything else serves one tank at a time. Picking a different one moves the device there and takes it off the old one. Assign the tank before you rely on the readings A device without a tank still reports, but its numbers have nowhere to go. If a device you just added isn't showing on a dashboard, check this first. What each brand's controls do is in Controlling your equipment .

Open the device and tap the pencil beside its name. Use what you call it day to day, like "Return", "Left gyre" or "Sump heater". The name shows up on widgets, in alerts and in anything you ask Cora. Names can be up to 40 characters. Leave the name empty to go back to the device's own name. If two devices of the same kind have no name, Cora tells them apart with a short code after the name. Cora never uses a serial number as a name. The new name only applies in Cora. It doesn't change the name in the manufacturer's own app.
Checking whether a device is healthy

Each device is one row on the Devices tab, with its icon, name, model and tank. The dot on the row shows its state. Dot What it means Grey Cora doesn't know yet Green Working normally Orange A warning or a fault Red Offline For more, open the device. Its Status section shows when Cora last heard from it. You want a recent time and no warning. What you see What it means A recent update time Working normally "Updated 3 h ago" on something that only reports every few hours Fine "Could not reach…" A network problem, or the device is off "…refused the sign-in" The manufacturer's account needs reconnecting. Open the device and sign in again Older readings while you're away Normal for Apex, Red Sea and Jecod without a Cora Max at the tank (see above) Nothing at all It's never reported. Check the tank assignment and the connection When a device stops reporting, Cora can alert you. The timings are in Alerts and thresholds . For anything else, see Troubleshooting .

Open the device and tap Remove device , or swipe its row to the left on the Devices tab. Cora asks you to confirm: "{name} will be removed from Cora. It is not reset or changed on the device itself." Your readings are kept. Removing a device stops Cora collecting new data from it. The history it already gathered stays on the tank, and any widget that used it keeps its past readings. You lose the live link. If the device connected through a manufacturer account, you also lose the saved sign-in, so you'll need to sign in again if you add it back. Quieten a noisy device without removing it If a device works fine but alerts too often, change its thresholds or notification settings in Alerts and thresholds . You keep the connection and the data, and the noise stops.

docs.t: Dosing products and the dose calculator
docs.d: Check the strength of your alkalinity, calcium and magnesium products, add your own, and use the dose calculator to work out how much to add.
x: Cora can only do dosing maths if it knows how strong your products are. This page covers the product list and the dose calculator that uses it. Go to Settings → Dosing Products . Products carry the strength Cora uses for dose and consumption calculations.

The Dosing products screen already lists common products, grouped under Alkalinity (dKH) , Calcium (ppm) and Magnesium (ppm) . Find yours and tap it to check its strength. Each strength is how much 1 ml (or 1 g of a dry product) raises the parameter in a set volume of water. That's the number that turns "5 ml" into "+0.2 dKH in your tank". Switch between per 100 L and per 100 gal at the top. Only change a built-in strength if your bottle says something different. Tap the product to open Adjust strength . Reset to default puts Cora's figure back.

If your product isn't listed, tap + ( Add custom product ). Give it a Product name , choose Liquid (ml) or Dry (g) , and fill in its strength for alkalinity, calcium or magnesium. Leave a field blank if the product doesn't move it. A two-part fills in one each, a balanced product several. The strength is almost always on the label, something like "1 ml per 100 litres raises alkalinity by 0.1 dKH". Use the strength the manufacturer gives If the strength is wrong, every dose Cora works out for that product is wrong by the same proportion. If you can't find the figure, leave the product out. Don't guess. Nitrate and phosphate products come from Cora's own list in the calculator. You can't add them here. Your tank's salt mix isn't a dosing product. You set it on the tank's profile, and Cora has a catalog of common reef salts with their published figures, with sources, to choose from. See Your tank profile .

The calculator works out how much product it takes to bring a parameter up to its target. It's there for alkalinity, calcium, magnesium, nitrate and phosphate. On the dashboard, tap the parameter's widget to open it. Tap the calculator icon at the top. A dot on it means the reading is below target. Check the numbers Cora filled in: Current is your latest reading. Update it if you've just tested. Target is the middle of your alert range for that parameter, or the typical reef range if you haven't set one. Net water volume (L) is 90% of your tank's volume, to allow for rock and sand. Change it if you know the real figure. Pick the Product . Your own products from the tank profile come first, then brand presets. You can also enter a Custom strength . Cora shows the total needed to reach the target. Spread a big correction out The calculator gives the total, not a daily dose. If the total is a bigger jump than is safe in a day, it says so, and you split it over several days. Ask Cora opens Cora Assistant with your numbers, if you want help planning how much per day. When you've dosed, tap Log the dose you gave . It adds an entry to your journal . If you're already at or above the target, the calculator tells you there's nothing to add. You can't dose a parameter down. The answer is a water change, a media change, or changing what you already dose. The volume matters here. If it's 20% out, the doses are 20% out too.

Once Cora can see both your doses and your readings, it can work out what your tank is using and tell you when that changes. When demand changes, take a closer look before drawing a conclusion. Rising alkalinity demand often means growth, but a sudden move in either direction can also come from a missed dose, a testing error, precipitation, a water change or an equipment change. Check what else changed around that date.

If you have a connected doser, such as a Neptune DŌS or a Red Sea ReefDose, its heads show up with their own readings, including what each head has left and what it's been dosing. How to run and refill them is in Controlling your equipment , and their low-container and missed-dose alerts are in Doser alerts . An automation can also dose from a DŌS head, capped at 10 mL per head per day. See Automations and scenes .

docs.d: Upload an ICP test PDF or have your lab send it, read the score, track each element over time, and run a Health Report of your whole system.
x: The Intelligence tab is where your lab results and long-term reports live. Pick a tank at the top first. Everything on the screen belongs to that tank. Upload ICP, run a health report, and see what moved since the last one.

Cora reads the PDF report your lab sends you. Download it from your lab's email or website first. Photos, scans and screenshots can't be read. Tap Upload ICP . Pick your lab, or leave it on Auto: detect the lab . Cora has tips for ATI, Fauna Marin, Modern Reef, Oceamo, Reef Zlements and Triton. Say what the sample is: Aquarium water , RO/DI water , Salt mix or Other . Only aquarium water updates your dashboard and alerts. Check the date the sample was taken. Labs print the date they analysed it, so Cora asks for yours and charts the results against it. Tap Choose PDF and pick the file. It usually takes one to two minutes. Keep the screen open and the report opens as soon as it's ready. You don't have to type anything. You can also email the PDF to icp@in.coraiq.tech . Send it from your sign-in email or a verified lab email (see below), and it arrives like a result from a lab. If you upload the same report twice, Cora shows you the one you already have and doesn't charge you again. Cora needs your OK first ICP analysis sends the report to the AI, so it needs Allow Cora Assistant to use saved tank data . If that's off, Cora asks before the upload. See what the switch covers .
Which email a lab can use

A lab or an emailed result finds your account by the email address it knows. That is your sign-in email, plus any lab email you add under Settings → your account card (Account & Subscription) → Lab & ICP emails . Tap Add lab email and type the address your lab uses. Tap Send code . Cora sends a 6-digit code to that address. It expires in 10 minutes. Enter the code and tap Verify . If you didn't get it, tap Resend code . You can add up to 3 lab emails. Each shows Verified or Waiting for code , and Remove takes one off. After that, results sent to it no longer reach your account. An address that already belongs to another Cora account can't be added. If you signed in with a hidden Apple email, labs can't find your account. The ICP screen shows a card, Get lab results automatically , that takes you to this setting. When you sign in with Apple, choose Share My Email to avoid the problem.
Send to Cora: results a lab or an email delivers for you

Some labs can send a result straight to Cora, and an ICP PDF you email in arrives the same way. You don't have to upload anything yourself. If you have one tank, a result from a lab you trust, or one you emailed in, goes straight to that tank. With more than one tank, you'll see a banner: "Lab result from {lab} is waiting." Tap Choose tank and pick the tank it belongs to. Cora can't work that out on its own. The report shows Sent by {lab} near the top, or Received by email , so you can tell it from one you uploaded. If Allow Cora Assistant to use saved tank data is off, the result waits with the message Cora Assistant needs your OK to read it. Give your OK and it comes in. The first time The first time a result arrives this way, Cora shows a short hint about what's going on, so it doesn't look like an error.
The first result from a new lab

The first time a lab sends you a result, Cora asks you to approve it before adding it anywhere, even if you only have one tank. You'll see who sent it and can tick Trust this lab to skip this check next time a result comes from them. Tap Approve to bring it in, or Decline to delete it without adding it to any tank.
Trusted labs and what labs can see

Settings → Cora Assistant → Trusted labs lists every lab you've trusted. The list shows up once you've trusted at least one. Revoke removes a lab, so its next result needs your approval again. Share Cora's analysis with labs , on the same screen, decides what a lab sees after it sends you a result. On, it can see Cora's scores and written analysis. Off, it only sees that the result was delivered. It's off until you turn it on. The same switch also shows on a report a lab sent you. If something here doesn't work, see Troubleshooting .

Each report carries a score and a summary written for your tank. You get a score out of 100 and a plain-language summary of what it means for your system, taking in your tank type, its age and your livestock. The score compares your results with their target ranges, including any ranges you've set yourself. If any result is outside its range, the score can't go above 70, so it can't read Healthy . If one is far outside, it can't go above 40, however good the rest are. The label under the score reads Healthy from 71 to 100, Needs Attention from 40 to 70 and Critical from 0 to 39. Health Reports are scored the same way. Every element is tracked, including trace elements and contaminants as well as the main parameters. Cora records all 71 elements a lab can report, and the line some labs call Acidity is pH. On each element row you'll see the range the lab printed, shown as Lab range , next to Cora's own range for that element. An element Cora has no reference range for carries the tag No Cora range . The report says how many elements have a Cora range and assesses the rest from general reef knowledge. Cora Assistant comments on every element that was tested, and its comment stands even when there's no Cora range. If the lab prints n.d. , or not detected , for an element, Cora records it as 0 and says it wasn't detected. Dissolved CO2 is not room CO2 Dissolved CO₂ in an ICP report is the CO2 in the water, in mg/L. It is a different reading from the CO2 of the air in your room. The two have different ranges and are never mixed. The Since your last ICP card shows what changed most since last time. It's usually the quickest way into a new report. Tap Trends to see any element across every test you've uploaded. This is where ICP becomes really useful. The second test is where it gets interesting One ICP tells you where you are. The second tells you which way you're heading, and that's what you can act on. Test on a regular rhythm, and don't wait for something to go wrong.

If you upload RO/DI or other source water, pick RO/DI water when you upload. Cora doesn't score it against your tank's targets. It gives a plain verdict on whether the water is clean enough to use, and it keeps those numbers out of your tank readings. It's saved as a separate report. Cora does the same for Salt mix or Other : it says what the sample looks like and doesn't score it as your tank.

A Health Report is a deeper check of the whole system, done from time to time. It looks at every parameter, every source, your dosing, your history and your recent ICP results together. Tap Health Report , then Generate . It usually takes about twenty seconds. Like ICP analysis, it needs Allow Cora Assistant to use saved tank data . Use it when you want a careful look at the tank. Good times are before a big change, after a problem, or every few weeks as a check-in. An open report has buttons at the top to export it as a PDF, share a snapshot of the tank, or delete it.

Cora compares your lab results with what your equipment reports. If your alkalinity probe says 8.4 and your ICP says 7.6, you'll want to know, and Cora shows you without quietly picking one. This is one of the most useful things an ICP does in Cora. Treat it as a third opinion . It isn't the final word. Labs differ, and how a sample is handled, stored and shipped all move the result. A single ICP is evidence, and two tests that agree count for much more than one. If the gap persists, check the probe. It doesn't prove the probe is wrong. Changing labs or test methods If you change labs, or switch between a lab's ICP-OES and ICP-MS tests, your results can move even though nothing changed in your tank. Cora points this out when it compares them. ICP-OES can't measure very low chromium, tin, nickel, copper, cobalt or selenium. So a Below detection result for those on an ICP-OES test doesn't mean your tank has none.

Your plan sets how many ICP analyses and Health Reports you get each month. The line under the buttons shows what you've used. The numbers for each plan are in Plans and subscriptions . When your ICP analyses are used up, Cora first shows the plans you can move to. If you'd rather not upgrade, it asks Save results without the AI analysis? Tap Save my results and Cora still reads the report and saves every value, so trends, history and your readings update as normal. The score and the written analysis stay locked. You can run them later from the report itself once you have an ICP analysis to spend. On top of your plan's limit, Cora accepts up to 10 ICP uploads a day. An upload turned down for that reason doesn't use up any of your plan's ICP analyses. Cora Mobile only shows a general upload error, though, so if uploads start failing after a lot in one day, try again tomorrow.

The Intelligence screen keeps the two kinds apart. Lab results are under ICP REPORTS and generated reviews under HEALTH REPORTS . Each list shows the newest first, with its score. Tap one to open it again in full. You can also get to them from Settings : open a tank, then ICP Reports or Health Reports .

docs.d: Write down or dictate what you did to your tank, log feeding, and ask Cora about an entry, so later you can see what caused what.
x: The journal is where you write down what you did to the tank: water changes, new livestock, dosing changes, equipment work and anything unusual. When a parameter moves and you don't know why, the journal shows what changed around that date. Tap Journal in the row of buttons under the dashboard to open the Tank Journal . It's also in Settings → your tank → Journal . Entries newest first, with category chips to filter them.

Tap New Entry . The form has: TITLE and DESCRIPTION , in plain words CATEGORY : Observation, Concern, Emergency, Change or Milestone. A concern or an emergency also gets a SEVERITY (Info, Warning or Critical) DATE & TIME , which starts at now. Change it if you're writing it up later TAGS , to find entries again PHOTOS , with Take photo or Choose from library . A coral colouring up, a pump acting strangely or a test kit result Attach water params , which saves the tank's current readings with the entry. It's what makes an entry useful months later Keep entries short A short note is enough. "20 l water change, 5 ml extra alkalinity" says it all. Write it at the time if you can.

The round Cora button labelled Journal at the bottom right of the dashboard records a voice note, which is easier with wet hands. Tap it, say what happened (up to a minute), and tap again to stop. Cora turns what you said into one or more journal entries and tells you how many it saved. The same button is on the tank's timeline. Dictation uses Cora Assistant. If you haven't allowed it to use your tank data yet, Cora asks first.

These tend to matter most: Water changes: how much, and when Anything new in the tank: livestock, rock, media Dosing changes: what you changed and why Equipment: cleaned, replaced, moved, failed Anything unusual: a power cut, a hot day, a spill Some entries are written for you. Completing a maintenance task adds one, and so does Log the dose you gave in the dose calculator .

Tell Cora once how you usually feed, then log only the exceptions. To set your routine, open Edit tank (the pencil at the top of the dashboard) and tap Feeding routine . A card on the dashboard, How do you usually feed? , takes you there with Set up routine until you've done it. For each food, give the food, an Amount , a Unit (cube, pinch, g, ml, drop, scoop or sheet) and Times per day . Tap Add food for more. Turn on I use an auto feeder if one feeds for you, and its feeds count as part of the routine. Under Portion weights (optional) you can say what one cube or pinch weighs, so Cora can compare feeds over time in grams. When a day differs from the routine, tap Feeding in the row of buttons under the widgets, or the feeding icon at the top of the journal. The sheet Log a feeding exception has three choices: Fed extra , Skipped a feed and Changed food or amount . You can add an Amount (optional) . Each one is an ordinary journal entry, and Reef Buddy uses it, so a stable tank isn't blamed for a snack you gave it. Other ways a feeding gets logged: On a Neptune Apex, a Feed A to D cycle is recorded when the Cora Max that reads your Apex sees it start. That covers a cycle you start at the Apex, in Apex Fusion or from the Apex's own schedule. Tell Cora Assistant, by voice or in a chat, something like "Log that I fed mysis." It writes the entry for you.
Tap an entry to open and change it. To remove one, swipe it to the left and confirm. A deleted entry can't be brought back.

An entry in the Concern or Emergency category has an Analyze button. It sends the entry, with the tank's readings from around the same date, to Cora Assistant , and the assessment appears on the entry. Use it when you've written down something that worries you and want a second opinion.

Each tank has its own journal, newest first, with photos in line. To narrow a long journal, tap a category chip at the top: Observation , Concern , Emergency , Change or Milestone . The Tank timeline icon at the top opens the tank's story, where journal entries sit beside maintenance, livestock, water tests and alerts. See Activity and timeline . Cora Assistant reads the journal too. It answers questions like "when did I last change water?" from your entries as well as your readings.

You can add journal entries on Cora Max too, which is handy when you're standing at the tank. Open the journal from the tank menu, or dictate an entry. The journal screen on Cora Max also has Fed extra and Skipped a feed buttons, with a line showing your feeding routine. If you haven't set one, the line says Set your feeding routine in the phone app , because you set the routine in Cora Mobile. More in Journal, livestock and maintenance on Cora Max.

docs.d: Start the guided cycling journey for a new tank, follow it to the end, and work through a dinoflagellate problem step by step.
x: In a journey, Cora walks you through something over days or weeks. There are two kinds, and they work differently: cycling a new tank, and working through an issue .

Guided cycling is free on every plan. You start it from the tank's dashboard. Open the new tank on the Dashboard tab. A card asks Starting a new tank? Tap it. The first time, Cora explains Guided cycling : while the tank cycles, your dashboard focuses on ammonia, nitrite and nitrate and pauses the usual reef checks, which don't apply yet. Tap Got it: start cycling . The journey opens. Start it before you log anything or link equipment The Starting a new tank? card only shows on a tank with no readings at all. As soon as you log a test or link a device that sends readings, the card goes away, and there's no other way to start the cycling journey. If your tank is still cycling, start the journey first, then log your first test from inside it. Once it's running, the dashboard card reads Continue cycling · Day N . Tap it to get back to the journey. If it says Resume cycling , the tank is still set up for cycling: tap it to reopen the guide.

This is for a tank that isn't ready for livestock yet. Cycling grows the bacteria that turn toxic ammonia into safe nitrate, and the journey follows that process to the end. The stage, the three numbers that define it, and how long since you last tested. The journey screen, New Tank: cycling , has Your setup checklist , with the steps for getting the tank ready and seeding it, and a short why and how for each. Tick them off as you go. Tap Log a test to add an ammonia, nitrite and nitrate test. Enter what your kit read and leave the rest blank, then tap Save test . Test every two to three days. Cora works out your stage from those readings: Stage What is happening Log your first test Nothing logged yet. The journey needs numbers before it can place you Ready to start Everything is near zero and there's no nitrate yet. Ammonia hasn't been added, or hasn't started converting Ammonia stage The first colony is growing and eating ammonia Nitrite stage: about halfway The second colony is clearing nitrite. This is usually the longest stretch, and the one where people think something's gone wrong because the numbers stop moving Looks cycled Ammonia and nitrite are both gone and nitrate is present. Do the final check on screen before you mark the tank as cycled Your cycle so far plots the three curves together. They're scaled against each other instead of to their real values, so you can see one colony hand over to the next. Tap a name to see the real numbers. For a second opinion, tap Ask Cora about cycling . It opens Cora Assistant with a question about your latest readings. Two things stall a cycle Ammonia or nitrite above 5 ppm stalls the bacteria you're trying to grow. If you overshoot, a partial water change brings it back down. pH under 7 stalls it too. The journey warns you if either happens, because waiting longer won't help. Log all three tests Cora only shows Looks cycled when ammonia and nitrite have each been measured at zero and nitrate is present. Nitrate alone isn't enough. Source water often has some, and on its own it could look like a finished cycle and tempt you to add livestock too early. Readiness comes from your readings The journey judges readiness on what you've logged. How many weeks have gone by doesn't count. If you haven't tested for a fortnight, the tank stays where it was. That's why it shows how long it's been since your last test.

When the journey shows Looks cycled , do the final check: dose a full ammonia load of about 2 ppm and test again about 24 hours later. If ammonia and nitrite both read zero with nitrate present, you're cycled. Tap Mark my tank as cycled . Cora asks Mark your tank as cycled? Tap Yes, cycled , or Not yet to keep going. The tank switches to normal monitoring and the full reef intelligence turns on. Add livestock slowly, hardiest first.

Issue journeys cover one problem: dinoflagellates . Cora offers one when your readings and your report point to it. The journey only starts if you accept. Cora never starts one on its own. Only two journeys so far Cycling and dinoflagellates are the only journeys for now. For other problems, use Cora Assistant and the journal . An issue journey has three stages: Verify : can you trust the reading? Confirm it with a fresh test, then tap Confirmed: it's real . If it doesn't match your tank, tap It's not that / dismiss . Plan : Cora lists the steps, with why and how for each. Tick them off as you go, for as long as it takes, then tap How's it going? Outcome : did it work? You complete Verify yourself An issue journey opens on Verify . It asks you to confirm the reading before it shows a plan. A cycling journey has no Verify step. It works from the tests you log.

At the end, you say what happened: Resolved · Improving · No change · Worse · Stopped Be honest, even if it's Worse . The outcome is saved with the journey, so if a similar problem comes up later you can compare it with what you tried and how it went.
If an issue journey isn't useful, dismiss it. It stops showing up, and Cora records the dismissal so it offers similar journeys less often.

docs.d: Add the corals, fish and invertebrates in your tank, and record losses, frags, sales and moves so you can spot patterns later.
x: Livestock is your list of the corals, fish and invertebrates in your tank. For each one, it keeps the date you added it and what has happened to it since. Tap Livestock in the row of buttons under the dashboard. It's also in Settings → your tank → Livestock . Inventory summary and recent losses, with entries grouped by type.

At the top you'll see the Inventory Summary , with totals for corals, fish and inverts, and how many losses you've recorded in the last 90 days. Below that, entries are grouped by type, such as SPS Coral, LPS Coral, Soft Coral and Fish. Each one shows its quantity and the date you added it. Tap Show Lost at the top to see what's no longer in the tank. Show Alive takes you back.

Tap Add Livestock at the bottom of the screen and fill in: Name \ *, whatever you call it. It's the only field you must fill in. Type : SPS Coral, LPS Coral, Soft Coral, Fish, Invertebrate, Anemone or Other. Species (optional) , if you know it. Quantity , for groups like a shoal or a frag pack. Notes (optional) , for anything else, such as supplier, placement or cost. The date added is set to today when you save.

Tap an entry to see what you can do with it: Mark as Lost when something dies. If the entry has a quantity above one, Cora asks How many lost? , so you can record part of a group. Set the date it was lost and pick a Reason , such as bleaching, RTN, aggression or unknown. Fragged when you've cut it up and the colony lives on. Sold when it went to someone else. Moved when it's now in another of your tanks. On an entry that's no longer alive, Restore to alive undoes the change, for example if you marked it by mistake. Edit changes the details. Delete removes the entry altogether. View history opens the item's story: when it was added, and when it was lost or left the tank. If you log every loss, patterns show up later. Maybe the losses cluster in one corner of the tank, or they follow a particular event. "unknown" is a fine reason Log the date even when you don't know the cause. The date is what you'll compare against later.
Livestock and the rest of Cora

Cora judges your parameters partly by how stocked the tank is. A packed SPS system and a lightly stocked softie tank aren't held to the same standard. You can also ask about it. Cora Assistant answers questions like "When did I add the hammer coral?" or "What have I lost this year?" from this list. Changes to your livestock also show up on the tank timeline . Write the story behind a loss or a new arrival in the journal .

docs.d: Add recurring jobs like cleaning the skimmer or changing filter socks, get reminded when they're due, and mark them done or snooze them.
x: Maintenance keeps the jobs your tank needs on a regular basis, with a reminder for each one. Tap Maintenance in the row of buttons under the dashboard. It's also in Settings → your tank → Maintenance . Compliance, overdue count, and each task with its last completion and next due date.

At the top you'll see Maintenance Compliance , the share of tasks that are on schedule right now, and how many tasks are overdue. Each task in the list is colour-coded as overdue, due soon or scheduled. It also shows when you last did it and when it's due next.

Tap Add Task , then choose: From Template for a common job with its interval filled in. Pick it, then set when it's next due and the time you want to be reminded, and tap Confirm . Custom Task for your own. Give it a Task name , an Interval (days) , a Category and a Next due date . Turn on Reminder and pick Remind me at if you want a notification. Some of the templates, with the interval they start on: Task Interval Change filter socks 3 days Clean skimmer cup 7 days Water change 7 days Test water parameters 7 days Replace carbon 30 days Calibrate pH probe 30 days Clean powerheads 90 days Upload ICP results 90 days You can change the interval of any task later.
Tasks Cora adds for Red Sea equipment

When you connect a Red Sea ReefDose, ReefATO+, ReefMat or ReefRun, Cora adds the servicing that unit needs, already on the right interval: Device Task Interval ReefATO+ Replace ReefATO+ EC sensor 42 days ReefATO+ Replace ReefATO+ return pump 135 days ReefMat Replace ReefMat carbon 25 days ReefRun Check ReefRun skimmer venturi 35 days ReefRun Replace ReefRun skimmer rotor 135 days ReefRun Calibrate ReefRun full-cup sensor 28 days ReefRun Calibrate ReefRun overskimming sensor 28 days ReefRun, per pump Service ReefRun pump motor 135 days ReefRun, per pump Clean ReefRun pump strainer 42 days ReefDose, per head Calibrate ReefDose head 90 days ReefDose, per head Replace ReefDose head tubing 450 days They work like any task you add yourself. You can rename them, change the interval, snooze them or delete them. If you delete one, Cora won't add it back for that device.

If you tap Remind me to test every week on the first-test card, Cora adds a weekly task called Test water , due on the Test day you pick. It works like any other task. See Setting up Cora Mobile . You can also add a testing reminder at any time with the Test water parameters template.

An automation with the action Create a Maintenance Task can put a job on this list when its rule fires, or make an existing task due now. A new one is a One-off task , due now, and it shows Raised by an automation with the reason. It leaves the list when you complete it. While it's still open, the same automation doesn't add another. You get one notification.

Open a task and turn on Reminder , then pick Remind me at . You get a notification the day before it's due and one on the day. While it's overdue, you get a reminder every few days. If several tasks on a tank come due together, they arrive as one notification. Reminders come under Maintenance Reminders in Settings → Notifications . If you'd rather just see a task in the list, turn its Reminder off.

Swipe the task to the right, or open it and tap Complete . If you swiped by mistake, tap Undo on the message that appears. Cora saves the time you finished and counts the next due date from then. So if you do a job three days late, the next one moves out by three days too. The task's sheet shows its Completion history , including how late each one was. Completing a task also writes a journal entry Cora adds a short entry to your journal for you, noting if it was late. Add your own entry when there's more to say, for example when the pump was full of sand or the socks were black after one day.
Tap a task to open it. You can change the Task name , Interval (days) , Notes (optional) , Next due date and the reminder, then tap Save . Delete removes it.

Can't get to a job right now? Open it, tap Snooze and pick 1 Day , 3 Days , 1 Week , 2 Weeks or 1 Month . It stays in the list as Snoozed with its new date, and you won't be reminded until then. Only mark a task done when you've done it The next due date is counted from the day you mark it done. If you mark an open task as done, every later due date shifts. Snooze it instead. There's no way to pause a task. For a job that doesn't apply this season, snooze it for 1 Month , or delete it and add it again later.

docs.d: Tap a widget to see a parameter's full history, compare sources and parameters, exclude a bad reading and record probe care.
x: A widget shows you a number. Tap it to see the story behind that number. There are two ways in. Tap a widget on the dashboard, or tap Parameter History in the row of buttons under the widgets and choose a parameter. Parameter History lists every parameter that has data, even one with no widget on the dashboard.

The dropdowns along the top, then the chart with your alert band shaded. A history chart. The row above it sets what it shows. Parameter switches to any other parameter that has data, and keeps your timeframe. Timeframe goes from 1h through 6h, 12h, 24h, 3d, 7d, 15d, 30d, 90d, 180d and 360d to All. Source starts on All sources and lists the sources that report this parameter on this tank, such as Apex , Cora , Red Sea or Manual . Pick one to see only its readings. Compare , at the end of the same row, draws a second parameter on the chart, like alkalinity with calcium or pH with temperature. The button then reads vs and the other parameter's name. Tap it again to take the second line off. A row with Latest , Min , Avg and Max for the time window on screen. Icons in the top bar: Readings opens the raw readings list, and Record probe care logs a calibration or cleaning. For alkalinity, calcium and magnesium there's also the dose calculator, which uses the tank volume from your tank profile and the strengths from Dosing . The screen always opens on 24h and All sources . It doesn't remember what you picked last time.

The green band is your alert range, so you see each reading against it. To change the range, long-press the widget on the dashboard. More in Alerts and thresholds . A dashed line marks a logged dose, so you can line up a change with what you dosed. 30d high and 30d low are dashed lines showing the last 30 days' extremes. A hollow dot is a reading you excluded. With Compare on, the second parameter uses the right-hand axis.

Pick the timeframe that fits how the parameter moves. Parameter Useful window pH 24 hours, since it swings on a daily cycle Temperature 24 hours or 7 days Alkalinity 7 or 30 days Trace elements 30 days or a year Flat line? Check how old the reading is A line that hasn't moved can mean the parameter is stable. It can also mean the source stopped reporting. The age next to the value on the widget tells you which.

When more than one source reports a parameter, Cora keeps them separate and doesn't average them. Use the Source dropdown to look at each one. It's the quickest way to compare a probe with a test kit. Which one shows on the dashboard is the newest. A live value is only replaced by a reading with a later measurement time, from any source. An older reading goes into history and doesn't overwrite what's on the widget. If you pinned a source in Parameter Mapping , Cora follows that source instead. If a probe and your hand-logged tests stay apart by the same amount, the probe usually needs calibrating. An ICP result is a useful third opinion, but it doesn't settle the question. Labs differ from each other, and how the sample was handled, stored and shipped all change the result. Treat one ICP as evidence. Two tests that agree are worth far more than one.
Choosing which source a reading follows

The source is set per tank and per parameter, not per widget. Go to Settings , tap the tank, tap Parameter Mapping , then the Sources tab. Pick a probe, or Automatic (newest reading wins) . The choice applies to that parameter everywhere for the tank. More in Parameter Mapping .

Maybe a probe spiked, you misread a test, or you took the sample in the middle of a water change. One wrong reading throws off the chart, the averages and anything worked out from them. Every reading behind the line, with its time and source. Tap one to exclude it. Tap Readings in the top bar, then tap a reading. Cora asks Exclude this reading? and explains that it stays in your log but stops counting toward averages, trends, insights and the assistant. Tap Exclude . Nothing is deleted, and you can bring it back the same way. Readings older than 90 days can't be excluded or brought back. Exclude wrong readings, not unwelcome ones Only exclude a reading you know is invalid. If you just don't like a reading but can't find anything wrong with it, it's real data. Removing it makes every later comparison less honest.

Tap Record probe care (the sensor icon in the top bar) and pick what you did: calibrate, clean, replace, move or compare. Cora puts the date on that source, so a fresh calibration isn't mistaken for drift. Later, if the probe disagrees with something, you can see when it was last looked after. More in Parameter Mapping .

You log readings from the dashboard, not from this screen. Tap Log Parameters under the widgets and enter what your test kit says. The list is grouped, and the Trace group covers iodine, iron and copper in µg/L, and potassium in mg/L. Hand-logged readings count as much as any other. They get their own source and time, show on the chart and feed Reef Buddy. They're also what Cora checks your equipment against. Cora double-checks odd-looking entries If a value is far from where the tank has been, Cora asks you to confirm it before saving. This catches a decimal point in the wrong place, or a reading entered under the wrong parameter. Once you confirm, the reading is saved as usual.

docs.d: With more than one Cora device, choose which one answers your voice and which one polls each tank, and see what works away from home.
x: This page is for a household with more than one Cora Max, or a Cora Max and several phones. Two settings decide which device does what, so they don't do the same work twice. It also helps to know what they share.
What is shared, and what is not

Shared across every device Belongs to one Cora Max Tanks, readings and history Its dashboard layout Devices and their settings Wi-Fi, brightness, audio Journal, livestock, maintenance Wake word and child lock Alerts, thresholds, automations Which tanks that screen shows Plans and usage If you change a threshold on one device, it changes everywhere. Dashboard layouts are different. Your phone layout follows your account, so every phone you sign in on shows the same one. Each Cora Max keeps its own layout, and the phone and Cora Max never share one.

Settings → Cora Assistant → Answering device picks the Cora device that answers when you talk to the room. However many devices hear you, only one answers. Set it to the one closest to where you usually stand. Only the Answering device listens for the wake phrase. Another Cora Max takes over listening while it's offline, or hasn't been seen for more than 15 minutes, and stops once it's back. More in Talking to Cora . This is separate from Primary Cora Max, further down. Answering device decides who answers your voice. Primary Cora Max decides who polls a tank's equipment. With two Cora Max devices at home, you might set them differently. Each device shows what it listens for, and whether it is online. Each device in the list shows its wake phrase and whether it's online. The wake phrases aren't always the same. The phrase is trained into the device, so different Cora models can listen for different ones. Check each device's own row. Don't assume the whole household uses one phrase. Your phone isn't in this list The phone doesn't listen for a wake phrase. You start a conversation on it by tapping, and that always works, whatever this setting says. The list only shows Cora hardware that has voice.

A Cora Max reads the equipment on your network. If more than one can reach the same controller, they'd all poll it side by side. Primary Cora Max lets you pick, for each tank, which device reads that tank's controller. In Cora Mobile, open the tank and tap Primary Cora Max . Setting Behaviour A named device It's the only Cora device that polls the controller. It stays the primary even while it's offline, and other Cora devices don't take over. Cora Mobile reads the controller only while that device is offline. Any active (automatic) Cora Mobile and any online Cora device share the work (last write wins). If one goes offline, another carries on. Good for a household with one device, and the safer choice if you're not sure which device should own the tank. While the device you named is offline, a command that has to go through it won't run. Cora tells you the tank is set to use that device, that it's offline and that nothing ran. Try again once it's back. If it'll be offline for a while, pick another device or Any active (automatic) . Two devices watching one tank? Set a primary Naming a primary takes load off the controller and gets rid of duplicate readings from the same source. This setting belongs to the tank Primary Cora Max is set per tank for the whole account. It doesn't belong to the phone or Cora Max you're holding. Change it from any device and it changes for the whole household.

When you're away from your tank's Wi-Fi, your phone doesn't talk to your equipment directly. A command goes to Cora Cloud, which hands it to a Cora Max at the tank. That Cora Max is what reaches the equipment. Here's what that means for you. Readings and history are always there, wherever you are. They're already stored in Cora Cloud. Controlling equipment works away from home too, as long as a Cora Max at the tank is online and can reach that equipment. That covers things like switching an outlet, starting a feed, dosing a head or pausing a pump. If no Cora Max can reach it, the command can't get through. A device's own settings (its native settings, not its readings) sometimes need a phone on the same network as the device. A Cora Max at the tank isn't enough for those. The page for that device says when this applies. Two messages tell you a command didn't go through cleanly. "Nothing was sent" means the command never left your phone, or no Cora Max at the tank could take it. Nothing ran. You'll see this if the tank's Primary Cora Max is offline and no other device on that tank can step in. "It may already have run" means the command went out, but no Cora Max confirmed it in time. Cora really doesn't know whether it ran. Check the equipment itself before you try again, so you don't send it twice. If either message keeps coming up, check that a Cora Max at the tank is online. You can also set Primary Cora Max to Any active (automatic) so any online device can pick up the command. Every possible outcome of a command is listed in Controlling your equipment .
Where each device's state is shown
Cora Max shows each tank's polling status under Settings → Cora Max Settings → Status . There's more in Devices and device health .

docs.d: Choose which notifications reach your phone, keep nights quiet, read what you missed under the bell, and fix notifications that don't arrive.
x: Settings → Notifications decides which of Cora's notifications reach your phone. This page also covers the bell, quiet nights, and what to check when nothing arrives. Each category has its own switch.

The card at the top says whether this phone allows notifications from Cora at all ( Notifications enabled or Notifications disabled ). Under App Notifications , each category has its own switch: Category Covers Parameter Alerts Water chemistry outside a range you set, and the recovered notification when it comes back Maintenance Reminders Tasks you scheduled, like water changes, and a one-time reminder to log your first test when a new tank still has no readings after three days Equipment Faults A device reporting a problem, for example a Trident that has stopped testing. Also a device that stopped reporting and a missed dose Supplies Running Low Reagent, top-off water, dosing containers, and a full waste bottle ICP Report Ready Your ICP results are analysed and ready to read When you turn a category off, it stops pushing. Cora still records the event, and you'll still find it under the bell. These switches belong to your account, so they apply to every phone you're signed in on. "Parameter Alerts" is only about chemistry That switch doesn't cover everything the tank might tell you. A Trident that has stopped testing is an Equipment Fault . Reagent running out is Supplies Running Low . Each has its own switch. If you've relied on Parameter Alerts for a long time, check the other two. The waste bottle counts as a supply even though it fills up instead of running down. It's something to empty before it stops the tests.

A few notifications aren't in that list: Reef Buddy's daily briefing. You choose when it arrives with Briefing time , the row just below Notifications in Settings. On the free plan there's no briefing notification. More in Reef Buddy . Plan notifications: trial reminders 7 days and 1 day before the trial ends and when it ends, and a warning when you've used 80% and 100% of your monthly Cora Assistant allowance. See Plans .

Cora Mobile has no quiet hours setting. A parameter alert is sent as soon as the reading crosses your range, day or night. These are the ways to keep a night quiet: Use your phone's Focus or Do Not Disturb. Cora's notifications wait silently and you'll find them under the bell in the morning. If you want real emergencies to wake you, allow Cora through. Turn off the categories you don't need at night. Supplies and maintenance can usually wait. A switch stays off all day, though. Lengthen a rule's cooldown. If one alert keeps waking you about a problem you already know about, raise its Cooldown between alerts . See Cooldowns . Pick when reminders arrive. Each maintenance task has a Remind me at time, and Reef Buddy uses your Briefing time (8:00 unless you change it). On Cora Max, Night dimming dims the screen overnight, and in the Sound & Voice section you can switch off Alert sound and Spoken alerts . Those two stay off until you turn them back on. See Cora Max settings . Don't silence what you'd want to hear A heater sticking on at 3 am is exactly the alert you want. If you silence your phone at night, allow Cora through Focus or Do Not Disturb so an alert like that can still reach you.

The bell sits at the top right of the main tabs. It holds everything Cora has raised, newest first, whether or not it was pushed. The number on it is how many you haven't read. Inside, notifications are grouped by Today , Yesterday and earlier dates. Use the tank chips at the top ( All , or one tank) to narrow the list. Mark all read clears the count. Clear All empties the inbox after you confirm, and it can't be undone. Check it after a day away from your phone, or when a category you switched off has raised something.

Go through these in order. Look at the card at the top of Settings → Notifications . If it says Notifications disabled , this phone blocks Cora. Tap Open Settings and allow notifications. While they're blocked, nothing reaches this phone, whatever the switches below say. Check the category's switch under App Notifications . Check your phone's Focus or Do Not Disturb. Ask whether there was anything to send. Reef Buddy stays quiet on days when nothing changed, and a free account gets no briefing. An alert that's already up waits for its cooldown before it notifies you again. Still nothing? See Troubleshooting .

Look at your thresholds before you turn notifications off. Too many alerts usually means a range is tighter than the tank really runs, or a source needs calibrating. More in Alerts and thresholds . Turning a category off silences all of it. If it's one alert pushing too often, change Cooldown between alerts on that rule instead. It goes from 15 minutes up to 1 week. The cooldown options, and what Snooze does on Cora Max, are in Cooldowns .

docs.d: What the Free, trial, Plus, Pro and Max plans include, how to subscribe or upgrade, where to see your usage, and how to cancel on iPhone or Android.
x: Monitoring your tank is free, with no limit. The paid plans give you bigger AI allowances and add Reef Buddy. This page covers what each plan includes and how to subscribe, change or cancel.

Live readings from your equipment, with dashboards and charts Devices, alerts and thresholds Journal, maintenance and livestock Push notifications for critical alerts Guided cycling for a new tank As many tanks as you like. AI features cover your first tank (see Which tanks get AI ) Exporting your data

Feature Free Assistant messages 20 a month. Voice uses the same pool and costs more per turn Voice sessions 20 a month Health reports 1 a month ICP analysis One, once . You get a single analysis for the life of the account, then it's locked AI on tanks Your first tank only Reef Buddy Not included. You see a locked card with See plans When an allowance runs out, you can still read everything Cora has already made for you.

Your 30-day Pro trial starts when you create your account . It doesn't wait until you first use a feature, and you don't need a card. Account & Subscription shows it as Cora Pro Trial , with the date it ends. During the trial Assistant messages 100 a month Voice sessions 60 a month Health reports 4 a month ICP analyses 1 a month Reef Buddy and AI monitoring Your first tank The trial includes Reef Buddy and Design with AI . Its allowances are smaller than the Pro plan's. When it ends, your account goes back to Free. Nothing is deleted. You can still read every reading, journal entry, report and briefing you have.

There are three plans, Plus , Pro and Max , each monthly or annual. Settings shows them as Cora Plus, Cora Pro and Cora Max. You'll find current prices in Cora Mobile and in your app store, since that's where you pay. Plus Pro Max Assistant messages / month 500 1,200 2,500 (fair use) Voice sessions / month 100 200 400 Health Reports / month 4 12 100 ICP analyses / month 1 3 30 Tanks with AI monitoring 1 5 20 Voice sessions have their own count, and every spoken reply also uses up your message allowance. Every paid plan includes Reef Buddy, ICP upload and analysis for the labs Cora reads, comparison with your own history, and Design with AI for dashboards (up to 5 designs a day for each tank). The Max plan isn't the Cora Max screen The Max plan is a subscription. Cora Max is the screen that sits by your tank. You don't need one to have the other.
Reef Buddy and AI monitoring cover as many tanks as your plan allows, counted from the top of Settings → Reorder tanks . To bring a tank in, move it up the list. Removed tanks don't take a place.

Open Settings and tap the account card at the top. Account & Subscription opens. Next to your plan, tap See plans (on Free or the trial), Upgrade (on Plus) or Upgrade to Max (on Pro). Choose Monthly or Annual . The annual price shows how much you save. Pick a plan and tap Subscribe . Confirm with the App Store or Google Play. Your new plan unlocks as soon as the store confirms it. Pick Monthly or Annual, then a plan, then Subscribe. The same plan picker also opens when you reach a limit, for example You've hit your message limit , and from the locked Reef Buddy card.

Your plan under Subscription, with Upgrade to Max and Restore Purchases. Account & Subscription shows your current plan and when it renews or ends. Below that are these controls. Control Does Redeem code Applies a promotional or partner code. Android only: iPhone doesn't show it Manage Subscription Opens your store's subscription page. It shows when Cora knows where you bought the plan Restore Purchases Brings back a purchase made on another device, or before you reinstalled

Each metered feature against its monthly allowance. Settings → Cora Assistant → Usage & Limits shows each metered feature next to its monthly allowance, all on one screen. That's Assistant messages, ICP analyses and health reports. You can also see usage where you use each feature. In Assistant , this month's messages are shown above the message box. In Intelligence , this month's ICP analyses and health reports are shown under the buttons. The counts start again at the beginning of each calendar month.

To move up, use Upgrade or Upgrade to Max as above. To move down or switch between monthly and annual, use Manage Subscription . Changes go through the App Store or Google Play and follow the same rules as any other subscription on your phone, including that store's refund and cancellation terms.

You cancel with the store you paid. You can't cancel inside Cora. Your plan runs to the end of the period you've paid for, then goes back to Free. The quickest way is Settings → your account card → Manage Subscription . If you bought the plan on the other kind of phone, Cora says so ( Bought on the App Store or Bought on Google Play ) and Continue opens that store's page. If Manage Subscription isn't there, go to the store directly. iPhone: open the Settings app, tap your name, then Subscriptions . Pick Cora and tap Cancel Subscription . Android: open Google Play , tap your profile picture, then Payments & subscriptions → Subscriptions . Pick Cora and tap Cancel subscription . Cancelling doesn't delete anything Your tanks, readings, history and journal stay as they are. You lose the paid features, but you keep your data. Come back later and it's all still there. Deleting your account doesn't cancel If you plan to delete your account, cancel the subscription first. Deleting the account doesn't stop the store billing you. See Deleting your account .
If your plan is not showing

Sometimes a purchase takes a moment to reach Cora Mobile. If it's been a few minutes, try these. Close Cora completely and open it again. Make sure you're signed in to the same account that made the purchase. Make sure the store account on your phone is the one you bought with. If it still isn't there, tap Restore Purchases . If Settings says Couldn't verify your plan , check your connection and tap Retry . Your access doesn't change while Cora checks. If none of that works, email cora@coraiq.tech with the date you bought it. Your data stays yours whatever plan you're on. More in Exporting your data and deleting your account . To report a billing problem from inside Cora Mobile, see Reporting a problem .

docs.d: Choose which probe drives each reading, tell Cora what each probe measures, and record probe calibration and cleaning.
x: Use Parameter Mapping to tell Cora what each probe measures and, when two probes report the same thing, which one to trust. Go to Settings , open the tank, and tap Parameter Mapping . It sits between Edit tank and Alert thresholds . The pencil at the top of the dashboard opens Edit tank , which doesn't have it. You can also reach it from the Neptune Apex device page. The screen has a search field ( Search parameters ) and two tabs, Mapping and Sources . Search looks at parameter names, probe names, devices and brands. The same search field is in every parameter picker.
Probes: telling Cora what each one is

Each probe, grouped by the device that reports it, with the parameter it's mapped to. The Mapping tab opens first. It lists every probe Cora knows about, grouped by the device that reports it, with its current reading. Cora recognises standard probe names on its own, and each row shows what it matched. Usually you only need to fix the few it couldn't place. Each row gives you three choices. A Cora parameter is the metric that probe measures. Custom… is for a probe Cora has no standard parameter for. Type a short upper-case name in Custom metric (UPPER token) , and Cora tracks it under that name. Ignore is for probes you don't want recorded at all. An ignored or unmapped probe won't show on a dashboard and won't trigger alerts. A mapping starts working the next time readings come in. Fixing one here doesn't rewrite history. It only changes what gets saved from then on. Tap Save to apply your changes. Cora can't see an unmapped probe If a parameter shows no readings but the probe is working, check its mapping first.

Each reading, the probe feeding it, and whether it's Automatic or Chosen by you. The Sources tab lists every metric Cora tracks for this tank, such as pH or temperature, and shows which probe is feeding it now. Tap a reading to see every probe that reports it, across every controller you've connected. Each one shows its brand, its own name for the probe, and its live value. Pick one to pin it, or choose Automatic (newest reading wins) to let Cora use whichever probe reported most recently. The others stay in history. A tag next to each reading shows which is in effect: Automatic , or Chosen by you once you've pinned a probe. Your choice applies to that reading across the whole tank, not to one widget. If a pinned probe stops reporting, Cora shows when it was last heard from and offers Back to Automatic , so a dead probe can't leave a reading stuck. Tap Rename to give a reading its own display name. This is separate from any name you give the probe itself. It's what shows up on your dashboard, in alerts and in Reef Buddy. The tank profile also has a Parameter Sources section (it's hidden while you create a new tank). It sets the same thing in a shorter form. Use Parameter Mapping when you want every probe on every controller in one place. A leak sensor can't be reassigned here A leak sensor's alarm depends on its own name, so it's excluded from this picker. It works the same as always.

If you have two temperature probes, whether on the same controller or on two different ones, map them both. Cora keeps them as separate sources, and the Sources tab is where you pick which one drives the reading, or leave it on Automatic. You can compare them in the parameter view . When two sources report the same parameter, the newest measurement wins. A value on screen is only replaced by a reading with a later measurement time, whichever device it comes from. An older reading, or a device that re-sends an old one, goes to history and doesn't overwrite the current value. If you pinned a source in the Sources tab, Cora follows that source instead.

Probes drift. When you calibrate, clean or replace a probe, tell Cora, so it doesn't mistake the jump in the reading for a real change in the tank. Tap the parameter's widget on the dashboard, for example pH, temperature, salinity or ORP. Tap Record probe care (the sensor icon) in the top bar. Pick what you did: Calibrated , Cleaned , Replaced , Repositioned or Compared to reference . You can add a Reference reading and a note. Tap Log probe care . The parameter view then shows how long ago that probe was calibrated. Probe care also works well as a recurring maintenance task . Calibration dates explain disagreements When a probe and a test kit disagree, check when you last calibrated the probe. That's usually the answer.

docs.d: Your daily Reef Buddy briefing, what it covers, when it arrives, how to read the scores, and why a briefing might not come.
x: Reef Buddy is a short daily look at your tank. It comes each morning, tells you what changed, and points out anything that needs your attention before you'd notice it yourself. You'll see it as a card at the top of your dashboard, and as one notification when there's something worth acting on. Stability and Data scores, a summary, then the insights behind them.

It starts with a headline, one line that sums up the tank today. Then come two scores. Score Means Stability Out of 100. How steady your readings have been over the last 30 days Data A percentage. How complete the data behind the assessment is A low Data score means Cora had fewer readings to work with than it wanted. Look at it first. When Data is low, take the Stability number next to it as a first guess. Next is a summary, a short paragraph that explains the headline using your real values and ranges. Then come the insights, one for each finding. Each has a category (such as Water Chemistry ) and a cadence (such as Daily ), and you can expand it for detail. A chip at the top of the section shows the tank type and how complete its profile is. Both affect what Cora can conclude. Cora filters insights before they reach you. An insight has to hold up over several readings. One isn't enough. It also has to tell you something a single chart wouldn't already show. Tap the card on the dashboard to open the full briefing.

Tap × to clear today's card from the dashboard. Tomorrow's still comes. To open today's briefing after you've cleared the card, tap the newspaper button at the top of the dashboard ( Reef Buddy daily health ). An older briefing opens from its notification.
Updating the briefing with a new test

If you log a test by hand or add an ICP result after the briefing came out, the full briefing shows New readings since this briefing with an Update briefing button. Tap it and Cora redoes the briefing with the new numbers. It uses one message from your Assistant allowance. You can do this once a day for your account. After that the button is greyed out and says You can update the briefing once a day. Next update: tomorrow. Probe and controller readings don't trigger this offer, because they come in all day.

Under an insight, tap Why am I seeing this? The sheet Why you're seeing this lists the Readings it used , the Target it compared against (your own target, or a reference range), anything From your journal that it took into account, and the time window in days it looked at. If the reasoning doesn't fit your tank, answer the insight as described in Correcting an insight . Briefings also draw on more than parameter readings. They can use the light schedules on your lights, the speed of a ReefMat roll, your hand-logged alkalinity next to a device's and the totals of your DŌS heads.

Once a day for each tank, at the hour you choose. Set it in Settings → Briefing time , next to Notifications . The briefing arrives within about 15 minutes of that hour, in your own time zone. If you never choose, it comes at 8:00. Pick an hour after your usual morning test, so today's result is in the briefing. On a day when nothing needs your attention, Reef Buddy usually stays quiet. It won't push just to say everything's fine. A push means there's something worth acting on. That could be a new change, or something that has gone on long enough to mention. One tank, one briefing Each tank your plan covers gets its own briefing, and each one is only about that tank. See Which tanks get a briefing . Cora Max has its own Reef Buddy setting Cora Max has a Reef Buddy section in its Settings too. Its Briefing time is the same setting as on your phone: change it on either one and both follow. The switch for the on-screen briefing belongs to that Cora Max only. Turning it off there doesn't stop the briefing reaching your phone.

Stability shows how steady your readings have been over the last 30 days. It measures steadiness only. It doesn't check whether readings are in range, so a tank held steady at the wrong level can still score well. To see how you're doing against your target ranges, run a Health Report . Treat Stability as a trend to watch over time. Compare it with your own earlier scores, and not with someone else's tank. Data shows how much recent information Cora had to work with. It drops when readings get old. A falling Data score usually means old readings If you haven't tested anything for a week, the Data score drops and the Stability score becomes less reliable. Log some readings to bring both back up.

Reef Buddy is part of the paid plans. It's also included in the 30-day trial that starts when you create your account. Each plan covers a set number of tanks: 1 on the trial and on Plus, 5 on Pro and 20 on Max. Briefings go to the first tanks in the order set in Settings → Reorder tanks . To include a tank that's missing out, move it up the list. Removed tanks don't take a place. After the trial, a free account sees a locked Reef Buddy card with See plans where the briefing was, and gets no briefing notification. More in Plans and subscriptions .

Nothing needed your attention. Reef Buddy stays quiet on a good day. The card is still on the dashboard. Your trial ended. A free account gets the locked card and no notification. The tank is past your plan's limit. Move it up in Settings → Reorder tanks . Notifications are off. Check Notifications . If you turned off Allow Cora Assistant to use saved tank data , the briefing still comes, but its summary is a plain fixed text and the AI-written observation is left out. See Asking Cora .

You can respond to each insight in one of four ways. Response Means Confirmed It was right, and useful Doesn't match It doesn't match what you're seeing Already knew Right, but you were aware Not sure You can't judge it yet When Reef Buddy flags a drift, it also asks Was this heads-up useful? You can answer Helpful , Not helpful , This change is expected or Reading looks wrong . Your feedback shapes what shows up first in later briefings. Hiding an insight only lasts for a while. If the problem is still there, the insight comes back. Serious findings are never hidden Feedback only quiets lower-severity insights. Warning and critical insights keep showing up, whatever you've answered before.

docs.d: Build a day program for a Jecod pump and copy it between pumps.
x: Use this page to give a Jecod pump a day program : a set of periods, each with its own intensity, that repeats every day. Open it from Devices → tap the pump. Lights and pumps from other brands keep their schedules in their own pages: Red Sea's ReefDose in Controlling your equipment . Schedule picked at the top, the feeding pause, then the day graph.

A pump runs in one of two modes. Pick one with the switch on its page. The one that is running is marked · running , and the page opens on it. Same all day runs at one intensity the whole time. Schedule follows a day program made of periods. Cora sends your choice straight to the pump when your phone is on its network. If your phone isn't, it goes through the Cora Max at the tank. A Bluetooth pump has to be in range. Until it is, your choice only changes what you see on screen. A feeding pause takes the pump off its schedule for a while, and on your phone the schedule comes back only while the pump's page stays open. See Feeding pause .

Every schedule screen has the same three parts. At the top is the day graph. It shows the whole day from 0 to 24 hours, and each period is a block whose height is its intensity. It's the quickest way to check that a program does what you think. Below the graph is the period list. Each period shows its hours, mode and intensity, for example Random, 00:00–03:00, Freq 50%, 40% . You add, edit and remove periods here. Tap Add to schedule to add a period. To change one, open it and tap Save . To remove it, tap Delete and confirm. Saving writes the schedule to the device When you save, Cora sends the program to the equipment, and the equipment runs it on its own clock. It keeps running whether Cora can reach it or not.
If you have several pumps that should behave the same way, build one program and copy it. Open the pump that has the program you want, tap Copy schedule to… and choose the pump to copy it to.

Once you have a schedule you like, you don't have to build it again. Save schedule as… keeps it under a name. Saved schedules… applies it again later. Share this schedule turns it into a short code. Paste a schedule code… applies a code someone sent you. This is a Cora Mobile feature. The code only carries the schedule. It gives no one access to your account.

When your phone isn't on the pump's network, Cora Mobile goes through the Cora Max at the tank. A few things work differently. Same all day and Schedule switch the pump through that Cora Max. A period you add or change only goes through if that Cora Max has reached the pump in the last hour. If it hasn't, the schedule tells you, and you can't change it from where you are. Copy schedule to… , Save schedule as… , Saved schedules… , Share this schedule and Paste a schedule code… need your phone on the pump's network. Until it is, they're greyed out and the menu tells you why. Without a Cora Max at the tank, you can only change a pump while your phone is on its network. More in Connecting your equipment . You can only reach a Bluetooth pump from a phone close to it. Stand in range to switch it, change its schedule or use any of those menu items.

You can give a pump a saved schedule in one step, without building the periods again. Open the pump, tap More at the top and choose Saved schedules… .
