The list holds every schedule saved on this tank, including ones you built on another pump. Pick one and tap Apply . It replaces the pump's whole day.
After you save, the device page shows the program the pump is running. If it doesn't match what you saved, the change didn't get through. Check that the device is reachable and try again.

docs.d: Where everything is in Cora Mobile's Settings tab, from your account and plan to tanks, Cora Assistant, language, dark mode, notifications and support.
x: This page walks through the Settings tab, in the order you'll find things. Your account card at the top, a Vacation mode banner while it's on, then the Cora group.

The card at the top shows who you're signed in as and which plan you're on. Tap it to open Account & Subscription . It has these, from top to bottom. Display name is what Cora Mobile calls you. Lab & ICP emails lets you add up to 3 more email addresses that your lab can use to reach your account. See ICP and health reports . Subscription shows your plan and when it renews, with See plans , Upgrade or Upgrade to Max , then Manage Subscription and Restore Purchases . On Android there's also Redeem code . All of it is explained in Plans and subscriptions . Sign Out Export My Data gives you your readings, journal entries and alerts as files, free on every plan. See Exporting your data . Delete Account is permanent. Read the two notes in Your data and privacy before you use it.

Automations are rules and scenes that run on their own. There's more in Automations and scenes . Cora Assistant holds the AI consent switches, AI memory, the Answering device, lab sharing and your usage. See Cora Assistant below. Activity is a log of every command sent to your equipment. More in Activity and timeline . Dosing Products holds the strength of what you dose. More in Dosing . Automations act on real equipment A rule that switches a pump will switch it even when you're not watching. Build rules one at a time, and check each one does what you expect before you add the next.

You'll see one row for each tank, then these. Add tank opens a new tank profile. Reorder tanks sets the order they come up when you swipe the dashboard. It also decides which tanks get Reef Buddy and AI monitoring when your plan covers fewer tanks than you have. See Plans and subscriptions . Removed tanks keeps tanks you've removed. Removing only hides a tank, and Restore brings it back with its readings, journal and devices. Adding, removing and restoring tanks are covered step by step in Managing your tanks . Open a tank and its settings page has three parts. Settings holds Edit tank , Parameter Mapping , Alert thresholds , Units , Primary Cora Max and Vacation mode . Records & Reports holds Journal , Maintenance , Livestock , Reef Buddy , Health Reports , ICP Reports , Activity and Guided setup . Devices on this tank is a read-only list. Parameter Mapping is where you choose which device feeds each reading. See Parameter Mapping . Units sets how this tank shows its readings, including litres or US or UK gallons for volume. See Your tank profile . Primary Cora Max is which device polls that tank's equipment, and is explained in More than one Cora device . To add or remove a device, use the Devices tab . Vacation mode is a plan for whoever looks after the tank while you're away. You set the dates and make a checklist of jobs, with how often each one needs doing. Cora turns it into a simple read-only page you can share with your tank sitter. They don't need an account. More in Going away .

Notifications decides what reaches your phone. More in Notifications . Briefing time is the hour your daily Reef Buddy briefing arrives, in your own time zone. It's one setting for the account, shared with Cora Max. More in Reef Buddy . Language is the account's language. See below. Appearance has a Dark Mode switch. On, Cora Mobile uses the dark Deep Reef theme. Off, it uses the light Luminous Azure theme. Device access is explained below. Help & Support is where you contact support, report a bug and find the Cora website and FAQ. See below. About is explained below.

There's one language for the whole account. Devices don't each have their own. If you change it on your phone, it changes on every Cora Max in the household too, and the other way round. New reports, alerts and Reef Buddy briefings use the new language from then on. Older ones stay in the language they were written in. They aren't translated again. If everything suddenly shows up in a language you didn't expect, someone changed it. They may have done it here, from another device on the account, or in the Language setting on a Cora Max. It's the same setting everywhere.

Device access opens your phone's own settings for Cora. That's where you allow what Cora needs to find your equipment. The row doesn't show whether anything is turned off. It just takes you to the place where you can check. On iPhone, it's Local Network and Bluetooth. Without Local Network access, a search for equipment on your Wi-Fi finds nothing, and you won't see an error. iPhone only asks once, so this is how you turn it back on. On Android, it's Bluetooth and location.

You open this from the Cora Assistant row under Cora , further up. Allow Cora Assistant to use saved tank data lets Cora Assistant use your tank history, metrics and devices. It has to be on for the Assistant (typed or spoken, on your phone and on Cora Max), ICP analysis, Health Reports and Design with AI . Reef Buddy still comes without it, with a plain summary. The full list is in Asking Cora . Contribute anonymized tank data keeps a de-identified copy of your parameter history for reef research. It's on unless you turn it off. That copy is made when you remove a tank, and it's the only thing kept after you delete your account. See Contributing anonymised data . AI memory is what Cora remembers about your system from one conversation to the next. You can read it and reset it. It only shows while the consent switch above is on. Answering device picks which Cora device answers the wake phrase in your home. More in More than one Cora device . Share Cora's analysis with labs decides whether a lab that sends you results can see Cora's scores and written analysis. It's off until you turn it on. Trusted labs lists the labs that can send results to your tanks without asking each time. It shows up once you've trusted one. More in ICP and health reports . Usage & Limits shows your monthly allowances and how much you've used.

Three settings about your data live in different places, so they're easy to miss. Export My Data is in Account & Subscription , just above Delete Account . See Exporting your data . Contribute anonymized tank data is under Cora Assistant , above. Send crash reports is in Help & Support . It sends the technical details when Cora Mobile stops or a screen fails to load, without you having to write anything. No tank data, photos or account details are included. Deleting your account does NOT cancel your subscription An App Store or Google Play subscription belongs to the store , not to Cora. Deleting your account removes your record here, but the billing doesn't stop . You keep being charged until you cancel with Apple or Google yourself. Cancel the subscription first, then delete the account. What deleting doesn't remove If Contribute anonymized tank data is on (and it is, unless you turned it off), a de-identified copy of your tanks' profiles and parameter history is kept for research when you delete your account. It has no link back to you. If you want that gone too, turn the switch off before you delete.

Settings → Help & Support has these. Contact Support opens an email to us. We usually reply within a day. Report a Bug / Send Feedback sends a report from inside Cora Mobile. See Reporting a problem . Send crash reports , described above. Cora Website & FAQ opens the Cora website.

This shows the version you're running, and a few more rows. Replay tips plays the first-run dashboard tour again, the one described in The first-run tour . It's handy after an update, or when someone new starts using Cora Mobile. Privacy Policy and Terms and Conditions link to the legal pages. Licenses lists the open-source software Cora Mobile is built on.

docs.d: Install Cora Mobile, create your account, add your first tank and get your first readings on screen, step by step.
x: This page takes you through your first ten minutes with Cora Mobile, in the order the screens appear. When you're done, you'll have an account, a tank and a dashboard with readings on it.
On iPhone, get Cora Mobile from the App Store . On Android, Cora Mobile is coming soon to Google Play. The icon on your home screen says Cora . That's Cora Mobile.

The first time you open Cora Mobile, a few short screens introduce it. Tap Next to go through them, or Skip at the top right to go straight to sign-in. Two of them ask for something: Your devices live on your Wi-Fi warns you about a question your iPhone asks later. When you add your first piece of equipment, iPhone asks whether Cora may find devices on your local network. Allow it, or Cora can't find anything on your Wi-Fi. If you said no, Settings → Device access takes you to the switch. See Settings . The last screen is about alerts. Tap Allow notifications , then allow it in your phone's prompt, so alerts reach this phone. Maybe later skips it. More in Notifications .

You don't need an account to look around. On the sign-in screen, tap Explore a demo reef . It's a sample tank with realistic data, laid out like a real one. No equipment is involved, and nothing you do there is saved. When you're ready for your own tank, tap Make it yours .

On the sign-in screen, tap Sign Up (under Don't have an account? ). Enter your email address and a password, twice. The password needs at least 8 characters, an uppercase letter, a number and a symbol. The list under Your password needs: ticks off as you type. Tick I agree to: Terms and Conditions and Privacy Policy . Both are links, so you can read them first. Tap Create Account . You can also tap Continue with Apple or Continue with Google and skip the password. Tick the terms box there too. With Apple, choose Share My Email when Apple asks, so lab and ICP results can reach your Cora account. If you signed up with an email address, Cora now asks you to verify it. Open the email from Cora on the same phone and tap Verify my email . Then come back to Cora Mobile and tap I've Verified My Email . If nothing arrives within a minute, check your spam folder, or tap Resend verification email . More in Signing in and account recovery . One account for every screen Your account holds everything. Pair a Cora Max with it, or sign in on another phone, and you'll see the same tanks, devices, readings and records. Your phone dashboard layout follows the account to any phone you sign in on. Each Cora Max keeps its own layout. See What is shared and what is not .

In Cora, a tank is any body of water you want to track. Most people have one. If you run a frag system or a quarantine tank, each of those is a tank of its own. After you sign in, Let's meet your tank asks three things. Only the name is required, and you can change all of it later in your tank profile . What do you call it? is the name you use day to day, like "Display", "Frag" or "QT". What kind of tank is it? is SPS Reef , LPS Reef , Mixed Reef , Soft Coral Reef , FOWLR or Fish Only . The type sets your starting alert ranges. If you're unsure, pick Mixed Reef . How much water? is the real water volume, sump included. Dosing maths uses this number, so try to get it roughly right. If you only know the size of the tank, tap Don't know the volume? Enter dimensions and Cora works it out. Tap Create my tank . Is your tank still cycling? Tap Starting a new tank? on the dashboard before you log a test or link equipment. That card only shows on a tank with no readings at all, and it's how you turn on guided cycling. More in Guided journeys . Cora also judges readings against what's normal for a tank of that age. The wizard doesn't ask for it, so set Tank start date in your tank profile, under Tank Dimensions .

Next you'll see your tank's name with is live , for example "Display" is live . It offers four next steps. Pick any of them, or none. Set up my tank, guided walks you through the rest of the profile, one section at a time. See Guided setup . It ends with Add devices , which takes you to adding your equipment. Connect your gear pairs a Cora Max. For a Neptune Apex, Red Sea or any other brand, use Devices → Add Device instead (see below). Log your first test opens the first-test step described in The first-test card . Ask the assistant anything opens Cora Assistant with a first question ready to send. When you're done, tap Go to my dashboard , or I'll do this later .

On a new free account, Go to my dashboard first shows Your first 30 days are on us . Your 30-day Pro trial started when you created your account, and no card is needed. Tap Start exploring to carry on, or See plans to look at the paid plans. More in Plans and subscriptions .
Your first look at the dashboard

Two things happen the first time you open the dashboard. Cora asks Enable Personalized Reef Guidance? Tap Enable if you want Cora Assistant to use your tank's saved data in its answers. Not Now leaves it off. More in Asking Cora . A short tour points out the main parts of the screen. See The first-run tour .

Go to the Devices tab, tap Add Device and pick the brand. Cora works with gear you already own. Connecting your equipment lists what's supported and what each device needs. You can skip this and come back later. A tank works fine without devices. You just log readings by hand.

Some parameters only come from a test kit. Scroll down the dashboard and tap Log Parameters , in the row of buttons under the widgets. Pick the date and time, then enter test-kit results under Core, Elements and Nutrients. Cora saves each reading with its source and time. That's how it can tell you when a probe and a test kit disagree.

A tank with no readings and no linked equipment shows a card under the widgets, just above Log Parameters . It says Log your first water test . One reading is enough for Reef Buddy, alerts and insights to start working. Tap the card and choose one of these. Log test results now opens the Log Parameters form. Link a device (Apex or Red Sea) opens the pairing screen for a Cora Max. To link an Apex or a Red Sea unit, go to Devices → Add Device and pick the brand. If your tank profile already lists a device Cora can link, the card names it, for example Link your Neptune Apex . Later closes the sheet. Remind me to test every week adds a weekly maintenance task called Test water . Pick the Test day first. Tap the cross on the card to hide it. The card goes away by itself once the tank has a reading or a linked source. Cora Max shows Log your first test on a tank with no data, too. If a tank still has no readings three days after you create it, Cora sends one reminder push. If none of your tanks has any readings, Cora also sends a short email on day 3 and day 10 after you signed up, once each. Both follow your Maintenance Reminders switch in Settings → Notifications , and the email has a line saying how to stop it.

You're set up when the Dashboard shows your tank name at the top and a few widgets with numbers in them. A Reef Buddy card follows once the first briefing runs overnight. Next, have a look at Finding your way around . To add a second tank, see Managing your tanks .

docs.d: Share a picture of your tank's readings to social media or a friend with a tank snapshot card.
x: Cora can make a tank snapshot : one picture of your tank's current parameters, laid out for social media or a message to a friend.

Tap the share icon in the tank header on the dashboard. You can also tap the camera icon at the top of a Health Report. Tank Snapshot opens with a preview of the card, and nothing is sent until you choose where it goes. Choose which metrics appear, and the shape of the card.
The card shows your tank's name, age, type and livestock count, plus its health score when there's a recent one. Below that are the metrics you picked, each with its current value and recent trend.

Metrics on the card shows a chip for every parameter with readings in the last week. Tap chips to add or remove them. Select all turns them all on, and once they're all on the button becomes Reset , which goes back to the starting choice. Three or four look best. Any more and the card gets cramped. The card always keeps at least one. This phone remembers your choice for that tank next time.
There are two formats. Square (1:1) is for a post or a message. Story (9:16) is for a full-screen story.

Share opens your phone's usual share sheet, so you can send the card anywhere your phone can send a picture. Nothing leaves your account until you pick where it goes. A snapshot doesn't give access A snapshot is only a picture. It doesn't let anyone into your account, your history or your equipment. If someone's looking after the tank while you're away, use Going away . It makes a read-only page for them.

docs.d: Report a bug or send feedback from inside Cora Mobile, see what gets sent with it, turn on crash reports, or email support.
x: To report a problem or send feedback, use Settings → Help & Support → Report a Bug / Send Feedback . Reporting from inside Cora Mobile attaches details that are hard to remember later. Pick what kind of thing it is, say what happened, and add a screenshot if it helps.

Under What kind of thing is it? , pick one: Something is broken , Feature request , Wrong data , Confusing , Billing or Something else . That gets the report to the right person. Under What happened? , write it in your own words. Tap Send . You'll see Thanks, we got your report. Say what you expected and what you saw. "Alkalinity showed 2 d old on the dashboard when the Apex was reading fine" helps far more than "readings broken". You can send up to 10 reports a day.

Every report includes a short line of context. The form shows it to you before you send, under Sent with your report . the Cora Mobile version your platform and OS version the screen you were on The report also carries your phone's language and the tank you had selected. With that, we can usually reproduce what went wrong.

Attach a screenshot adds an image from your photos to the report. Remove screenshot takes it off again before you send. Take the screenshot first, then open the form. Cora support will see your screenshot Cora Mobile tells you this above the button. Check the image before you attach it. A dashboard screenshot shows your tank names and readings, plus anything else that was on screen. No screenshots in sitter mode When you're looking at someone else's tank through a shared link, you can't attach a screenshot. It would put their data in your support ticket, and they'd never know.

Send crash reports , in Help & Support under the report row, does the same job without you having to notice something broke and write it up. If Cora Mobile stops or a screen fails to load, it sends the technical details. No tank data, photos or account details are included. See Cora Mobile settings .

Settings → Help & Support → Contact Support opens an email to cora@coraiq.tech with your Cora Mobile version filled in. We usually reply within a day. If your phone has no mail app, write to that address from any email account.

Questions about your own tank are usually quicker to answer with Cora Assistant , since it can see your readings. If something doesn't work the way this guide says, check Troubleshooting first. For a billing question, see Plans and subscriptions .

docs.d: Fill in or change your tank's volume, type, livestock, lighting, dosing and equipment, which Cora uses to judge readings and work out doses.
x: The tank profile describes your system. Cora uses it to judge readings, work out doses and decide what's normal for your tank in particular. To open it, tap the pencil on the right of the tank header , or go to Settings , tap the tank and choose Edit tank . Tapping the tank name in the header is a quick rename. It doesn't open the profile.

There's a lot in a profile, so Guided setup takes you through it one section at a time. It opens from Set up my tank, guided right after you create a tank, from Settings → your tank → Guided setup , and from the profile prompt on the dashboard. The sections come in this order: Tank Name & Type , Tank Dimensions , Lighting , Dosing , Water Management , Livestock , Temperature Control , Flow & Filtration and Pest & Treatment . The top of the screen shows Step 2 of 10 and so on. Save & continue saves the section and moves on. Skip moves on without saving it. Finish later takes you back and keeps the answers you've saved so far. When you open guided setup again, it picks up where you stopped. If you leave a section with unsaved changes, Cora asks Leave this step? Tap Keep editing or Leave . If you haven't answered it yet, the last page is Cora Assistant & your data . Turn on Use my tank data for personalized advice if you want Cora Assistant's answers to use this profile, then tap Save , or tap Decide later . You can change it any time in Settings. See Asking Cora . At the end you'll see Nice work: your tank profile is set up . Add devices takes you to the Devices tab to add equipment for this tank, and Go to my dashboard takes you back. Each section changes what Cora can tell you The more you fill in, the more Cora can do. Dosing products make the dose calculator and consumption tracking work. Livestock and tank type change what your readings are judged against. Equipment tells Cora what you have. With a thin profile, you'll get more general answers. Each section shows a completion state. The score at the top reflects how much Cora knows about the tank.

The percentage at the top of the profile shows how much of it you've filled in. Tap it to jump to the next section that isn't finished. The fuller the profile, the more specific the advice. With an empty one, Cora falls back on defaults. The dashboard shows a prompt to finish the profile while it's under 80% complete. It opens guided setup until you've been through it once, and the profile after that. Close the prompt and it stays away until you next open Cora Mobile.

In the profile, the sections are listed like this. Tap one to open it. The info icon next to each one tells you what its fields are used for. Section Covers Feeding routine How you usually feed, so you only log the exceptions. See The journal Tank Name & Type What you call the tank and its type Tank Dimensions Physical size, total water volume and the tank's start date Dosing What you dose and how Water Management Water changes, top-off, salinity targets Livestock What the tank holds and how heavily it is stocked Temperature Control Heating and cooling equipment Lighting Fixtures and photoperiod Flow & Filtration Pumps, skimming, media and your controller's brand and model Parameter Sources Which source each parameter is read from Pest & Treatment Pests you've dealt with, their status and what you tried When you add a heater, pump, light or skimmer under Temperature Control , Flow & Filtration or Lighting , Cora suggests brands and models as you type. If yours isn't on the list, type it in anyway. Cora keeps whatever you enter. Parameter Sources isn't shown while you're adding a new tank. It covers the same choice as Parameter Mapping in the tank's settings, which gives you full control over every probe. See Parameter Mapping . Parameter Sources and Pest & Treatment, then Remove Tank at the bottom. Devices live on the Devices tab Your Apex, Red Sea units and every other device are added, assigned and removed from the Devices tab, not from the profile. See Adding, editing and removing devices . The tank's page in Settings shows a read-only Devices on this tank list if you just want to check what's assigned.

Each tank has its own display units. Tap the ruler icon in the tank header, or go to Settings , tap the tank and choose Units . You can set how this tank shows salinity, temperature, alkalinity, volume, phosphate and nitrate. Volume can be litres, US gallons or UK gallons. The units apply to this tank on every phone and Cora Max that opens it. Your readings aren't changed, only how they're shown. Gauges, tiles, history, reports and what Cora Assistant says all follow the choice. On Cora Max, open the tank menu and tap Units .

Enter the real water volume, sump included. Don't use the display volume printed on the tank. Doses scale directly with volume If the volume is 20% too high, dose suggestions are 20% too high as well. If you're not sure, measure it. Don't guess.

Set Tank start date under Tank Dimensions . Cora judges readings against what's normal for a tank that age, so a three-month-old system and a five-year-old one are judged differently. If the tank is still cycling, tap the Starting a new tank? card on the dashboard to start guided cycling. Do it before you log the first test or link equipment, because the card only shows on a tank with no readings at all. More in Guided journeys .
Update the profile when your system changes, for example new equipment, different stocking or a new dosing routine. Cora works from the profile, so if it's out of date, the advice will be too.
Go to Settings and tap Add tank . It opens this same profile, empty, with Save Tank at the bottom. The full steps, including equipment and Cora Max, are in Managing your tanks .
Remove Tank is at the bottom of the profile. It hides the tank and keeps its data, and you can bring it back later. Before you use it, read Removing a tank , because some things keep running.

docs.d: Add another tank, switch between tanks, change their order and which tanks get Reef Buddy, and remove or restore a tank.
x: This page covers having more than one tank: adding one, moving between them, putting them in order, and removing one you no longer keep. Each tank has its own dashboard, devices, alerts and records. You can have as many tanks as you like on any plan. Your plan only decides how many of them get Reef Buddy (see The order decides which tanks get Reef Buddy ).

Go to Settings and tap Add tank , under your list of tanks. Add Tank opens the full tank profile. Give the tank a name under Tank Name & Type , and fill in whatever else you know, like the type and the water volume under Tank Dimensions . You can finish the rest later. See Your tank profile . Tap Save Tank . Cora offers the first-test step. Log a test, set a weekly reminder, or tap Later . See The first-test card . Then give the tank its equipment: To add new equipment for it, go to Devices → Add Device , pick the brand and choose this tank. See Connecting your equipment . To move equipment you already have, open the device on the Devices tab and change its tank. See Adding, editing and removing devices . To show the tank on Cora Max, go to Devices , open your Cora Max and tap Add Tank under Assigned Tanks . A Cora Max shows up to 4 tanks. Is the new tank still cycling? Tap Starting a new tank? on its dashboard before you log a test or link equipment. The card only shows on a tank with no readings at all. More in Guided journeys .

Dashboard : swipe left or right. The dots at the top show which tank you're on. Settings : every tank has its own row. Tap one to open that tank's settings, like Alert thresholds , Parameter Mapping and Units . Assistant and Intelligence : pick the tank at the top of the screen. See Asking Cora . A notification about one tank opens that tank's dashboard. On Cora Max, the Reef Room shows every tank side by side. See The Reef Room .

Go to Settings and tap Reorder tanks , then drag the tanks into the order you want. You can also drag a tank by its handle in the list on the Settings screen. Reorder tanks only works once you have two tanks or more. The order is the order you swipe through on the dashboard.
The order decides which tanks get Reef Buddy

Your plan covers a set number of tanks for Reef Buddy's daily briefing. Cora gives it to the first ones in your Reorder tanks order. On Plus, and during the 30-day trial, that's your first tank only. Pro covers 5 tanks and Max covers 20. More in Plans and subscriptions . If a tank gets no briefing, move it to the top of the list. Removed tanks don't count.

Open the tank profile: tap the pencil in the tank header, or go to Settings , tap the tank and choose Edit tank . Scroll to the bottom and tap Remove Tank . Cora asks Remove this tank? Tap Remove . Removing only hides the tank. It leaves your dashboard and your Settings list, and its readings, journal and records are kept. You can bring it back at any time. These stop for a removed tank: Reef Buddy's briefing, maintenance reminders, and its place in your plan's Reef Buddy count. A removed tank's equipment keeps running Removing a tank doesn't unlink anything. Its devices stay assigned to it and keep reporting, a Cora Max assigned to it keeps showing it, and its equipment can still send you alerts. Before you remove a tank, move or remove its devices on the Devices tab. Then open your Cora Max under Devices and tap the Remove tank icon next to that tank under Assigned Tanks . When you remove a tank, a de-identified copy of its parameter history goes to reef research, with no link to you. If you don't want that, turn off Contribute anonymized tank data first. See Your data .

Go to Settings and tap Removed tanks . The row only shows when you have a removed tank. Tap Restore next to the tank. Its readings, journal and devices come back exactly as they were. Cora Mobile has no way to delete a single tank for good. The only way to delete a tank's data is to delete your account. See Your data .

docs.t: Finding your way around Cora Mobile
docs.d: A tour of Cora Mobile's five tabs, Dashboard, Devices, Assistant, Intelligence and Settings, plus the tank header, the bell and the Journal button.
x: Cora Mobile has five tabs along the bottom: Dashboard , Devices , Assistant , Intelligence and Settings . Almost everything you do happens in one of them. Dashboard, Devices, Assistant, Intelligence, Settings.

This is the main screen of Cora Mobile. It shows live readings for one tank. If you have more than one tank, swipe left or right to move between them. The dots at the top show which one you're on. See Managing your tanks . The tank header has the tank name, which you tap to rename the tank, and a row of icons: Feed opens Feed mode , where you start one of your Neptune Apex feed cycles. It only shows on a tank with an Apex. See The tank header . The newspaper icon opens the latest Reef Buddy briefing. The share icon makes a snapshot of the tank to send. See Sharing your tank . The ruler opens Units , which sets how this tank shows its readings. The pencil opens the tank profile . Just under the widgets is Edit dashboard , for changing the dashboard itself. Below it, a row of buttons has Log Parameters , Parameter History and Feeding , then shortcuts to the tank's journal, alerts, maintenance and livestock. You'll find more in Reading your dashboard .

Here's everything you've connected, grouped by brand. You can collapse each group, so even a reef room full of equipment is easy to read. This is where you add new equipment, rename it, assign it to a tank or remove it. More in Adding, editing and removing devices .

Ask Cora about your tank in plain language, by typing or by voice. It can see your live readings, your history and your ICP results. So if you ask "why is my alkalinity falling?", it answers about your tank. More in Asking Cora .

This is where your lab results and health reports live. Upload an ICP test and Cora reads it, tracks every element over time and tells you what's changed since last time. A Health Report is a full check of the whole system, and you run one whenever you want it. More in ICP and health reports .

Here you manage your account, your tanks, dosing products, Cora Assistant, notifications, automations and your plan. Tap a tank in the list to open everything that belongs to it, like its alert thresholds, Parameter Mapping and Units . More in Cora Mobile settings .

The first time you open the dashboard, Cora points out the parts of the screen one by one: the widgets, Edit dashboard , long-pressing a widget to tune its alert range, Log Parameters , the shortcuts to your records, and the Devices , Assistant and Intelligence tabs. It only does this once. To see it again, go to Settings → About → Replay tips . The tour restarts and takes you to the dashboard to begin. It's handy after an update, or when you hand your phone to someone else.

The bell at the top right holds your notification history, with every alert Cora has raised, newest first. The number on it is how many you haven't read yet. The Journal button floats at the bottom right of the Dashboard. Tap it and say what you just did, like a water change, a new coral or a dose you changed. Tap the stop button when you're done, and Cora writes it into the journal. See The journal .

docs.t: Going away: a plan for your tank sitter
docs.d: Turn on vacation mode, build a checklist for your tank sitter, and share it as a read-only page with live readings that they open without an account.
x: Vacation mode helps someone else look after your tank while you're away. You pick the dates and the jobs, and Cora makes a web page you send to your sitter. Go to Settings → your tank → Vacation mode . If you have more than one tank, pick the tank at the top. Each tank has its own plan. The tank, a reminder that alerts still come to you, the trip dates, then the sitter checklist.

Under When are you away? , tap Pick your travel dates . Build the Sitter checklist . Maintenance tasks that come due while you're gone are offered for you, each with how often it's needed. Tap a suggestion to add it, such as Feed the tank , Check the ATO reservoir , Empty the skimmer cup or Call me if anything looks wrong . To add your own job, type it under Add your own task… and tap Add task . Under Notes & contact , write Notes for the sitter and, under If anything looks wrong , how to reach you. Tap Start vacation mode . Each job shows how often to do it, for example Daily , Every 3 days , Once or Always (a standing instruction). Cora works this out from the maintenance task or the suggestion. A job you type yourself has no tag, so put the timing in its wording. Write the checklist for someone who doesn't know reef tanks. Spell out amounts and how to do things. "Feed one cube of frozen food, thawed, once a day" is much clearer than "feed as usual". Say what to leave alone Add a job for any equipment the sitter shouldn't touch, for example "Don't change anything on the controller". Put it in the notes too.

Tap Create sitter link . Cora makes a read-only web page with the checklist, your notes and live tank readings. Your sitter doesn't need Cora Mobile or an account. Tap Share to send it, or Copy the link. On that page the sitter can tick jobs off as they do them. You see each one under Sitter activity , with the time. They can't change anything else, control equipment or see the rest of your account. The link works until your end date plus 2 days. New link makes a fresh link and the old one stops working, which is handy if you sent it to the wrong person.

Everything else keeps working as usual, including readings, alerts, Reef Buddy, dosing and automations. Vacation mode doesn't pause anything. While it's on, the top of Settings says Vacation mode is on . Tap it to review the plan or end it. Alerts still come to you The sitter's page shows active alerts, but the sitter is never notified. Parameter alerts keep going to your phone. Keep your phone reachable, and put your number in the plan. Check your notification settings before you leave. To change the plan while you're away, tap Edit , then Save changes .
Tap End vacation mode and confirm with End it . The sitter link stops working right away. Your checklist stays saved for next time.

docs.d: Every widget type on the Cora Mobile dashboard, from value, gauge, graph, status and outlet to the device tiles, and when to use each one.
x: A widget is one tile on your dashboard, and it shows one thing. This page goes through each type and what you can set on it. You add and arrange widgets in the dashboard editor . Tap a widget there to open its settings: Type and Parameter for a metric, the outlet or device for the others, then Width and Height , and Time range for a graph. The lower half of a widget's settings: the parameter, width, height and time range, then Remove and Done.

Type Shows Value The current reading, its unit, age and source Gauge An arc with your range banded onto it and a knob at the value Graph A trend over a time range you choose Status The reading as plain text with a coloured dot Outlet A three-way control: Auto, Off, On ReefBeat One Red Sea unit, with its own summary Apex module One fitted Apex module, such as a Trident or DŌS Jecod One Jecod pump, with its mode and intensity Everything after Outlet is a device tile. Each one belongs to a piece of equipment instead of a parameter, and shows whatever that unit reports. Cora Max also has a Scene tile, which you add on Cora Max. See Editing the Cora Max dashboard .

Width and Height can each be 1× or 2× , so a widget is one or two cells wide and one or two cells tall. A graph is never one cell wide. On a three-column dashboard, a two-wide gauge takes up two thirds of the row. That's usually a good shape for your most important parameter.

Value, Gauge, Graph and Status widgets all show a measured parameter, and they always show three things. Outlet and device tiles show their own state, since there's no single reading behind them. The value , in large type The age ( now , 1h , 2d ), which is how long ago the source last confirmed the value. For a probe, that's when its device last checked in, so a steady reading stays fresh. For a test-kit or ICP result, it's when you took the test. More in Reading your dashboard . The source , a small badge that says where the number came from A parameter widget has no range or source setting of its own. The range comes from the tank's alert thresholds (long-press the widget on the dashboard), and the source from Parameter Mapping . Tap the widget on the dashboard to see its full history, every source that reports it and your alert band.

This is the plain number. It shows the current reading, its unit, how old it is and where it came from. Use it for parameters you check by the number more than by the trend, like calcium, magnesium or nitrate.

A gauge is an arc with your alert range marked on it, and a knob at the current value. The knob's colour tells you where you are: inside the range, drifting or out. Use it for the parameters you actively manage, like alkalinity, pH, salinity or temperature. Make gauges at least two columns wide At one column the arc is too small to read quickly. If you're short on space, use a Value widget.

A graph is a sparkline over a time range you choose: 1h, 6h, 24h, 7d, 30d or 1y. It marks the high and low and labels the current value. For a parameter you test (with a Trident or a test kit), the line joins up your real tests. If there's only one test in the window, the line comes in from the test before it, and there's no high or low. If there's no test in the window, or nothing earlier to join a single test to, the tile shows Collecting… in place of a line. Use it for anything that moves, like pH through the day, temperature in a heatwave or alkalinity between doses. A graph is always at least two cells wide . A sparkline squeezed into one cell tells you nothing, so the editor won't let you make one. Pick the range that fits the parameter pH swings on a daily cycle, so 24 hours shows you the pattern. Alkalinity moves over days, so 7 or 30 days tells you much more.
This shows the reading as plain text, with a coloured dot for in range, drifting or out. Use it for a parameter that has no useful gauge range.

This is a three-way switch for an Apex outlet: Auto , Off and On . You pick which outlet it controls. Auto gives the outlet back to whatever normally runs it. That might be a schedule, a rule or the controller it belongs to. Off and On are manual overrides. They stay until you change them back. Manual overrides don't wear off Off means off until you set it back to Auto. If you switch a return pump off to work in the tank, put it back to Auto when you're done. Cora won't do it for you.

This is one tile for a whole piece of equipment. It shows the unit's own summary instead of a single parameter, for example an ATO's status and reservoir, a doser's heads or how many days a mat roller has left. You pick which device it shows. Which devices can have a tile depends on what you've connected. See Connecting your equipment .

A tile for a doser (an Apex DŌS or a ReefDose) shows one row per head. A head name is never shrunk below a readable size. On a tall tile the row takes two lines, with the name on the first and what's left on the second, for example 40d and 2.8 L . On a short tile the detail line is dropped and the name stays readable. Set what comes first with Show remaining as : Days or Milliliters (mL) . A ReefDose head with no name of its own is shown as the device name followed by "head" and its number. A Jecod doser tile is read only and shows the daily plan, because Jecod doesn't report how much is left in the bottle.

docs.d: Fix a stale reading, a device that went offline, a command that didn't go through, a Cora Max that won't pair, or an alert that won't clear.
x: Find the family your problem belongs to, then the message or symptom you see. Headings in quotes are the exact words Cora shows you. Readings and widgets A device stopped reporting or can't be reached A command didn't go through Cora Max Alerts, notifications and the daily briefing Cora Assistant and voice Lab results and health reports Language, units and signing in

Go through these in order. Look at the age on nearby widgets. If they're all old too, it's the connection, not the parameter. Open the Devices tab. If a device can't be reached, its row has a red dot or says so. Check which tank the device is on. A device reporting to the wrong tank looks exactly like one that isn't reporting. Open the device and check its tank. Check that something measures it. Nothing reports phosphate unless you have equipment that measures it or you log it by hand.

Grey means Cora isn't grading that reading. There are three usual reasons. The alert for it is turned off. Turn it back on in the Rules tab of the Alert Center. It has no range to judge it by. Long-press the widget and set a range. The reading is too old. Check the age on the widget, then log a new reading or check the device. What each colour means is in Reading your dashboard .

The age on the widget is right. Nothing new has come in. Hand-logged parameters go stale when nobody has logged a reading. Log one. Equipment readings go stale when the device stops reporting. Check its row in Devices . Some equipment only reports now and then. A titrator that measures hourly usually shows 1h . That's normal.

Nothing is broken. When your probe and your test kit disagree, that tells you something real about your system. Usually the probe needs calibrating. Sometimes the test kit is old. Calibrate the probe, retest with fresh reagent, and compare the two under the same conditions. If one reading was plainly wrong, you can exclude it. See Looking into a parameter . An ICP result gives you a third number to compare, but it won't settle the question by itself. Labs differ from each other, and how a sample is handled and shipped changes the result.
A widget shows the wrong units

That's the tank's display units. Your data is fine, and values are stored the same way however they're shown. Open Settings , open that tank and choose Units . Change them there. Every phone and Cora Max showing that tank updates to match.
A gauge or threshold looks different after changing units
That's expected. Gauges, tiles and history redraw in the unit you picked. The values underneath haven't changed.
My dashboard looks wrong after editing

Your readings, history and journal are stored apart from the layout, so you haven't lost anything. On your phone , the editor has no undo or saved designs. Open Edit dashboard and put the widgets back. More in Editing your dashboard . On Cora Max , load a saved design: open Dashboard layout , tap My dashboards and pick one. If you haven't saved one, rebuild the layout and tap Save this design , so next time it takes one tap. More in Editing the Cora Max dashboard .
Settings → Activity lists every outlet switch, feed and dose, and what asked for it: Cora Mobile, a Cora Max, voice, the Assistant, an automation or your account. More in Activity and timeline .
A device stopped reporting or can't be reached

Cora sends this when a device goes quiet. It doesn't mean the device is broken, only that Cora hasn't heard from it for a while. How long Cora waits for each brand is in Alerts and thresholds . Check the device's power, and its Wi-Fi or Bluetooth range. Check that the Cora Max reading it is switched on and online. Without a Cora Max, your phone reads a Neptune Apex, Red Sea or Jecod device only while Cora Mobile is open on the same Wi-Fi. Wait for the next reading. You get a second notification once it's reporting again.
"Device is offline. Showing last known state."

The device stopped reporting, and Cora is showing the last values it had. They aren't current. Check the device's own network connection. Don't treat the values as live until the row stops saying offline.

It's usually the network. Is the equipment powered on and working in its own app? Is it on the same network you added it on? Has anything changed with your router (new hardware, new network name, guest network isolation)? Equipment on your local network has to be reachable on that network. Equipment that connects through a manufacturer account doesn't, but that account still has to be valid. If the device's address changed, open it on the Devices tab and tap Edit connection under Connection .
A device says the sign-in was refused
The manufacturer rejected the saved sign-in. Almost always, that's because you changed your password with them. Open the device's row and sign in again.

Nothing on this tank is reading your Red Sea equipment right now, so the readings on screen aren't being refreshed. Open Settings , open the tank, then Primary Cora Max . Check that a Cora Max is set, or that Any active (automatic) is chosen. If you have no Cora Max, open the tank in Cora Mobile while your phone is on the same Wi-Fi as the Red Sea gear. Check that the Red Sea equipment is powered on and online in its own app.
Some ReefBeat settings are greyed out or missing

That's normal. A Red Sea device's own settings only open when your phone is on the same network as the device. Away from that network you only see readings. Join the tank's Wi-Fi to change those settings. Readings and history keep working when you're away.
Every command ends as Confirmed , Unconfirmed , Refused or No change . What each one means is in Controlling your equipment .
"Could not reach this pump: nothing was sent"

A command to your Jecod or Jebao pump never left Cora. On your phone the message reads "Could not reach this pump. It needs to be on the same Wi-Fi as your phone." Usually the pump is off or not on its network. Check the pump is powered on. Check it's on the same network you added it on, and that your phone or Cora Max is on that network too. Tap Retry .
"Could not reach this pump over Bluetooth. Stand near it and try again."
Your phone is out of range of a Bluetooth-only Jecod pump. Move closer to the pump and tap Retry .
"Could not reach the Apex: nothing changed" / "nothing was dosed"

A Neptune Apex, Trident or DŌS head didn't respond to a command or a dose request. Open the Apex's own app and check it's online. Check the network connection on the phone or Cora Max you're using. Changing a DŌS head from your phone needs the phone on the same network as the Apex. Tap Retry .
"… could not be sent: this Cora Max has no Apex details"

Cora Max shows this when it has no way to reach your Apex and no other device on the tank can send the command for it. The message says to add the Apex details in Settings, but they're now set on your phone. On your phone, open Devices , then your Apex, and check its address and sign-in under Connection . Fix them with Edit connection . Or make a working Cora Max the Primary Cora Max for this tank: Settings , open the tank, then Primary Cora Max .
Feed doesn't start from the phone

On your phone, Feed only shows on a tank with a Neptune Apex, and it starts one of the feed cycles programmed on the Apex. "No Cora on this tank can reach the Apex, and you're not on its network." Join the Apex's Wi-Fi, or pair a Cora Max to the tank. "The Apex didn't answer, but it may already be feeding." Check the controller before you try again.
A dose stopped partway through and a "restore" alert appeared

The DŌS head lost contact during the dose. Cora tells you so it doesn't have to assume the full dose went in. Open the alert and check how much was dosed before it stopped. Use that amount to decide whether to resume or adjust the dose.

On your phone, its row on the Devices tab has a red dot. While it's offline, equipment it reads stops updating, you may get "stopped reporting" alerts for that equipment, and commands sent from away can come back as "Nothing was sent" . Check that Cora Max has power and the screen is on. On Cora Max, check Settings → Cora Max Settings → Wi-Fi , and that your router is working. If another Cora Max is on the tank, set Primary Cora Max to Any active (automatic) so it can take over. See More than one Cora device . If it won't start up properly, see Updates and recovery . Get told next time In Cora Mobile, open Settings → Automations and make a rule with the trigger When a device goes offline , pick your Cora Max, and add the action Notify Me . More in Automations and scenes .

Cora Mobile finds a new Cora Max over Bluetooth, then gives it your Wi-Fi. Before you start, have at least one tank in Cora Mobile, Bluetooth on, and your phone near the screen. If pairing stops partway, Cora Mobile tells you why, with Cancel and Retry underneath. "Bluetooth is off. Turn it on, then tap Scan again." Turn Bluetooth on and scan again. "Bluetooth permission is off for Cora. Enable it in Settings, then tap Scan again." Allow Bluetooth for Cora in your phone's settings. Settings → Device access in Cora Mobile takes you there. "No nearby Cora setup devices were found over Bluetooth." Stand next to Cora Max, check that it shows its setup screen, and scan again. No Tanks Found : create a tank in Cora Mobile first, then pair. "Your phone could not reach the Cora Max on your Wi-Fi." Put your phone and Cora Max on the same Wi-Fi network. On iPhone, also check that Cora has Local Network access ( Settings → Device access ). Then tap Retry . "The Cora Max did not accept this pairing session." Retrying won't help. Close the screen and start again from Devices → Add Device → Cora . For any other message, tap Retry . The whole setup is in Setting up Cora Max .

Look at the status tag in the top bar. Online and Cloud are both fine. If you have more than one Cora Max, the one that isn't collecting the data shows Cloud , and its readings are just as current. Stale or Offline means Cora Max has lost its source and is showing the last data it got. Check Wi-Fi under Settings → Cora Max Settings → Wi-Fi . Check that your network itself is working. If the tag says Online or Cloud and the data is still old, the problem is before Cora Max. Check the same tank on your phone.

Your Apex turned down the sign-in Cora has saved, usually because the Apex password was changed. On your phone, open Devices , then your Apex, and tap Edit connection under Connection to enter the new one.

Cora Cloud is refusing to save some of this screen's data. Nothing is wrong with your tank or with Cora Max, and nothing needs changing on the screen. The fix is a Cora Cloud update. Open Settings → Cora Max Settings and scroll to STATUS . The Cloud save line says which data is being refused, for example a device's readings or outlets. Contact support and tell us what that line says. Your readings keep showing on Cora Max in the meantime. They just aren't saved to your account until the fix is in.
A second Cora Max shows "Main Cora offline"

The Primary Cora Max for this tank has gone offline. This screen is showing the last data it received, so it isn't live. Check the primary Cora Max's power and Wi-Fi. Wait for it to reconnect, or change the Primary Cora Max to a device that's online.
Cora Max won't reconnect right away after a Wi-Fi outage

After it loses its connection, Cora Max waits a bit longer before each retry so it doesn't flood your network. The wait grows to about a minute. Give it about a minute after your network comes back. If it still hasn't reconnected, check Settings → Cora Max Settings → Wi-Fi .
Renaming a Cora Max on the phone doesn't change what it shows

The name you set on your phone is the account's label for that device. The name Cora Max shows on its own pairing screen can be a different one. Check which name you're looking at: the one in your phone's device list, or the one on Cora Max's pairing screen. To change the account label, rename it from your phone's device list.
I can't find where to turn off the wake word

Wake-word controls are with the sound settings, not the Cora Assistant settings. On Cora Max, go to Settings → Cora Max Settings , and find Wake word under SOUND & VOICE . Turn it off. You can still tap the Cora Assistant icon to start talking. More in Talking to Cora .
Child lock won't let anyone into Settings

That's what child lock does. After a set time with no touch, it stops anyone switching equipment from this screen, by touch or by voice. Readings keep updating, and you can still ask Cora questions. To unlock: Press Volume Up or Volume Down three times within two seconds, or Hold five fingers in the top-right corner of the screen for ten seconds. More in Cora Max settings .
A scene made on the phone isn't editable on Cora Max

Only newer Cora Max versions can edit scenes on the screen. Older versions still run scenes you made on your phone, but can't edit them. Update Cora Max ( Updates and recovery ), or Keep editing that scene on your phone. It runs on Cora Max either way.
Alerts, notifications and the daily briefing

An alert clears when the reading is back in range. If it won't clear, there are three likely reasons. The reading really is out of range. Look at the widget's history. The range doesn't suit your tank. See Alerts and thresholds . The source is off. A probe that needs calibrating reports a number that really is out of range. Fix the probe and leave the range alone.
An alert won't stop notifying after I acknowledged it

Snooze and Dismiss on Cora Max only quiet that one Cora Max. Your phone keeps getting notifications for as long as the reading is out of range. To hear about it less often, open the alert rule in Cora Mobile and set a longer Cooldown between alerts (up to 1 week). If the range doesn't suit your tank, change the range itself.

In Settings → Notifications , check that the category is allowed to send notifications. Check your phone's own notification permission for Cora. The daily briefing stays quiet on days when nothing changed. If it has stopped altogether, see the next entry. More in Notifications .

Your trial ended. Reef Buddy is part of the paid plans. After the 30-day trial, a free account stops getting the daily briefing. See Plans and subscriptions . The tank isn't covered by your plan. Each plan covers a set number of tanks, counted in the order of Settings → Reorder tanks . Move a tank up to include it. Nothing changed today. The briefing stays quiet on a quiet day. More in Reef Buddy .
Alerts keep coming from a tank I removed

Removing a tank only hides it. Its devices stay linked to it, and a Cora Max can still be reading it, so its equipment can keep reporting and alerting. Restore it from Settings → Removed tanks so you can see it again. Remove or move its devices on the Devices tab. Take it off your Cora Max: on your phone, open Devices , then your Cora Max, and under Tanks tap Remove tank next to it. Then remove the tank again. More in Managing your tanks .
Cora Assistant answers about the wrong tank
You didn't pick a tank before asking, or the wrong one is selected. Pick the tank you mean, then ask again. More in Asking Cora .
Cora Assistant refuses to answer, or shows a consent screen again
Allow Cora Assistant to use saved tank data is turned off, so it has nothing to answer from. Tap Agree & Continue on the consent screen, or turn the switch on in Settings → Cora Assistant .
Cora Max says "Voice needs your OK"

Voice on Cora Max uses the same data-sharing choice as Cora Assistant on your phone. In Cora Mobile, open Settings → Cora Assistant and turn on Allow Cora Assistant to use saved tank data , then try again. More in Talking to Cora .
A lab or emailed ICP result never showed up

A result only attaches once it has a tank, sometimes Cora also needs to recognise the sender, and Cora needs your OK to read it. If you see "Cora Assistant needs your OK to read it." , open Settings → Cora Assistant and turn on Allow Cora Assistant to use saved tank data . The result comes through once you agree. Check the hint Cora shows the first time you send it a result. When Cora asks, confirm which tank the result belongs to. If you've sent a result before, send this one from the same email address. More in ICP and health reports .
Cora reads the PDF report your lab sends. Photos and screenshots can't be read. Download the PDF from your lab first, then tap Upload ICP again.
The screen goes black after a health report or ICP upload

This could happen in Cora Mobile 1.2 and earlier, and Cora Mobile 1.3 fixes it: update Cora Mobile from the App Store or Google Play. If you see it before you update, close Cora Mobile and open it again. The report was saved, and you'll find it under Intelligence .
Everything is suddenly in the wrong language

Someone changed the account language on one of your devices. It's one setting for the whole account. Open Settings → Language in Cora Mobile or on Cora Max. Set it back. The change applies everywhere.
An old alert or report is in a different language after switching
That's expected. Cora doesn't retranslate anything it already wrote. New alerts, reports and briefings use the new language.
"Could not reach Cora. Check your Wi-Fi or mobile data, then try again."

Your phone can't reach Cora Cloud to sign in. This is about your phone's connection, not your tank equipment. Check that your phone has working Wi-Fi or mobile data. Try a different network if you have one. Tap Retry . Other sign-in problems are in Signing in and account recovery .
Email cora@coraiq.tech , or report it from Cora Mobile as described in Reporting a problem . Tell us which tank, which device, which screen, and what you expected to see.
